title: Trusting the Machine: How Consumer Trust in Artificial Intelligence Shapes Future Adoption Intentions
affiliations: University of Oklahoma, Islamic Azad University, Islamic Azad University and Payame Noor University

detail.title: Trusting the Machine: How Consumer Trust in Artificial Intelligence Shapes Future Adoption Intentions
detail.abstract: Although the use of artificial intelligence (AI) by consumers is growing, one of the most important factors influencing whether or not they incorporate AI into their daily lives is trust. This study examines the relationship between trust and the intentions to adopt AI-driven products in the future as well as their current use. Based on the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and related frameworks, we argue that perceived knowledge about AI helps to explain how trust translates into behavioral intentions and that trust functions as a fundamental mechanism influencing openness toward AI technologies. We also investigate whether this relationship is moderated by education and age. Regression results from a survey of 205 consumers provide strong support for H1: future adoption of AI is significantly predicted by trust in AI. H2 is supported by mediation analyses, which show that the trust-adoption relationship is partially mediated by perceived knowledge. Although older and less educated people descriptively reported lower trust and adoption intentions, H3, which proposed moderation by age and education, was not statistically supported. Separate trust-based segments with various behavioral patterns were also identified by cluster analysis. By highlighting trust and user knowledge as key factors in AI adoption contexts, these findings go beyond TAM/UTAAUT. They also recommend that companies looking to increase AI acceptance should give top priority to improving transparency, lowering uncertainty, and informing customers about AI capabilities.

title: Stock Predictor: Predicting Stock Movements Based on Current Global News Using Artificial Intelligence

detail.title: Stock Predictor: Predicting Stock Movements Based on Current Global News Using Artificial Intelligence
detail.abstract: The prediction of stock price dynamics, a central challenge in financial econometrics, is increasingly influenced by the continuous flow of information from global news that shapes investor sentiment. This research quantifies the incremental predictive power of news by proposing a multimodal deep learning framework that systematically fuses sentiment signals, derived from real-time global news, with historical market data to forecast short-term stock movements. The proposed architecture leverages a domainspecific language model, FinBERT, for robust textual feature extraction, which is then integrated with advanced sequence models, including LSTMs and transformers, to model the temporal interplay between market and sentiment dynamics. Through rigorous empirical evaluation on a diverse set of stock indices and individual equities from 2021-2024, our findings demonstrate that these sentiment-augmented models achieve a significant performance gain over traditional time-series baselines. Specifically, our topperforming transformer-based fusion model registers a directional accuracy of 63.2%, a notable improvement over the 56.5% accuracy of a baseline LSTM relying solely on price data. The analysis confirms that news sentiment is a particularly potent predictive feature during periods of high market volatility. This work concludes with a critical discussion on inherent limitations, such as signal noise and causality challenges, while outlining future research directions for enhancing model explainability and real-world deployment readiness.

detail.title: Government Support as a Moderator of Sustainable Competitive Advantage, Entrepreneurial Marketing, and Business Sustainability Performance
detail.abstract: Micro and small enterprises (MSEs) in developing countries face persistent challenges in maintaining competitiveness and business sustainability, particularly amid global market uncertainty and resource constraints. This study examines the roles of Entrepreneurial Marketing (EM) and Social Media Promotion (SMP) in strengthening Sustainable Competitive Advantage (SCA) and their subsequent effects on Sustainable Business Performance (SBP), with Government Support (GS) as a moderating factor. Using a quantitative explanatory design, data were collected from 150 food and beverage MSEs in Tasikmalaya, Indonesia, through purposive sampling and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS version 4.1.1.4. The findings indicate that EM and SMP significantly and positively influence SCA, and that SCA itself contributes positively to SBP, underscoring the strategic importance of entrepreneurial-based marketing and digital promotion in enhancing long-term competitiveness and resilience. However, GS did not significantly moderate the relationships between EM and SCA or between SCA and SBP, suggesting that current policy interventions are not fully aligned with the strategic needs of MSEs in the digital era. These results highlight that internal strategies such as innovation, customer orientation, and digital adoption are more critical drivers of sustainable performance than external support mechanisms alone. The study contributes to the literature by clarifying the mechanisms linking entrepreneurial marketing, digital promotion, and business sustainability in a non-metropolitan context and by providing practical implications for policymakers to redesign support programs that better address sectoral needs, digital readiness, and the long-term competitiveness of MSEs.

title: The Winner's Curse in Data-Driven Decision Making: Evidence and Solutions
affiliations: Washington University in St. Louis - John M. Olin Business School, Olin School - Washington University in St. Louis and Washington University in St. Louis - John M. Olin Business School

detail.title: The Winner's Curse in Data-Driven Decision Making: Evidence and Solutions
detail.abstract: Data-driven decision making involves estimating the value of each potential option and selecting the one with the highest estimated efficacy. This approach underpins a wide array of modern marketing, operations, and AI applications, including A/B testing, advertising and bidding, pricing, and personalized targeting. However, several papers have shown that the estimated effectiveness of the chosen options will be systematically overoptimistic (Smith and Winkler 2006, Efron 2011, Andrews et al. 2024), even when the estimated outcomes are themselves unbiased and efficient. Using simulations calibrated to realistic parameter values from recent marketing studies, we first demonstrate that the magnitude of the winner's curse is often high in relevant marketing contexts, and that the severity of the winner's curse depends on the true performance difference between options relative to the level of noise in the data, the number of alternatives under consideration, and the number of observations per tested condition. We further show that using machine learning methods to evaluate what treatment to give to individual consumers can lead to extremely high levels of winner's curse, especially if the machine learning functional form is very flexible. We propose a correction method based on a non-continuous bootstrap, and benchmark our method against several existing proposed solutions across many common marketing scenarios. We demonstrate that our bootstrap approach generally performs well, and usually outperforms the solutions that have been previously proposed in the literature.

title: The S-O-R Model and Impulsive Buying Behavior in Live Commerce

detail.title: The S-O-R Model and Impulsive Buying Behavior in Live Commerce
detail.abstract: This study examines how the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S–O–R) model explains consumer behavior dynamics in the context of live shopping on social commerce platforms. The research aims to understand how digital stimuli influence emotional and behavioral responses during interactive online shopping sessions. Using a qualitative approach, data were collected through in-depth interviews with five participants, consisting of three buyers and two hosts, to explore their experiences and strategies in live shopping environments. The findings reveal that stimuli such as interactivity, time-limited promotions, and social cues evoke emotional engagement and perceived value among consumers. These internal reactions lead to impulsive purchasing tendencies and repeated participation in live shopping activities. The study concludes that live shopping represents not only a digital purchasing process but also a socially driven and emotionally engaging experience. The results contribute to advancing interactive marketing strategies and provide deeper insights into consumer behavior within the evolving landscape of digital commerce.

title: Green Leadership: A Systematic Literature Review and Future Research Agenda
affiliations: , Bakrie University and Bakrie University

detail.title: Green Leadership: A Systematic Literature Review and Future Research Agenda
detail.abstract: Green leadership has emerged as a critical factor in promoting organizational sustainability, particularly in response to global environmental challenges. This study conducts a systematic literature review of green leadership research published between 2019 and 2024, aiming to synthesize existing knowledge, identify key themes, and propose directions for future research. Using the PRISMA framework, we analyzed 48 peer-reviewed articles from Scopus and Web of Science databases. The findings highlight four dominant themes: (1) conceptual dimensions of green leadership, (2) its impact on environmental performance, (3) mediating mechanisms, and (4) contextual influences. The review reveals that green leadership enhances sustainability outcomes through employee engagement, green culture, and organizational learning. However, gaps remain in understanding its role in SMEs, non-Western contexts, and under regulatory variations. This study contributes by offering a structured overview and a future research agenda to advance theoretical and practical applications of green leadership.

detail.title: Geolocation, Managerial Prerogatives and Fundamental Rights in Brazilian Labour Law: Privacy, Proportionality, and the Primacy of Reality
detail.abstract: This article examines the compatibility between employers' managerial prerogatives supported by geolocation technologies and the constitutional protection of privacy within Brazilian labour law, in light of the General Data Protection Law (LGPD), the Internet Civil Framework (MCI), and the labour-law principle of the primacy of reality. It argues that geolocation data may serve as proportionate and reliable evidence for working-time verification provided that data minimization, temporal limitation, and confidentiality are ensured. Drawing on recent Superior Labour Court (TST) decisions, the article proposes a proportionality-based test and datagovernance safeguards that preserve fundamental rights without undermining fact-finding.

detail.title: Selling with Seduction: Analyzing Lust-Based Advertising Strategies in the Philippine Alcohol Industry
detail.abstract: This study critically analyzes the impact of lust-based advertising strategies on Filipino consumers, focusing on the alcohol industry in Gen. T. De Leon, Valenzuela City. Anchored on the Elaboration Likelihood Model and Sex Appeal Theory, the study utilized a quantitative descriptive-correlational design and surveyed 405 respondents aged 18-59. Results show that lust-based advertising can elicit consumer perceptions and attitudes, with provocative themes (e.g., rebellion, going against social expectations) proving more persuasive than explicit sexual imagery. These advertisements effectively gain attention, create interest, and enhance brand recall, but are less effective at creating intense emotions or lasting brand loyalty. The study concludes that although lust-based advertisements can attract consumers, they raise significant ethical concerns regarding gender representation and public health, particularly for younger audiences. Recommendations include the adoption of more value-driven appeals and stricter digital advertising policies to ensure responsible marketing.

title: Brand Discourse Analysis of the #EnjoyResponsibly Campaign: Upholding Brand Social Responsibility Values

detail.title: Brand Discourse Analysis of the #EnjoyResponsibly Campaign: Upholding Brand Social Responsibility Values
detail.abstract: This study aims to analyse Heineken's brand communication strategy in promoting the values of Brand Social Responsibility (BSR) through the digital campaign #EnjoyResponsibly. Using a qualitative approach with the Brand Discourse Analysis (BDA) method, the research focuses on four main aspects: message, mode, medium, and milieu. Data were collected through campaign documentation on social media and other digital platforms, then analysed by examining message elements, media, and the socio-cultural context surrounding the brand communication. The results show that Heineken consistently delivers BSR values through educational messages, appealing visual styles, and effective media channels. The campaign also demonstrates strong engagement with the social environment through community collaboration and the use of popular cultural moments. This research concludes that Heineken's BSR strategy in the #EnjoyResponsibly campaign successfully builds a responsible brand image while educating the Indonesian public about mindful, healthy alcohol consumption.

title: Coordination through Bargaining in Weakest-link Games
affiliations: New York University (NYU) - New York University, Abu Dhabi, New York University (NYU) - New York University, Abu Dhabi and New York University (NYU) - New York University, Abu Dhabi

detail.title: Coordination through Bargaining in Weakest-link Games
detail.abstract: Coordination problems are often modeled as weakest-link games, where the minimum-contributing agent determines their group's surplus to be shared in equal parts. Yet in many settings, the sharing of a jointly-produced surplus occurs through bargaining, which acts as a double-edged sword: It can promote effort by disciplining low contributors or deter it through the added uncertainty of returns. We present experimental evidence that bargaining improves coordination by promoting equitable divisions that reward higher contributions, even in one-shot interactions. High contributors are more likely than low contributors to propose allocations that reward effort, creating a virtuous cycle that increases efficiency. Allowing groups to endogenously select who can act as proposers can backfire: Efficiency increases when high contributors are endorsed but falls otherwise. These results highlight the scope and limits of participatory surplus division mechanisms in providing incentives for efficient coordination.

detail.title: Financial Shocks, Productivity, and Prices

publicationDetails.journalName: National Bank of Belgium Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: We study the interconnection between the productivity and pricing effects of financial shocks. Combining administrative records on firm-level output prices and quantities with quasi-experimental variation in credit supply, we show that a tightening of credit conditions has a persistent, yet delayed, negative effect on firms’ long-run physical productivity growth (TFPQ) but also induces firms to change their pricing policies. Commonly used revenue-based productivity measures (TFPR)—which conflate price and productivity—offer biased predictions regarding the consequences of financial shocks for firms’ productivity growth, underestimating the long-run elasticity of physical productivity to credit supply by half. We also show that the pricing adjustments themselves have productivity implications. Firms use low pricing as a source of internal financing, allowing them to avoid cutting expenditures on productivity-enhancing activities, thereby softening the impact of financial shocks. We incorporate these forces into a quantitative model of firm dynamics to quantify the importance of productivity and pricing dynamics (and their interplay) in driving the scarring effects of financial crises on aggregate productivity and welfare.

detail.abstract: This paper aims to analyze the implementation of Statement of Financial Accounting Standards (PSAK) 234 concerning Interim Financial Reports at PT Asri Karya Lestari Tbk for the period ending March 31, 2025. This research uses a qualitative descriptive method with a case study approach based on consolidated financial statement data obtained from the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) website. The analysis is conducted by comparing the components and disclosures of the company's interim financial statements against the minimum requirements of PSAK 234. The results of the study indicate that the interim financial report of PT Asri Karya Lestari Tbk has complied with all the main components of PSAK 234, including the presentation of the statement of financial position, profit and loss, changes in equity, cash flows, and notes to the financial statements. The company has also included a statement of compliance with Financial Accounting Standards (SAK). However, several aspects of disclosure were found that need improvement, such as management's analysis of the decline in profit, sustained negative operating cash flow, and details of debt covenants and the financial impact of legal disputes. Overall, the implementation of PSAK 234 in the Q1 2025 interim financial report of PT Asri Karya Lestari Tbk has met the standards, although the quality of disclosure can be improved to be more informative for investors and regulators.

title: What's the Value of Music, and who Should Decide its Worth?
affiliations: Stockholm School of Economics

detail.title: What's the Value of Music, and who Should Decide its Worth?
detail.abstract: In the streaming era, music revenues have become increasingly measurable, which has led to a surge in music rights investments. Yet the question of how to assess the value of music as an investable asset remains largely unresolved. This paper explores how to value something as priceless as music, outlining the shift from costly expert valuation of music rights to auction and participatory market models. Using Tangy Market as a case study, it examines how datadriven machine learning founded valuation and real-time trading can improve price transparency and lower transaction costs. The findings suggest that open, participatory markets may enhance price discovery and help define a fair market value for music.

title: Institutional Trust as a Lever to Integrate Iraq’s Informal Economy

detail.title: Institutional Trust as a Lever to Integrate Iraq’s Informal Economy
detail.abstract:
This research examines the role of institutional trust as a strategic lever for integrating Iraq’s informal economy into the formal state system. It begins by mapping the current landscape of the informal economy, its scale, dominant patterns, and its interaction with governmental institutions. The study argues that weak institutional trust—across legislative, executive, and service-delivery bodies—constitutes a fundamental barrier to integration, compelling individuals and small businesses to avoid official channels and prefer an unregulated environment where they perceive greater protection and flexibility.
Adopting an analytical approach that combines quantitative indicators with a sociological perspective, the research explores the link between institutional trust and the behaviour of economic actors. The findings indicate that rebuilding trust can become a dynamic tool for change through transparent digital services, simplified procedures, and practical incentives that demonstrate the real benefits of joining the formal system. The study also discusses international examples where trust-building—rather than mere legal enforcement—proved essential in integrating large informal sectors into the legal and administrative framework.
Ultimately, the research proposes a multi-layered practical framework that includes legal and administrative reforms, tailored digital solutions, and community engagement models. Together, these elements aim to redefine the relationship between citizens and the state, paving the way for gradual and effective integration of Iraq’s informal economy while strengthening institutional credibility as a reliable economic actor.

Unlike print ads, web ads are dynamic and interactive, which makes them difficult to archive and replay (i.e., load archived web resources in a web browser) successfully . To explore these challenges, we created a dataset of 279 archived web ads. During this study, we identified five major problems with archiving and replaying web ads, which we discuss in detail in our article "Problems With Archiving and Replaying Current Web Advertisements".

title: Hybrid Augmented Reasoning Interpretation (HARI) Framework for Massive Scientific Literature Semantic Retrieval Analysis
affiliations: Beijing Information Science and Technology University, Beijing Information Science and Technology University, Beijing Information Science and Technology University and Beijing Information Science and Technology University

detail.title: Hybrid Augmented Reasoning Interpretation (HARI) Framework for Massive Scientific Literature Semantic Retrieval Analysis
detail.abstract: Classical retrieval methods based on classifications, bibliometrics, keywords, and Subject-Action-Object (SAO) features have reached limitations in semantic understanding, ranking, and interpretability. To address these issues, a Hybrid Augmented Reasoning Interpretation (HARI) framework was proposed. The objective was to enhance retrieval precision and interpretability in large-scale scientific literature. Within this framework, a functional knowledge graph (FOPNet) was constructed to capture fine-grained semantic structures. A hybrid retrieval strategy combining keyword-based search and FOPNet-derived semantic vectors was applied, followed by RankNet-based reranking. Experimental evaluation was conducted on the USPTO (over 30 million patents) and arXiv (over 2 million papers) datasets. Results showed that FOPNet-based reranking improved ranking accuracy by 31.8%, while the hybrid retrieval strategy yielded a 36.2% improvement. Furthermore, the Augmented Reasoning Interpretation (ARI) module, leveraging large language models, achieved a 49.2% increase in Hit@1 and Hit@10. Overall, the HARI framework significantly advanced retrieval performance and interpretability.

title: Evaluating Multiple Classifiers and Model Quantization Techniques for Efficient On-Device Android Malware Detection
affiliations: Government of the United States of America - Air University, Government of the United States of America - Air University and Government of the United States of America - Air University

detail.title: Evaluating Multiple Classifiers and Model Quantization Techniques for Efficient On-Device Android Malware Detection
detail.abstract: The increasing sophistication of Android malware poses significant security challenges that demand efficient and scalable detection solutions, particularly for resource-constrained mobile environments. Although numerous machine learning  approaches based on static, dynamic or hybrid features have been proposed  for android malware detection; yet, the best performance has been of the ones based on  hybrid features. However, the contemporary solutions suffer from low accuracy and high computational cost. Thereby;  we propose an Android malware detection approach that integrates feature reduction with the NODE architecture, an attention-inspired deep learning framework, to deliver an effective and efficient detection solution. We initially analyzed five different classifiers, including Multi-layer Perceptron, Gradient boosting classifiers (XGBoost, CatBoost and LightGBM) coupled with CNN based feature extraction and NODE, by considering the complete feature set. Later on we applied mutual information analysis to reduce the feature set to analyze the effectiveness and efficiency of both complete and reduced feature based options. We evaluated the models on the subset of the Kronodroid dataset (41,382 malware and 36,755 benign samples) and achieved a detection accuracy of up to 99\% (for all classifiers, with feature reduction). All the classifiers were evaluated in detail by assessing precision, recall, and F1-score using confusion matrices, making NODE as our best performing model. To overcome limitations associated with deploying such model on edge devices, we conducted an extensive evaluation of various compression techniques such as full integer quantization, dynamic range quantization, and float-16 quantization and identified dynamic range quantization as the most effective approach. This approach efficiently reduced the model's size and computational overhead while preserving higher classification rate and an accuracy of 92.3\%. Real-world testing on a resource-constrained mobile device demonstrated that our quantized model successfully identified all malware and benign apps from 60 test samples of Kronodroid dataset by utilizing key static and dynamic features. Overall, our work offers a practical and efficient solution for Android malware detection in constrained environments, advancing the development of lightweight, high-performance security models capable of operating effectively on mobile devices.

title: Enhanced Fiber-Wireless Networks Performance: Multi-ONU Placement Optimization with Load Balancing and Hop Count Constraints Using Mountain Gazelle Algorithm
affiliations: , Devi Ahilya University (DAVV) and Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Technical University - Institute of Engineering & Technology

detail.title: Enhanced Fiber-Wireless Networks Performance: Multi-ONU Placement Optimization with Load Balancing and Hop Count Constraints Using Mountain Gazelle Algorithm
detail.abstract: Fiber Wireless (FiWi) Networks are multi-domain networks that integrate optical infrastructure with wireless access technology to improve overall network performance. FiWi networks offer huge bandwidth, low latency while providing a cost effective solution to the increasing need for applications such as video streaming, online gaming, and cloud based services. Optimal placement of ONUs play an important role for achieving cost effectiveness and improves the efficient utilization of resources. This research proposes a Mountain Gazelle Optimization algorithm (MGO) to optimize the placement of various ONUs while considering the various distributions of routers and ONUs. The critical constraints such as load balancing and hops number have been incorporated in the analysis to increase the efficiency of the network design. Also, the exploration and exploitation of MGO capability are analyzed through varying step size demonstrating the robustness and adaptability in ONU placement. The results obtained using MGO algorithm are benchmarked against existing metaheuristic algorithms such as Moth-Flame Optimization (MFO) and Artificial Hummingbird Optimization (AHO). The results prove that MGO algorithm consistently yields the lowest cost function value, faster convergence rate, less time complexity and provides a better exploration and exploitation balance as compared to MFO and AHO. The outcome of this research conclusively establish that MGO is a promising approach for efficient ONU placement in FiWi networks.

title: Financial Integration and Vulnerability of European Microeconomies: The Impact of Global and Eurozone Crises
affiliations: and Independent

detail.title: Financial Integration and Vulnerability of European Microeconomies: The Impact of Global and Eurozone Crises
detail.abstract: This article investigates the relationship between financial integration and the vulnerability of European microeconomies, with particular attention to the impact of the global financial crisis (2008-2009) and the eurozone sovereign debt crisis (2010-2014). While financial integration is often associated with efficiency gains, capital access, and growth opportunities, small and highly open economies face disproportionate risks due to structural constraints, limited policy autonomy, and concentrated financial systems. The study employs a mixedmethods approach: a panel dataset of European economies (1999-2020) is analyzed using econometric models, and case studies of Cyprus, Malta, and Luxembourg provide contextual depth. Quantitative results reveal a strong positive association between financial integration-especially reliance on cross-border banking liabilities-and vulnerability, with microeconomies displaying significantly higher susceptibility during crisis periods compared to larger states. Case studies illustrate the mechanisms of exposure and resilience: Cyprus exemplifies systemic fragility under excessive banking sector dependence, Malta demonstrates the benefits of selective regulation and fiscal prudence, and Luxembourg highlights the role of strong institutions in mitigating risks. Overall, findings underscore that integration amplifies vulnerabilities in microeconomies unless accompanied by robust domestic governance and effective supranational mechanisms, suggesting urgent policy needs in both national and European financial architecture.

title: Climate Resilience and Yield Vulnerability of Key Crops in Moldova: A Case Study of Wheat, Maize, and Sunflower

detail.title: Climate Resilience and Yield Vulnerability of Key Crops in Moldova: A Case Study of Wheat, Maize, and Sunflower
detail.abstract: The purpose of this research is to assess the impact of climate change on the crop production sector in the Republic of Moldova, with a focus on wheat, maize and sunflower crops, in the period 2007–2024. The analysis aims to identify the degree of resilience and vulnerability of these crops according to variations in the average annual temperature and rainfall regime. The data used in this study were from the databases of the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS), and the climatic information on temperature and precipitation was provided by the State Hydrometeorological Service (SHS). The methodology included descriptive statistical analysis and multiple regressions, in order to establish the causal relationships between the variables. The results reveal significant differences between the three crops analyzed. Sunflower show high resilience, with low yield variability and moderate correlation with rainfall. Wheat is sensitive to the rainfall regime, highlighting a strong correlation with it while maize registers the greatest production instability and a weak correlation with the climatic factors analyzed. Regression models indicate a significant impact of rainfall on wheat and sunflower yields, while temperature has negative or reduced influences. The study confirms the vulnerability of agricultural crops to climate variability and underlines the urgent need to adapt agricultural practices, by promoting drought-resistant varieties, using conservative soil technologies and developing irrigation infrastructure.

title: CROSS-BORDER DATA FLOW: A TRILEMMA OF MOBILITY, MONETIZATION, AND PRIVACY
affiliations: University of Sussex - Institute of Development Studies, University of Indonesia, University of Indonesia, University of Indonesia and

detail.title: CROSS-BORDER DATA FLOW: A TRILEMMA OF MOBILITY, MONETIZATION, AND PRIVACY
detail.abstract: This paper introduces and conceptualizes a data governance trilemma that captures the inherent tensions among cross-border data flows, data monetization, and privacy and security—three dimensions central to digital sustainability. As data becomes a foundational economic resource, policymakers face growing challenges in balancing economic value creation with long-term trust, resilience, and social legitimacy. Using data from 50 countries (2014–2020), the study empirically examines how these trade-offs manifest across economies at different stages of digital maturity, classified as Watch-Out, Break-Out, Stall-Out, and Stand-Out. The results show that less digitally mature economies tend to emphasize data monetization and cross-border flows, often at the expense of privacy and security, while more advanced economies achieve stronger data protection but experience slower monetization growth. These findings suggest that digitally sustainable governance does not arise from optimizing a single policy goal, but from managing structural trade-offs in a context-sensitive manner. The paper offers policy-relevant insights for designing adaptive data governance frameworks that support innovation, economic growth, and long-term digital sustainability.

title: ReChat: A Cloud-Based Platform for Structured Real-Time Text Interaction
affiliations: Northeastern University

detail.title: ReChat: A Cloud-Based Platform for Structured Real-Time Text Interaction
detail.abstract: ReChat is a cloud-based software system designed to administer structured real-time text interactions among multiple participants. The platform allows researchers, educational programs, and organizations such as polling firms and marketing research teams to configure chatroom templates, define question sequences, and manage participant assignment without writing code. ReChat enables preprogrammed instructions, automated moderation, and configurable waiting-room environments. Communication events are time-stamped, stored, and exportable for downstream analysis. The software supports simultaneous multi-room operation and can be embedded into external survey platforms. ReChat incorporates features for transcript reuse, participant screening, and real-time session monitoring. The system is intended for users seeking an adaptable environment for programmable text-based communication workflows and may be licensed for research, educational, or organizational applications.

title: The dynamics of social media usage: Exploring intermittent discontinuance and related factors
affiliations: Kyung Hee University and Kyung Hee University

detail.title: The dynamics of social media usage: Exploring intermittent discontinuance and related factors
detail.abstract: While users stay active in certain social media, users use certain social media in a less frequent and irregular manner without fully opting out – this behavior is defined as intermittent discontinuance. Regarding the abundance of different social media alternatives, intermittent discontinuance is accepted as a natural behavior of users. Although intermittent discontinuance imposes a great challenge for social media platforms, social media firms often overlook the importance of managing intermittent dormant users. It is also true that the discussion on intermittent dormant users has not been greatly concentrated in the academic field. In this aspect, this study systematically presented the triggers and processes of intermittent discontinuance behaviors, and derived academic and practical implications through the empirical process.

title: Bridging Conceptual and Methodological Gaps in Digital Economy Indices: A Two-Stage Framework
affiliations: Yalova University and Yalova University

detail.title: Bridging Conceptual and Methodological Gaps in Digital Economy Indices: A Two-Stage Framework
detail.abstract: Measuring the digital economy presents persistent conceptual and methodological challenges, particularly in constructing composite indices that are both robust and policy-relevant. This study proposes a two-stage framework for digital economy measurement that bridges these gaps by integrating conceptual and methodological decision points. Stage 1 clarifies the scope, objectives, units of analysis, and intended audience, ensuring internal consistency and practical relevance. Stage 2 addresses methodological considerations, including outlier treatment, handling missing data, normalization, weighting, aggregation, and robustness checks, thereby enhancing replicability and reducing arbitrariness. The framework is flexible and applicable to diverse composite indices beyond the digital economy, serving as a systematic checklist for transparent and coherent index construction. The proposed approach offers value for policymakers, academics, and practitioners by facilitating benchmarking, comparative analyses, and informed decision-making.

title: Reimagining the Future of Banking in a Protocol-Driven World
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Reimagining the Future of Banking in a Protocol-Driven World
detail.abstract:
The World is Changed. Has Your Bank?  

A fintech executive in New York, USA. An AI researcher in Amsterdam, Netherlands. An MSME owner in Bengaluru, India. Each of them interacts with money not by logging in but living. Money flows, credit adjusts, identity streams, and ethics calculate, all ambiently, intelligently, and consent driven. Not science fiction. This is the shape of banking in a  programmable world. Banks are at a crossroads. The question is no longer: "How digital are we?" It is: "How programmable, ethical, and modular is our institution?" 


Four Strategic Shifts Redefining the Future Bank

1. From Platform to Protocol Thinking : Banks must move from developing closed platforms to enabling open, interoperable protocols. Value today flows across shared infrastructure, not proprietary rails such as UPI in India or JPMorgan's Onyx.

2. Autonomous Regulation and AI-Led Compliance: Compliance is evolving from checklists to machine-based, real-time auditability. Banks like Monzo, BNP Paribas, and OCBC are using AI, smart contracts, and rule-as-code engines to reduce costs and deliver explainability.

3. ESG Scores to Ethical Intermediation: Greenwashing discredited scores. Forward-thinking banks are embedding ethics at the code layer, carbon-aware pricing, dynamic ESG-linked loans, and real-time ethical telemetry are replacing static scores.

4. Identity Custody to Consent-Led Monetization: Identity is no longer a file to have on hand; it's a trust asset to broker. With federated ID, reusable credentials, and consent in the hands of the customers, banks like Capital One and Caixa Bank are transforming into identity orchestrators.


Strategic Implication for Leadership

Banks must reimagine themselves as "Programmable Institutions" which:

• Orchestrate trust among ecosystems

• Bake compliance into operations, not surveillance

• Monetize identity and ethics—not just deposits and loans


Future revenues will not derive from what you own, but what you enable, command, and responsibly grow.


“The danger is not FinTechs. It is irrelevance. The reward is not market share, it is trust-share.”

title: E-Commerce Customer Satisfaction: Expectation versus Reality of Online Shoppers
affiliations: Western Philippines University and

detail.title: E-Commerce Customer Satisfaction: Expectation versus Reality of Online Shoppers
detail.abstract: The study aims to elucidate the level of satisfaction of online shoppers, the expectations and realities of shopping experiences, and the problems encountered. Additionally, it investigates the significant relationships and differences between the main variables of the study. The study employs a quantitative-descriptive correlational research design; data were collected through scrutinized questionnaires and analyzed using frequency counts, percentages, weighted means, the Chi-Square Test of Association, and the Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test. Utilizing quota and convenience sampling, the study gathered responses from 352 online shoppers within the research locale, supplemented by faceto-face interviews to ensure data validity and depth. The results revealed that most respondents were aged 15 to 21, female, single students, college undergraduates, had a business with a monthly income of 10,000 to 24,599 pesos, and frequently used Shopee to purchase clothing. Respondents expressed a high level of satisfaction with product delivery services; however, their expectations of product quality were often unmet. While no significant correlation was found between demographic profiles and purchased products, significant differences emerged between expectations and actual experiences regarding product quality, delivery, and packaging. Delayed delivery was the most common problem encountered by the respondents. The study recommends further exploration to bridge the gap between consumer expectations and online shopping experiences. Additionally, future researchers investigate the findings and consider the recommendations made by the researcher.

title: Who Pays When the Agent Fails? Liability Frameworks for Autonomous Payment Systems in a Fragmented Regulatory Landscape
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Who Pays When the Agent Fails? Liability Frameworks for Autonomous Payment Systems in a Fragmented Regulatory Landscape
detail.abstract:
Autonomous AI payment agents represent a fundamental shift in financial intermediation, moving from deterministic software executing pre-programmed instructions to adaptive systems making independent decisions in real time. While recent research demonstrates that AI agents can successfully replicate treasury management and cash optimisation tasks, a critical gap remains unaddressed: who bears liability when these autonomous systems fail? This paper examines how current liability frameworks designed for human principals and deterministic software break down when applied to agentic payment systems that learn from experience, make autonomous decisions and operate across fragmented regulatory jurisdictions.

Through detailed analysis of three failure scenarios (hallucinating payment agents causing supplier damage, regulatory arbitrage agents exploiting weak-AML corridors and flash crash events from correlated agent behavior), this paper identifies specific breakpoints in existing legal architectures. Traditional liability regimes rely on concepts of direct causation, human intent and jurisdictional clarity all of which become ambiguous when autonomous agents make emergent decisions across borders. The fragmented global regulatory landscape exacerbates these challenges: the EU AI Act treats payment systems ambiguously; the United States lacks federal AI legislation and cross-border enforcement mechanisms remain underdeveloped.

This paper proposes a graduated liability framework that distinguishes between policy defects, credential compromises, infrastructure failures, model errors, and emergent coordination failures. The framework establishes clear responsibility allocation across the payment ecosystem model developers, system deployers, financial institutions, and end users while accounting for the unique characteristics of autonomous decision-making. Additionally, the paper argues for harmonised cross-border standards, mandatory insurance requirements and specialised dispute resolution mechanisms to address the liability uncertainty that currently threatens the viability of agentic payment systems.

title: Context-Aware Visual Prompting: Automating Geospatial Web Dashboards Using Large Language Models and AI Agents for Decision Support
affiliations: Government of the United States of America - Oak Ridge National Laboratory, Oak Ridge National Laboratory and Government of the United States of America - Oak Ridge National Laboratory

detail.title: Context-Aware Visual Prompting: Automating Geospatial Web Dashboards Using Large Language Models and AI Agents for Decision Support
detail.abstract: The development of web-based geospatial dashboards for risk analysis and decision support is often challenged by the difficulty in visualization of big, multi-dimensional environmental data, implementation complexity, and limited automation. We introduce a generative AI framework that harnesses Large Language Models (LLMs) to automate the creation of interactive geospatial dashboards from user-defined inputs, including UI wireframes, requirements, and data sources. By incorporating a structured knowledge graph, the workflow embeds domain knowledge into the generation process and enables accurate and context-aware code completions. A key component of our approach is the Context-Aware Visual Prompting (CAVP) mechanism, which extracts, encodes, and interfaces semantics from visual layouts to guide LLM-driven generation of codes. The new framework also integrates a self-validation mechanism that uses an agent-based LLM and Pass@k evaluation alongside semantic metrics to ensure output reliability. Dashboard snippets are paired with data visualization codebases and ontological representations, enabling a pipeline that produces scalable React-based completions using the MVVM architectural pattern. Our results demonstrate improved performance over baseline approaches and expanded functionality over third-party platforms, while incorporating multi-page, fully functional interfaces. We successfully developed a framework to implement LLMs, demonstrated the pipeline for automated code generation, deployment, and employed chain-of-thought AI agents for self-validation. This integrative approach, guided by structured knowledge and visual prompts, offers an innovative geospatial solution for enhancing risk analysis and decision-making.

title: Onto-Security Checks: An Ontology-Based Reasoning Approach for Automated Security Verification in Software Architectures
affiliations: University of Batna 2,  and

detail.title: Onto-Security Checks: An Ontology-Based Reasoning Approach for Automated Security Verification in Software Architectures
detail.abstract: Software architectures are growing so complex that existing security verification methodologies can no longer efficiently identify and handle vulnerabilities at the architectural level. **This paper presents Onto-Security Checks**, an ontology-based approach for the automated security verification of software architectures. The approach is based on a security ontology a semantic OWL model representing key entities of the problem domain, such as users, systems, vulnerabilities, threats, countermeasures, and risks, and their relationships and extends it with logical SWRL rules and SPARQL queries to detect non-protected components, infer new risks from known weaknesses, and suggest countermeasures. The method is arranged into seven phases, ranging from architecture extraction to ontological reasoning and report generation. We demonstrate the approach through two case studies, namely Damn Vulnerable Web Application (DVWA) and a realworld Pharmacy Management System (PMS). Detection rates stand at 1.00 in all the tested scenarios; the engine has consistently found missing protection means, derived non-trivial risk chains, and proposed consistent mitigation strategies. Reasoning times remain low (≈2.0 s for single systems and ≈9.0 s for configurations with ten replicated subsystems), thus showing practical scalability for small to medium-sized architectures. Overall, Onto-Security Checks will increase the reliability, explainability, and automation of architecture-level security verification through semantic modeling and logical reasoning, thereby contributing to information system security and modernization.

title: Artificial Intelligence: An Economic Miracle or an Economic Disaster?
affiliations: Moscow State Institute of International Relations (MGIMO)

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence: An Economic Miracle or an Economic Disaster?
detail.abstract: A study of the readiness of economic solutions for the use of various artificial intelligence (AI) models is presented, in contrast to the existing approach, when types of economic solutions are experimentally selected for a specific AI model. It is argued that the formation of assessments on the possibility of using AI in economic decisions should take into account the historical experience of creating automated control systems, which argues for the inevitability of a wave-like (cyclical) development of the "boom-bust" type. It is shown that in classical studies, the understanding of the category "economic decision" is different, while the interpretation of economic decisions through the prism of economic theory shows their unwillingness to use AI, while the managerial view is much closer to modern AI models. The importance of the still not fully realized premise of the need to initially divide all solutions into structured, poorly structured and unstructured ones is shown, despite the existence of such a classification for more than half a century. In conclusion, the most common strategies of modern AI implementation are systematized, showing the lack of criteria-based approaches to choosing implemented AI models, relying only on an experimental approach.

title: Mandatory Sharing of Trade Secrets: International Flexibilities and EU Models
affiliations: King's College London and King’s College London

detail.title: Mandatory Sharing of Trade Secrets: International Flexibilities and EU Models

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None.
declarations.ethicsApproval: None.
declarations.funderStatement: None.

detail.abstract:
The issue of mandatory sharing of trade secrets came to the fore during the Covid-19 pandemic. In essence, the concern was that any compulsory licence or waiver of patent rights on much needed vaccines would be thwarted by the ability to keep secret vital know-how related to how best to manufacture them.  As such, there were calls for mandatory sharing (or compulsory licensing) of trade secrets in the face of this public health crisis. Other concerns, too, have been expressed about the potential for trade secret protection to impede data sharing, whether in relation to AI innovation and transparency, aftermarket services for interconnected products, or transparent pricing for pharmaceuticals. In short, the obstructive use of trade secret protection in order to thwart public interest objectives has been gaining greater attention.

This chapter will tackle the circumstances in which the sharing of trade secrets may be mandated for public interest purposes. It will do this through the lenses of international and EU law. Section II will start by discussing the flexibilities within the TRIPs Agreement that enable Member States to facilitate the sharing of trade secrets. It will suggest that countries largely have discretion in how they design their mandatory sharing regimes, subject to an overarching “reasonableness” guide. Sections III and IV will examine two regimes for mandatory sharing of trade secrets that have emerged in the EU, which we believe are consistent with the TRIPs Agreement and offer useful models for other countries to follow. The first is the proposed Regulation on compulsory licensing for crisis management, which, at the European Parliament stage, included mandatory sharing of trade secrets necessary to ensure the effective compulsory licensing of patented crisis related products. The second is the Data Act, which creates mandatory data sharing for Internet of Things (“IoT”) data. Section V will draw out seven observations from these two models of mandatory sharing of trade secrets that need to be considered when designing such frameworks in the future. These lessons include how the regimes must meet the “reasonableness” requirement we see mandated in TRIPs, and some unresolved challenges in the regimes, which only emerge after deeper investigation.

title: Understanding Our Reactions: A Unified Model of Human Behavior Under Uncertainty

detail.title: Understanding Our Reactions: A Unified Model of Human Behavior Under Uncertainty
detail.abstract: Humans often believe their reactions̶fear, defensiveness, avoidance, misinterpretation, collapse̶reflect personal flaws or fixed traits. This paper proposes a unified, predictive model showing that these reactions are instead automatic outputs of a nervous system responding to uncertainty.

title: Exploring the Potential of Information and Multimedia Technologies in Teaching High School Physics in Kazakhstan
affiliations: Kazakh National Women's Teacher Training University, Almaty, Kazakhstan

detail.title: Exploring the Potential of Information and Multimedia Technologies in Teaching High School Physics in Kazakhstan
detail.abstract: The integration of Information and Multimedia Technologies (IMTs) in high school physics education presents a transformative potential for teaching methodologies and student learning outcomes. This paper explores the multifaceted opportunities that IMTs offer in enhancing the delivery and comprehension of physics concepts in high school settings. Through a comprehensive review of existing literature and educational practices, we identify key areas where IMTs can significantly contribute, including interactive simulations, virtual laboratories, and digital content platforms. These technologies afford students the ability to visualize complex physics phenomena more intuitively and engagingly, thereby facilitating a deeper understanding of the subject matter. Moreover, the use of IMTs encourages active learning, critical thinking, and collaborative problem-solving among students, aligning with contemporary educational goals. The paper also addresses challenges in implementing these technologies, such as accessibility, teacher training, and curriculum integration, proposing strategies to overcome these barriers. Empirical evidence suggests that students who engage with physics content through IMTs demonstrate improved academic performance, increased motivation, and a stronger interest in STEM fields. This study underscores the importance of adopting IMTs in high school physics education as a means to prepare students for the demands of the 21st-century knowledge economy and to inspire the next generation of scientists and engineers.

title: The Career Services Premium: How University Job Placement Boosts Graduate Earnings
affiliations: UPF Barcelona School of Management, University of Glasgow - School of Education and European Union - Joint Research Centre-Seville

detail.title: The Career Services Premium: How University Job Placement Boosts Graduate Earnings
detail.abstract: Purpose: This paper assesses the impact of university career services on graduates' earnings. Design/methodology/approach: Using data from a Catalan graduate follow up survey for the period 2008-2023, we compare the earnings of graduates that accessed first job after graduation through a university provided careers services, with those entering employment through alternative routes. Drawing on the richness of the dataset, we employ an instrumental variable approach to overcome bias from non-random sorting of graduates into job entry routes. Findings: We find an earnings premium for those that accessed the first job through university career service. These effects are particularly strong for women and graduates with limited work experience. Originality/value: To our awareness, this is to date the only estimate of the causal impact of university career services on graduate earnings. Research limitations: This study is based on repeated cross-sectional survey, and it cannot assess the medium and long-term returns of university career services. Practical implications: Our results show that the return of investment of career services is higher for women and for those with limited working experience. Social Implications: The paper contributes robust evidence which suggests scaling-up employability practices is an effective education policy for ameliorating labour market inequalities.

title: Comparison of IFRS and SAK Implementation in Improving Transparency and Sustainability of Company Financial Reports in Indonesia

detail.title: Comparison of IFRS and SAK Implementation in Improving Transparency and Sustainability of Company Financial Reports in Indonesia
detail.abstract: This study aims to analyze the comparative implementation of International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) and Financial Accounting Standards (SAK) in Indonesia in supporting transparency and sustainability of financial reporting. Through a descriptive qualitative approach and a literature review of recent research, the analysis shows that the convergence of IFRS into SAK has a significant impact on improving financial reporting accountability, particularly for public companies and entities with international ties. However, IFRS implementation still faces obstacles such as limited human resource competency, digital infrastructure gaps, and adaptation challenges in the micro, small, and medium enterprise (MSME) sector. These findings demonstrate the importance of synergy between regulators, the accounting profession, and the business sector in strengthening transparent, accountable, and sustainable financial reporting practices in Indonesia.

title: Beyond profits: exploring the role of religion in shaping financial decision-making on global dividend policies
affiliations: Cardiff School of Management, Cardiff Metropolitan University UK, Cardiff School of Management, Cardiff Metropolitan University UK and University of Central Lancashire

detail.title: Beyond profits: exploring the role of religion in shaping financial decision-making on global dividend policies

keywords: Tobit regression Paper type Research article

detail.abstract: Purpose-This study investigates how an informal institution in the shape of religion shapes corporate dividend policies across countries. It examines both the direct influence of dominant religious affiliations and the moderating roles of national culture and legal origin. Design/methodology/approach-Using a comprehensive panel of 45,899 listed firms from 90 countries over the period 1987-2019 (344,014 firm-year observations), we employ Logit models to analyse dividend payment propensity and Tobit models to estimate dividend size. Religion is measured at the national level by the dominant religious affiliation, while Hofstede's cultural dimensions and legal origin (common vs. civil law) are incorporated as moderators. Robustness tests include cultural interactions, legal traditions and dynamic panel estimations with lagged dividends to address potential endogeneity. Findings-We find robust evidence that religion influences dividend policy. Catholic, Hindu, Indigenous, Jewish, Islamic and Orthodox contexts are positively associated with dividend payments and sizes, while Atheist, Buddhist and Protestant contexts exhibit negative associations. The moderation results show that Hofstede's Uncertainty Avoidance Index (UAI) amplifies Catholic and Islamic tendencies toward higher payouts while reinforcing Protestant restraint. Legal origin further conditions these effects: in Common Law systems, results align with the outcome hypothesis, where strong shareholder rights discipline payouts; in Civil Law systems, findings support the substitute hypothesis, with higher dividends used to compensate for weaker investor protection. Research limitations/implications-This research provides evidence that religious background significantly shapes corporate dividend policy, implying that religious affiliations may be as important as the personal traits of executives in shaping corporate financial decisions. This highlights how religious contexts can moderate traditional influences, such as legal origin and national culture, thereby affecting how companies set their dividend policies. Originality/value-This study makes three contributions. First, it extends the scope of prior literature by analysing nine major world religions, rather than focussing narrowly on Protestant, Catholic or Islamic contexts. Second, it demonstrates how religion interacts with broader institutional environments, national culture and legal systems to shape financial outcomes, thereby advancing theoretical integration between finance and sociology. Third, by employing a uniquely large and diverse crosscountry dataset over 3 decades, it offers one of the most comprehensive examinations of the intersection between religion and corporate payout policy.

title: Comparative Algorithmic Governance of Public Health Instruments Across India, EU, US and LMICS

detail.title: Comparative Algorithmic Governance of Public Health Instruments Across India, EU, US and LMICS
detail.abstract: This study investigates the juridico-technological architecture of international public health instruments. It focuses specifically on their differential implementation across India, the European Union, the United States, and LMICs, particularly in Sub-Saharan Africa. Despite the proliferation of binding nature the International Health Regulations (IHR 2005) and the WHO FCTC, jurisdictional asymmetries in compliance remain pronounced. The study addresses a critical research lacuna: the inadequate harmonisation between normative health law and algorithmic public health infrastructures in resource-constrained and technologically underserved jurisdictions. The principal objective is to assess the extent to which artificial intelligence augments IPHI implementation while analysing emergent doctrinal and infrastructural bottlenecks. Employing a comparative doctrinal analysis and legal-normative mapping, the study triangulates legislative instruments, WHO monitoring frameworks, AI applications (e.g., BlueDot, Aarogya Setu, EIOS), and compliance metrics. Preliminary results demonstrate that while AI technologies have enhanced early detection, surveillance precision, and health system responsiveness in high-capacity jurisdictions, LMICs continue to encounter impediments due to infrastructural scarcities, data privacy vacuums, and fragmented legal scaffolding. Notably, the EU’s Artificial Intelligence Act and GDPR present promising regulatory prototypes for health-oriented algorithmic governance, whereas LMICs exhibit embryonic AI integration, limited internet penetration, and insufficient jurisprudential coherence. The findings underscore the imperative of embedding AI within a rights-compliant, supranationally coordinated regulatory framework to ensure equitable health outcomes and compliance with global normative instruments. This research advances the discourse by proposing a model for global algorithmic treaty-making inspired by FCTC architecture and advocates for WHO-led compliance mechanisms modelled on WTO’s Dispute Settlement Body. The study offers a prescriptive framework aimed at reconciling technological modernisation with public health legality to fortify pandemic preparedness, surveillance equity, and transnational governance resilience.

title: The Lasting Impact of Youth Bullying Exposure on Adult Labor Market Outcomes: An Inter-Disciplinary Review of the Literature
affiliations: Vanderbilt University, University of Texas at San Antonio - College of Business - Department of Economics and Vanderbilt University

detail.title: The Lasting Impact of Youth Bullying Exposure on Adult Labor Market Outcomes: An Inter-Disciplinary Review of the Literature
detail.abstract: Higher direct and indirect exposure to bullying has been linked to long-term increases in healthcare costs, worse mental health, and poorer social relationships as well as a reduction in human capital accumulation and economic productivity. Consequently, preventing and mitigating the long-lasting negative effects of bullying has become a worldwide challenge for school and health policies. This paper aims to review the evidence supporting an effect on earlylife bullying victimization on adult socioeconomic outcomes and develop an integrative framework for understanding these effects that encompasses (1) how bullying processes emerge and are sustained during childhood and adolescence; (2) how they affect labor opportunities in adulthood; (3) the mediating role of skill, social capital, identity, and mental health; and (4) how social structures as well as individual characteristics determined early in life (e.g., innate capacities, vulnerability and susceptibility) may operate as moderators or potential confounders. Our framework draws from theoretical and empirical work in education and labor economics as well as in clinical and developmental psychology. Our integration and synthesis on how the processes relate over time provides researchers, practitioners, and policymakers concrete directions for future research and support evidence-based arguments in favor of continued development and improvement of antibullying programs by both schools and governments.

detail.abstract: The accelerating integration of digital technologies into governance has transformed the nature of state power in the 21st century. Governments across the world now deploy sophisticated surveillance infrastructures ranging from biometric recognition systems and big data analytics to artificial intelligence-driven predictive policing to monitor, categorize, and influence their citizens. While initially justified in the name of security and efficiency, these technologies have increasingly become instruments of political control, enabling what scholars term digital authoritarianism. This paper offers a comparative analysis of digital authoritarianism as a global phenomenon, focusing on how digital surveillance erodes democratic accountability, privacy, and freedom of expression. It draws on case studies from China, Russia, the European Union, and Turkey, demonstrating that digital authoritarianism is not limited to autocracies but also emerges within liberal democracies under the guise of "technological governance." The paper concludes by proposing a normative framework for balancing innovation with human rights protection and suggests an international digital ethics compact to safeguard democracy in the algorithmic age.

title: Hidden Vulnerability of Banking System: A Climate Transition Risk Stress Test Framework Under NGFS Scenarios
affiliations: School of Management, Northwestern Polytechnical University, Northwestern Polytechnic University (NPU), Northwestern Polytechnical University and

detail.title: Hidden Vulnerability of Banking System: A Climate Transition Risk Stress Test Framework Under NGFS Scenarios
detail.abstract: With the global push towards a low-carbon economy, climate transition risk is increasingly recognized as a pivotal factor affecting financial stability worldwide. Transition risk not only affects the financial performance of banks but also extends to the entire banking system through interbank contagion effects. We developed a network-based stress testing framework using the DebtRank model, which combines scenarios from the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS) with an analysis of transition risks and intersectoral spillover effects. This framework helps us trace how climate policy shocks can impact hidden vulnerabilities within China's banking system. The results indicate that (1) changes in primary energy consumption significantly impact the fossil fuel sector, which in turn affects other sectors through spillover effects, thereby increasing pressure on the banking system; (2) state-controlled large commercial banks experience the highest direct losses among all categories of banks, while foreign-funded banks incur the lowest losses; and (3) the DebtRank model reveals the banking system's hidden vulnerability: the greatest transition risk lies not in traditional systemically important banks (such as state-controlled large commercial banks) but in certain smaller-scale banks once interbank contagion is considered. The insights obtained from this study provide valuable guidance for regulators in effectively managing climate risk and maintaining the stability of the banking system.

title: Stoic Attitude as a Psychological Resource. An Integrative Model of Stoic Cognition, Emotion and Action in the Light of Modern Self-Regulation

detail.title: Stoic Attitude as a Psychological Resource. An Integrative Model of Stoic Cognition, Emotion and Action in the Light of Modern Self-Regulation
detail.abstract: This article develops an original and theoretically grounded model of stoic attitude as a psychological resource. While the relevance of Stoicism has increased in contemporary discussions of resilience and self-regulation, no existing framework captures its core components in a conceptually coherent and empirically testable way. The present work introduces a three-dimensional model that conceptualizes stoic attitude as the interaction of stoic cognition, stoic emotion and stoic action. Stoic cognition refers to rational appraisal, clarity about control and deliberate guidance of thought. Stoic emotion describes the capacity to integrate affect without being dominated by it. Stoic action reflects value aligned and reason guided behaviour in concrete situations. Drawing on research in emotion regulation, cognitive appraisal, resilience and moral psychology, the model connects ancient philosophical principles with modern empirical theory. On this basis, a measurement approach is outlined and testable hypotheses are derived. The contribution of this article is original in that it integrates stoic cognition, emotion and action for the first time into a unified framework that can be operationalized and empirically examined in future research.

title: Steering Frontier Artificial Intelligence: Venture Capital, Governance Incentives, and the Innovation Trajectory of Advanced AI
affiliations: University of San Francisco, University of San Francisco

detail.title: Steering Frontier Artificial Intelligence: Venture Capital, Governance Incentives, and the Innovation Trajectory of Advanced AI
detail.abstract: Advances in frontier artificial intelligence are increasingly driven by large-scale models with broad generalization capabilities, raising governance challenges with systemic economic and societal implications (Bostrom, 2014; Russell, 2019; Weidinger et al., 2021). While prior research has emphasized technical alignment and regulatory approaches (Amodei et al., 2016; Floridi and Cowls, 2019; NIST, 2023), the role of venture capital (VC) in shaping the innovation trajectory of advanced AI remains underexamined (Dafoe, 2018; OECD, 2023). This paper develops a conceptual framework integrating AI governance, innovation economics, and labor market research to examine how capital allocation influences organizational incentives, safety investment, and deployment behavior in frontier AI systems.  We identify four archetypal VC positioning strategies—Accelerator, Guardian, Neutral Capital Provider, and Bridge Builder—and analyze their implications for governance quality, competitive dynamics, and long-horizon risk (Gompers and Lerner, 2004; Kortum and Lerner, 2000). Comparative synthesis across leading AI organizations, complemented by evidence from global industry and workforce surveys, reveals substantial heterogeneity in governance structures driven by financial and institutional design rather than technical architecture alone (Kaplan et al., 2020; Stanford HAI, 2024; World Economic Forum, 2023).  The analysis suggests that conventional venture capital models optimized for rapid scaling are increasingly misaligned with the governance requirements of advanced AI, while long-horizon investment structures may reduce systemic risk while sustaining innovation (Mazzucato, 2018; UNESCO, 2022).

title: Correcting the Factor Mirage: A Research Protocol for Causal Factor Investing
affiliations: Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, Cornell University - Operations Research & Industrial Engineering and Abu Dhabi Investment Authority

detail.title: Correcting the Factor Mirage: A Research Protocol for Causal Factor Investing
detail.abstract: In factor investing, p-hacking is a well-understood cause of false positives. A far less studied cause is factor model specification choices encouraged by the current econometric canon. We prove that specification errors can cause factor strategies to underperform and potentially yield systematic losses, even if all risk premia remain constant and are estimated with the correct sign. Unlike the p-hacking–driven factor zoo, where noise is mistaken for signal through repeated testing, we identify a distinct phenomenon—the factor mirage— in which canonical econometric practices systematically reward misspecified models that appear statistically strong but are structurally flawed. We show that these practices, especially overcontrolling for colliders, increase the likelihood of few-shot p-hacking and adverse outcomes. The implication is that specification errors are a more insidious and underappreciated threat to investors than previously recognized. To our knowledge, this is the first study to connect factor model selection, collider bias, underperformance, and systematic losses through a unified causal framework. These findings challenge the scientific credibility and long-term viability of the current associational (noncausal) multi-trillion-dollar factor investing industry. To address these risks, we propose adjustments to the econometric canon, informed by recent advances in machine learning and causal inference.

detail.abstract: Modern international conflicts are increasingly taking place below classic escalation thresholds and combining diplomatic, economic, technological and digital means into hybrid strategies of influence. These developments pose structural challenges to international law, as central norms such as the prohibition of the use of force, the prohibition of intervention, and the rules of state attributability are designed for a binary understanding of war and peace. This article examines the legal scope and limits of state diplomacy in an environment in which states deliberately operate with strategic ambiguity and use operational intermediate layers of private and semi-state actors to avoid immediate accountability. The analysis shows that although current international law provides essential normative guardrails, these are increasingly circumvented or undermined by hybrid means of influence. Digital and economic interventions generate effects that are highly politically relevant but are difficult to classify legally. The article argues that a further development of international law is needed that considers the cumulative effects of subliminal measures, adapts the rules of attribution to complex constellations of actors and readjusts the scope of protection of political autonomy. Only through targeted normative clarifications and institutional reforms can international law preserve its stabilising function in the age of hybrid conflicts. The results show that existing categories of international law are no longer sufficient to systematically capture hybrid strategies of influence and that normative and institutional adjustments are necessary to ensure the protection of political autonomy under modern conflict conditions. The analysis thus provides a basis for future research on functional coercive concepts, extended attribution models and international governance mechanisms in the digital and hybrid power environment.

detail.title: Evaluating the Performance and Reliability of Lulc Change Simulation Models: Ca-markov and Ca-ann Within the Southwestern Region of Nigeria
detail.abstract: Accurate modelling of Land Use/Land Cover Change (LULCC) is essential for assessing the impacts of climate change, land degradation, and population growth, as well as for guiding natural resource management and sustainable urban planning. However, existing models often produce heterogeneous results with varying levels of reliability. This study compares the performance of Cellular Automata Markov (CA-Markov) and Cellular Automata Artificial Neural Network (CA-ANN) models in simulating future LULC dynamics in southwestern Nigeria. Using remotely sensed data and Geographic Information System (GIS) techniques, LULC maps were generated and analysed and generated for years 2002, 2012 and 2022, and projections were generated for 2032. The results revealed marked discrepancies between model outputs and the observed 2022 classification, particularly for Built-Up Areas, Wetlands, Vegetation, Water Bodies, and Open Surfaces. CA-Markov projected substantial expansion of Built-Up Areas, whereas CA-ANN predicted a decline. Similarly, CA-ANN indicated an increase in wetlands, contrary to the contraction forecasted by CA-Markov. These inconsistencies underscore the methodological differences between the models and the importance of critically evaluating both predictive accuracy and practical implications. The study recommends refining CA-ANN parameterisation, incorporating socio-economic drivers, enhancing ground-truth data collection, and fostering interdisciplinary collaboration. Such improvements would strengthen the reliability and applicability of LULC models, supporting evidence-based decision-making for urban planning and sustainable development.

title: Fate of Nitrogen in Rainfed Maize (Zea mays) Systems of the Tropical Highlands of Kenya Under Increasing Nitrogen Fertiliser Application Rates
affiliations: University of Eldoret, University of Eldoret, University of Eldoret, University of Eldoret, , , , ETH Zürich, , CGIAR - International Livestock Research Institute (ILRI), ,  and

detail.title: Fate of Nitrogen in Rainfed Maize (Zea mays) Systems of the Tropical Highlands of Kenya Under Increasing Nitrogen Fertiliser Application Rates
detail.abstract: Nitrogen is one of the most limiting nutrients in sub-Saharan Africa's agro systems, resulting in low crop yields and thus requiring intensified application. However, increased N fertiliser use is associated with elevated reactive nitrogen loading in the environment, resulting in leaching, eutrophication, and N2O emissions. Therefore, a 329-day study was conducted in the Kenyan highlands under a maize cropping system to assess the effect of increased nitrogen rates (0-125 kg ha-1) on the environment. Data on soil mineral N (Nmin) concentration at three depths (0-20, 20-40 and 40-60 cm), N2O fluxes and relevant nitrogen use efficiency (NUE) indices were collected. Time-weighted Nmin increased with rising N rates at 0-20 and 20-40 cm depths, with the highest intensity observed at 125 kg N ha-1 (28.9 mg d kg-1). Annual N2O fluxes measured from plots receiving 50 and 100 kg N ha-1 were 210 and 400 g N2O-N ha-1, respectively. Rainfall-induced soil moisture variations were found to directly and indirectly influence Nmin availability and movement down the soil profile. The NUEgrain reduced with increased N rates (1.20 to 0.37), while grain yield and N uptake increased by 7% to 46% and 7% to 67%, respectively. However, the optimal NUE (0.50) and PNB (0.96) were achieved at 75 kg ha-1, indicating that applying N at this rate would optimise N use and balance the trade-off between uptake and N losses.
