detail.abstract: The World Health Organization (WHO) occupies a central position in international health law as the coordinating authority for global public health. Yet, the legal basis and binding force of its pandemic declarations remain ambiguous. This article examines the WHO's legal mandate under the International Health Regulations (IHR 2005), focusing on Article 12 and the procedure for determining a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC). It argues that, while the IHR establish a binding framework for the notification and assessment of global health threats, the later "pandemic" characterisation has no autonomous legal effect. The resulting gap between soft-law guidance and enforceable obligations undermines accountability and highlights the structural tension between state sovereignty and collective responsibility. The article concludes that future treaty reform-especially the forthcoming pandemic instrument under Article 19 of the WHO Constitution-should codify clearer triggers, transparency duties, and compliance mechanisms to strengthen global health governance.

detail.abstract: We examine whether rising stock market concentration affects investment fund behavior and asset prices. Regulatory limits on portfolio concentration have become increasingly binding for U.S. funds, especially large-cap growth funds. As they approach or breach these limits, funds trim their largest holdings and reduce overall equity exposure. Funds tend to perform worse when constrained. A constraint-based ownership measure helps predict individual stock returns, particularly among the largest firms. An investment strategy exploiting this predictability earns abnormal returns. These findings suggest that high stock market concentration can distort stock prices by limiting the ability of optimistic investors to scale their positions.

title: Christian Faith as a Psychological Resource: An Integrative Model Combining Religious Meaning Making and Stoic Stress Regulation

detail.title: Christian Faith as a Psychological Resource: An Integrative Model Combining Religious Meaning Making and Stoic Stress Regulation
detail.abstract: Christian faith is increasingly conceptualized in psychology as a multidimensional resource that strengthens cognitive appraisal, emotional regulation, and coping processes. This article analyses Christian faith as a structured belief system that influences perception, motivation, and resilience. Drawing on empirical research on religious coping, meaning making, and self-transcendence, the paper examines how Christian convictions contribute to psychological stability in stressful contexts. The analysis integrates Paulini’s Stoic Stress Model to highlight the theoretical intersections between religious meaning construction and philosophical emotion regulation. The goal is to offer a scientifically grounded understanding of the psychological mechanisms activated by Christian faith in challenging life situations.

title: Steering Frontier Artificial Intelligence: Venture Capital, Governance Incentives, and the Innovation Trajectory of Advanced AI
affiliations: University of San Francisco, University of San Francisco

detail.title: Steering Frontier Artificial Intelligence: Venture Capital, Governance Incentives, and the Innovation Trajectory of Advanced AI
detail.abstract: Advances in frontier artificial intelligence are increasingly driven by large-scale models with broad generalization capabilities, raising governance challenges with systemic economic and societal implications (Bostrom, 2014; Russell, 2019; Weidinger et al., 2021). While prior research has emphasized technical alignment and regulatory approaches (Amodei et al., 2016; Floridi and Cowls, 2019; NIST, 2023), the role of venture capital (VC) in shaping the innovation trajectory of advanced AI remains underexamined (Dafoe, 2018; OECD, 2023). This paper develops a conceptual framework integrating AI governance, innovation economics, and labor market research to examine how capital allocation influences organizational incentives, safety investment, and deployment behavior in frontier AI systems.  We identify four archetypal VC positioning strategies—Accelerator, Guardian, Neutral Capital Provider, and Bridge Builder—and analyze their implications for governance quality, competitive dynamics, and long-horizon risk (Gompers and Lerner, 2004; Kortum and Lerner, 2000). Comparative synthesis across leading AI organizations, complemented by evidence from global industry and workforce surveys, reveals substantial heterogeneity in governance structures driven by financial and institutional design rather than technical architecture alone (Kaplan et al., 2020; Stanford HAI, 2024; World Economic Forum, 2023).  The analysis suggests that conventional venture capital models optimized for rapid scaling are increasingly misaligned with the governance requirements of advanced AI, while long-horizon investment structures may reduce systemic risk while sustaining innovation (Mazzucato, 2018; UNESCO, 2022).

detail.abstract: This study evaluates the impact of behavioural interventions on the uptake and payment of tax arrears through an amnesty program in Kenya. Using a randomised controlled trial, 43,666 tax delinquents from Nairobi region were evaluated. Taxpayers were assigned to receive either a neutral informational email, one of three behavioural messages on deterrence, social norms, payment plans, or no message at all. The experiment was conducted over three treatment rounds between December 2023 and May 2024, allowing for the analysis of both immediate effects and sequencing dynamics. Non respondents were re-randomised across message types in the final round. Results show that all message treatments significantly increased amnesty uptake relative to no communication. Additionally, deterrence messages were more effective than social norms or payment plan reminders. Changing message framing in the third round enhanced participation among late responders but was associated with smaller payments relative to early takers. Overall, the findings suggest that while behavioural messages can promote engagement, informational communication may be equally effective in improving compliance. The study contributes to the literature by highlighting the effectiveness of behavioural intervention in an amnesty context and illustrates the importance of message sequencing in sustaining taxpayer attention.

detail.title: Bequest Division: The Roles of Parental Motives and Children’s Gender Composition

publicationDetails.journalName: National Bank of Belgium Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Drawing on two data sources from across Europe, we show that both bequest motives of parents and children’s gender composition shape unequal divisions of bequests. First, the Survey on Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe reveals that observed bequests are divided unequally when children differ in sex, caregiving, or income, with bequest motives strongest among mixed-sex children. Second, in a vignette experiment featuring alternative bequest motive scenarios and randomised gender compositions for two fictitious children, hypothetical bequests are most unequally divided under the exchange motive while children’s gender composition matters more under the altruistic motive. Fictitious parents favour daughters regardless of deservingness, granting the highest bequest share to a deserving daughter with a brother. In return, these patterns reinforce traditional gender norms.

title: Faith and Inner Governance: Integrating Christian and Stoic Virtue Ethics for Resilient Leadership in the Digital Age

detail.title: Faith and Inner Governance: Integrating Christian and Stoic Virtue Ethics for Resilient Leadership in the Digital Age
detail.abstract: This paper develops an integrated theoretical model that combines Christian virtue ethics and Stoic philosophy to strengthen inner governance as a foundation for resilient leadership in contemporary organizations. Drawing on research in moral psychology, spirituality studies and organizational behavior, the article demonstrates that both traditions converge on key mechanisms of meaning-making, emotional regulation, moral responsibility and disciplined self-leadership. The model introduced here, termed Virtue-Centered Inner Governance, conceptualizes leadership as a character-based process grounded in transcendent meaning orientation on the one hand and rational emotional regulation on the other. Four core competencies emerge from this synthesis: meaning competence, control competence, ethical competence and emotional competence. The paper outlines practical implications for decision-making, crisis management and ethical leadership behavior, and discusses opportunities and limitations of the model in diverse organizational contexts. The findings suggest that integrating philosophical and spiritual resources can enhance leadership resilience, moral clarity and sustainable authority in increasingly complex environments.

detail.abstract: The firm sector continuously engages in the reallocation of physical capital. We study the implications for credit market outcomes of banks' engagement in borrowing firms' capital reallocation. We develop a model in which banks' experience with the reallocation opportunities of physical capital raises their ability to recover liquidation values after firm defaults and asset reallocations, diluting banks' incentives to monitor borrowers. To test the model, we then construct an empirical measure of banks' engagement in capital reallocation using US loan-level data matched with firm-level data on capital asset transactions. We find that, unlike lending relationships and experience with co-lenders, capital allocation engagement dilutes banks' monitoring incentives, calling for larger involvement in loan syndication.

detail.abstract: I evaluate the link between automation and the rise in top income concentration when inequality matters for macro. The novel mechanism is that automation redistributes income towards high-wealth households who save more, which lowers the interest rate and incites firms to automate more. To operationalize this, I build a tractable heterogeneous-agent model (1) with wealth in the utility function as a luxury good, and (2) a firm-side choice on automation. I find that introducing realistic savings rate heterogeneity largely eliminates the need for ad hoc technology shifts. Rather, automation is the outcome of increased top income concentration, not just its driver.

title: AI for Incentive-Compatible Insurance Design: Learning Optimal Indemnity with Lipschitz Networks
affiliations: Central University of Finance and Economics (CUFE),  and Nanyang Business School, Nanyang Technological University

detail.title: AI for Incentive-Compatible Insurance Design: Learning Optimal Indemnity with Lipschitz Networks
detail.abstract: Many optimal insurance design problems with the incentive-compatible (IC) condition lack closed-form solutions and efficient numerical methods. This paper proposes a novel algorithm to obtain numerical  solutions of optimal insurance by parameterizing the indemnity function using a Lipschitz Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) architecture. To incorporate the principle of indemnity and  the IC condition, we introduce constrained affine transformation layers and a special activation function while preserving the MLP’s universal approximation. We provide a theoretical justification for the proposed architecture and develop a gradient-based algorithm that efficiently approximates optimal indemnity functions with very high accuracy. We validate the algorithm’s accuracy against classical benchmarks with known analytical solutions, and demonstrate its applicability to several economically important yet previously intractable settings including optimal insurance with a dependent background risk, loss ambiguity, or rank-dependent utility. A case study on Florida hurricane insurance further illustrates how derived optimal contracts can mitigate the crowding-out effect of government relief to enhance welfare.

detail.abstract: Many states have capped consumer loan interest rates to protect households from high-cost lenders. Using triple-difference and event study analysis, we investigate how these usury limits affect the availability and allocation of credit across households. Consistent with standard price theory, we find that credit to the riskiest borrowers contracts under usury limits without improving delinquencies. More surprisingly, credit to lower risk borrowers expands under usury limits. This reallocation suggests that usury limits have unintended effects that are not entirely explained by standard theory.

title: The Wealth of Civilization: A General Theory of Capital, Welfare and the Economics of Time
affiliations: America First Policy Institute (AFPI)

detail.title: The Wealth of Civilization: A General Theory of Capital, Welfare and the Economics of Time
detail.abstract:
The Wealth of Civilization offers a rethinking of modern economics through the lens it has most persistently mishandled: time. Drawing on insights from neoclassical, Austrian, Keynesian, and welfare economics, this book develops a unified framework for understanding value, cost, capital, and policy in a world that unfolds dynamically rather than instantaneously.

At its core is a simple but radical claim. Long-run prosperity is governed not by static efficiency or momentary equilibrium, but by the accumulation and stewardship of capital across generations. Markets excel at allocating resources in the present, yet systematically underinvest in the future. This intertemporal gap—driven by time preference, missing markets, and mismeasured opportunity costs—constitutes the most consequential market failure of all.

The book revisits foundational concepts that economists often treat as settled, including opportunity cost, surplus, discounting, externalities, and social welfare. It argues that costs are objective but dynamic, that surplus is heterogeneous and intertemporal, and that welfare cannot be understood without explicit attention to investment, compounding, and bequests. Building on these insights, it reframes cost-benefit analysis, critiques conventional approaches to inflation adjustment and value-of-life estimation, and shows why static reasoning obscures the forces that shape civilization’s long-run trajectory.

The result is neither a defense of laissez-faire nor an apology for central planning. Instead, The Wealth of Civilization advances a pragmatic vision in which markets remain indispensable, but properly designed public institutions play an indispensable role as custodians of intergenerational welfare. Written for economists, policymakers, and intellectually curious readers alike, the book avoids technical formalism in favor of conceptual clarity, offering a general theory suited to the economic challenges of the twenty-first century.

title: SOFR so Good: Transaction Costs and Resilience in the Post-Libor Swap Market
affiliations: and Copenhagen Business School

detail.title: SOFR so Good: Transaction Costs and Resilience in the Post-Libor Swap Market
detail.abstract: Using novel transaction and quote data, we find that transaction costs in the SOFR swap market are low on average, but somewhat higher for dealer-to-client than interdealer trades partly reflecting differences in (permanent) price impact. Costs vary systematically with trade characteristics and market conditions, but this does not explain cost differences across market segments. Average swap execution costs are moderately higher than the minimum cost of trading on-the-run Treasuries on the main limit-order book, yet a substantial share of swap trades achieve cheaper execution. During recent crises, both transaction costs and trading activity increase sharply, providing a mixed picture of market resilience. However, based on comparable measures of volatility, trading activity, and liquidity stress, we conclude that the swap market appears more resilient than the Treasury market.

detail.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is a threat to democratic norms. Machine learning bots have been used by malign forces to disrupt democratic processes. The literature as a result is replete with warnings! The goal of this project is to turn the threat that AI poses on its head: to use AI to advance democratic norms. This is not about the efficiency benefits that AI will produce, often lauded in contradistinction to AI’s problems. There are very important values that can be fostered by AI. To improve democratic participation and render the tax system more legitimate in the UK, this report makes 5 recommendations for the use of AI in the tax system.

title: Energy supply chain resilience under geopolitical disruption: Assessing global and Red Sea oil tanker networks
affiliations: Shanghai Maritime University, ,  and

detail.title: Energy supply chain resilience under geopolitical disruption: Assessing global and Red Sea oil tanker networks
detail.abstract: The Red Sea crisis exemplifies how regional geopolitical disruptions propagate through energy seaborne transportation system. This study develops an integrated dual-indicator framework to assess resilience of the global oil tanker network and its Red Sea subnetwork during this ongoing crisis. The static resilience index conducts targeted attack-recovery simulations across five strategies. Dynamically, we monitor resilience index using monthly network data, employing Granger causality tests to identify transmission mechanisms from shocks. Results reveal four key findings:First, the Red Sea's ports are characterized by dense concentration in the north and sparse distribution in the south. Although the conflict has continued for a considerable period,  two networks have not yet recovered to its pre-crisis level. Second, the impact of subnetwork on the global network reflects a typical “early-intensified and later-attenuated” pattern. Furthermore, oil tanker transportation systems are highly dependent on bottleneck corridors and key ports of cross-regional traffic flows. Third, exogenous shocks influence network resilience primarily through oil price fluctuations and operational adjustments. Endogenous factors affect two networks in distinct ways. Granger causality tests further reveal a bidirectional feedback relationship between the global system and the Red Sea subnetwork. Fourth, critical infrastructure analysis indicates that the north-south channels of the Red Sea plays a dominant role in the oil transportation system, whereas ports located in the central Red Sea play a comparatively minor role. These findings advance maritime resilience theory by operationalizing hierarchical network relationships and provide actionable strategies for enhancing energy supply chain stability under geopolitical uncertainty.

title: If the utility function is unbounded, any finite utility assignment to the St Petersburg game is consistent with expected utility theory
affiliations: University of Edinburgh - Usher Institute

detail.title: If the utility function is unbounded, any finite utility assignment to the St Petersburg game is consistent with expected utility theory
detail.abstract: The von Neumann Morgenstern theorem gives necessary and sufficient conditions for a binary relation on a convex subset of probability measures to be represented by a linear functional on the vector space of signed measures. Unbounded utility functions do not provide enough data to determine the representing functional. This requires specifying utility values on a Hamel basis of the vector space of signed measures, which may be non-constructive. Extending by continuity and truncation continuity can enlarge the domain where the expected utility representation is valid, but not to probability measures that have undefined expected utility. Utility values can thus be freely assigned to any linearly independent set of probability measures whose expected utility is not defined. In particular, any finite utility value assignment to the St Petersburg, Pasadena and related games is consistent with expected utility theory.

title: An Analysis of Interim Resolution Professional; Issues and Challenges

detail.title: An Analysis of Interim Resolution Professional; Issues and Challenges

keywords: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI)

detail.abstract: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (IBC) revolutionized India’s insolvency regime by introducing a time-bound, creditor-centric resolution framework. At the heart of this process lies the Interim Resolution Professional (IRP), entrusted with the responsibility of managing the corporate debtor’s affairs from the initiation of the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) until the appointment of the Resolution Professional (RP). This paper critically examines the evolving role, powers, and challenges faced by IRPs between 2016 and 2025, against the backdrop of legislative, judicial, and regulatory developments. It explores key amendments enhancing IRP independence through panel-based appointments, stricter disclosures, and quasi-judicial powers; judicial interpretations clarifying their autonomy, liability, and fiduciary duties; and regulatory reforms by the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) focusing on standardization of fees, conflict-of-interest management, and enhanced accountability. The study also highlights technological interventions such as e-filing, Information Utilities, and centralized auction platforms reshaping insolvency practice. Despite these progressive reforms, IRPs continue to encounter operational hurdles including promoter non-cooperation, delayed remuneration, and overlapping liabilities. The paper concludes by proposing recommendations for strengthening institutional support, digital integration, and statutory protections to ensure efficient, transparent, and equitable insolvency resolution aligned with global best practices.

detail.abstract: This study aims to analyze the governance and accountability challenges faced by Regional-Owned Enterprises (BUMD) as the Project Responsible Party (PJPK) in public-private partnership infrastructure projects, with a case study on the Bandar Lampung Drinking Water Supply System (SPAM). Sustainable and adequate drinking water services are fundamental to human well-being and are integral to achieving Sustainable Development Goal 6 (SDG 6). In Indonesia, the Government-Business Partnership (KPBU) scheme has been implemented to overcome budgetary constraints and expand service coverage. However, the SPAM Bandar Lampung project has faced issues related to transparency, internal control, and risk allocation between the government and BUMD/PJPK. This study employs a qualitative approach using document analysis, academic literature, and project reports as primary data sources. The findings indicate that the success of KPBU implementation depends heavily on clear governance structures, strong accountability mechanisms, and effective coordination among stakeholders. Additionally, the institutional capacity of BUMD as PJPK, the culture of accountability, and external oversight are critical factors in preventing mismanagement and ensuring service sustainability. This research contributes theoretically to the literature on public-private partnerships and public sector governance while providing practical implications for policy strengthening, transparency, and project management in regional water infrastructure initiatives.

title: In Search of the Causal Greenium
affiliations: WU Vienna University of Economics and Business,  and Reykjavik University

detail.title: In Search of the Causal Greenium
detail.abstract: We propose a regression discontinuity design to determine whether there is a difference in the expected returns of green versus brown securities (greenium). We analyze daily changes in option-implied expected returns following the outcome of close vote ecology-related shareholder proposals to estimate the causal impact of a small change in investors' aggregate greenness perception on expected returns. Upon proposals' passage, expected returns with a forecast horizon of 365 (730) days drop by approximately 7.2% (9.6%) relative to proposals' failure, indicating the existence of a negative greenium in US equity markets. We introduce a battery of fixed effects, account for multiple periods around shareholder proposal voting dates, and remove confounding governance and social proposals, and find that our results are robust in these specifications.

detail.title: The Role of Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs) in Financing the Probolinggo-Banyuwangi Toll Road Development: A Perspective on Efficiency and Sustainability
detail.abstract: This study aims to analyze the role of Public Private Partnership (PPP) in financing the construction of the Probolinggo-Banyuwangi Toll Road from the perspectives of efficiency and sustainability. The research employs a descriptive qualitative method using a literature study approach, focusing on an in-depth analysis of previous studies, government policies, and official documents related to PPP implementation in toll road infrastructure projects. The findings indicate that the application of PPP in the Probolinggo-Banyuwangi Toll Road project significantly contributes to financing efficiency through proportional risk-sharing between the government and the private sector, while also accelerating project completion without heavily burdening the state budget. From the sustainability perspective, the project demonstrates positive impacts on regional economic growth and connectivity improvement, although challenges remain in addressing social and environmental issues. The study concludes that PPP serves as a strategic instrument for supporting sustainable infrastructure financing in Indonesia, but its effectiveness depends on transparent governance, strong regulatory oversight, and the integration of sustainability principles throughout the planning and implementation stages.

detail.title: Fiscal Spending News, the Cost of Capital, and Corporate Investment
detail.abstract: We revisit the effect of government spending on corporate investment. Employing a narrative approach to identify exogenous variation in government expenditures (Ramey, 2011b; Ramey and Zubairy, 2018), we find that a one-percentage-point increase in military spending news, as a share of GDP, raises capital expenditures of publicly listed US firms by more than one percent over five years. The investment response is not driven by contractors with the Department of Defense, financial constraints, unconventional monetary policy, or geopolitical and economic uncertainty. Instead, we show that news about military spending lowers longterm nominal and ex-ante real interest rates on impact, with effects persisting for up to five years after the shock. Lower interest rates critically translate into a decline in the firm-level cost of capital, particularly the cost of debt. Consistent with the decline in the cost of capital, firms expand debt holdings and investment.

detail.abstract: This study investigates the impact of foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows on economic performance in Nigeria, utilizing the autoregressive distributed lag (ARDL) model and estimation technique. The study employed secondary data collected over the period 1980 to 2023, sourced from the World Development Indicators (WDI). The results indicate that FDI inflows have both short-term and long-term effects on Nigeria's economic performance. The analysis revealed a positive and statistically significant relationship between FDI inflows and economic performance, as proxied by gross domestic product per capita (GDP per capita). Hence, this research highlights the importance of FDI inflows in stimulating the economic performance of the Nigerian economy and recommends that the government and policymakers should undertake policy reforms that prioritize investment in critical infrastructure, such as transportation, energy, and communication (to improve mobile network coverage) to create an enabling environment for FDI-driven industries, and identify and promote key sectors with high growth potential.

detail.title: National Culture and Bank Branching
detail.abstract: We investigate why commercial bank branch presence diverges across countries with a global panel. We show that beyond traditional determinants, national culture, particularly individualism, plays a pivotal role in shaping bank branching. Individualistic countries exhibit higher generalized trust and stronger preferences for digital channels, reducing reliance on physical branches. Moreover, banks operating in individualistic environments tend to be more technologically sensitive and rely on standardized contracts, in contrast to collectivism that depends more on in-person interactions in physical branches. Finally, banks in individualistic countries display greater resilience during the COVID-19 crisis.

title: An Empirical Analysis of Microeconomic Variabvles and Economic Growth in Nigeria (1981-2023)

detail.title: An Empirical Analysis of Microeconomic Variabvles and Economic Growth in Nigeria (1981-2023)
detail.abstract: Economic growth is the most powerful tool a country can use to reduce poverty and improve quality of life. This study investigates the Empirical Analysis of Microeconomic Variables and Economic Growth in Nigeria using Auto Regression Distribution Lag (ARDL). Data was sourced from CBN Statistical bulletin from 1981 to 2023. The findings reveal that in the shot run; the balance of trade has mixed effects on economic growth, with initial deficits hindering GDP while subsequent improvements contribute positively. Exchange rate depreciation, inflation and unemployment exhibit negative but statistically insignificant effects on GDP in the short run. In the long run, a persistent trade deficit significantly hampers economic growth, while exchange rate depreciation and inflation continue to show negative but statistically insignificant impacts. Notably, unemployment displays a positive relationship with GDP, suggesting structural labour market dynamics, such as shifts towards informal or capital-intensive employment, may influence economic performance. The presence o a highly significant error correction term indicates that about 41% of deviations from the long-run GDP equilibrium are connected each period, reflecting the economy's gradual adjustment mechanism. Based on these findings, the study recommends policies aimed at improving Nigeria's trade balance through export diversification, ensuring exchange rate stability, addressing inflation through coordinated monetary policies, and implementing structural labour market reforms. Furthermore, enhancing economic flexibility and long-term planning is crucial for fostering sustainable economic growth.

detail.abstract: Despite significant global progress in expanding access to quality healthcare, Nigeria’s advancement has remained relatively slow. Previous studies have focused largely on one or a few dimensions of healthcare access, while evidence reflecting its multidimensional nature remains limited. This study evaluated access to healthcare and its determinants among rural households in Nigeria using cross-sectional data from 624 households. A 10-item measurement instrument was employed to assess access based on the psychological experiences of households. Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) was used to test the validity and reliability of the instrument, while descriptive statistics, bar charts, Lorenz curves, Gini coefficient, and Instrumental Variable (IV) ordered probit and linear models were applied for data analysis. Two items were removed due to non-convergence and high residual correlation, resulting in an 8-item scale with acceptable reliability (Cronbach’s α = 0.70).Overall, 88.1% of rural households were at risk of inadequate healthcare access. Factors that significantly increased access included monthly per capita expenditure (β = 0.169; p < 0.001), household size (β = 0.086; p < 0.1), residence in the northern region (β = 0.081; p < 0.1), facility operating hours (β = 0.015; p < 0.001), and perceived service quality (β = 0.110; p < 0.01). Conversely, secondary education (β = -0.074; p < 0.001) and waiting time (β = -0.056; p < 0.001) reduced access. Strengthening informal health insurance schemes is recommended to improve coverage and equitable access.

detail.abstract: This study discusses the use of a cooperation model between the government and the private sector, known as Public Private Partnership, with the Design-Build-Finance-Operate-Maintain (DBFOM) approach in the Palapa Ring project, a digital infrastructure development project in Indonesia. This project aims to expand internet access to remote areas by building a fiber optic network spanning more than 35,000 km. The PPP model was chosen because the government faced budget constraints and needed large funds to build digital infrastructure. The DBFOM approach is important because it involves the private sector in the entire project process, from designing, building, managing funds, operating, and maintaining it. This study uses a qualitative descriptive method by collecting data from various official sources such as the Ministry of Communication and Information Technology, the National Development Planning Agency (Bappenas), national media reports, and the latest scientific publications. The results of the study show that the application of DBFOM in the Palapa Ring project improves efficiency, transparency, and accountability in the provision of public services. The partnership between the government and the private sector divides risks evenly, with the private sector bearing technical and financial risks, while the government provides regulatory support and ensures that the project runs smoothly. Of the three parts of the Palapa Ring project, namely West, Central, and East, the DBFOM model is most suitable for the Eastern part due to more complex geographical challenges and greater investment needs. The study also found that the successful implementation of PPPs with the DBFOM approach depends on good contract management, transparency in financial reporting, and consistent government support for national digital infrastructure policies. The recommendations emphasize the importance of enhancing cooperation between government agencies and the private sector, implementing independent oversight mechanisms to maintain accountability, and improve the capacity of institutions to manage national-scale PPP projects. With the DBFOM model, Indonesia has a great opportunity to develop other digital infrastructure projects such as telecommunications towers and 5G networks in the future.

detail.abstract: Youth unemployment remains a persistent challenge in Bangladesh, despite the country's consistent economic growth over the past two decades. This study examines the impact of public education expenditure and tertiary enrollment on youth unemployment, using annual time-series data from 1995 to 2023 within an Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) model. The model, estimated in both its long-and short-run forms, verifies cointegration through the bounds testing approach and captures short-run adjustments via an error correction mechanism. The study finds that in the long run, 1% rise in tertiary enrollment and public education spending reduces youth unemployment by 0.0415% and 0.4886%, respectively, while GDP growth remains insignificant, reflecting a "jobless growth" pattern. In the short run, education spending lowers unemployment with both immediate and lagged effects, whereas tertiary enrollment initially increases it, likely due to delayed graduate absorption. These findings underscore that investment in education expansion effectively mitigates youth joblessness, whereas economic growth alone fails to generate sufficient employment. From a policy perspective, emphasis should shift toward improving education quality, aligning curricula with labour market needs, and fostering industry-academia partnerships. Expanding vocational and technical training, promoting practical skill development, and integrating job-matching mechanisms would ensure that educational progress translates into sustainable employment and inclusive economic growth.

Recognizing that electrification programs need to expand access by incorporating demand-side investments and policies, this study establishes a baseline for better integrating EPUE in business settings. Drawing insights from three participatory surveys conducted in Uganda with women business owners, electric equipment vendors, and representatives of financial institutions, this paper provides an overview of the current and potential state of EPUE adoption in womenled businesses. It describes the current state of EPUE uptake, the types of electric equipment currently being used, and the financial and non-financial barriers to using electricity to develop and grow those businesses. Findings underscore the need for capacity building in both EPUE and business skills adoption, as well as a shift in attitudes towards electric equipment and financing models. The paper concludes by emphasizing the importance of expanding tailored energy access programs to encompass women-centric demand-side strategies, particularly within the enterprise sector.

detail.abstract: Startups are critical engines of innovation but face high uncertainty and mortality. Existing life cycle models offer limited guidance because they define evolving stages inconsistently and often overlook non-linear trajectories. The aim of this research was to (i) systematically review the startup life cycle literature and (ii) propose and validate an integrative framework for the startup life cycle. This framework clarifies stage boundaries, acknowledges pivots and premature scaling, and enables startup development diagnosis and guidance. The methodological procedures embraced a systematic analysis with 54 studies, interviews with 20 entrepreneurs and the participation of validation process that involved 20 innovation specialists. The framework was later applied to assess more than 1,300 startups in a public policy initiative in Brazil. This study contributes theoretically by integrating fragmented approaches into a coherent structure and offering a basis for comparing studies on startup evolution. It also allows examining edge cases such as multi-product ventures and atypical growth paths. From a practical perspective, it helps entrepreneurs allocate resources more effectively, enables accelerators to tailor mentoring and support, and assists policymakers in designing stage-specific interventions. By bridging academic rigor with actionable insights, this research advances knowledge on startup development while improving decision-making in entrepreneurial ecosystems.

detail.abstract: This research aims to analyze the concept of human existence in Modern Arab Theater by checking some dramatic functions that deal with the subjects of existence and non-liking in different social and cultural contexts. Research examines the most prominent philosophical topics related to human existence, such as contradictions between individual and society, a sense of isolation, and the damage of modern people in a world dominated by stress and uncertainty. The dramatic methods used to express these ideas by authors are also analyzed through dialogue, dramatic structure, and character design. Research depends on analyzing dramatic texts using philosophical equipment to read the dimensions of the existence of these functions, which reveal the effect of existentialism and non-equation in presenting psychological and intellectual challenges that individuals face. Through this analysis, the research wants to provide a deep understanding of how the theater can be a platform for detecting existential problems, while modern Arabs reveal the social and cultural references that shape human experience in the Arab Theater.

detail.title: AI-Driven Crypto Finance: Market Integrity, AML/CFT Risks, and Policy Priorities for Emerging Economies
detail.abstract: The rapid diffusion of artificial intelligence (AI) and cryptoassets is transforming how value is created, transferred, and concealed across borders. AI is now embedded across the crypto lifecycle: in high-frequency algorithmic trading, market-making and arbitrage; in automated DeFi protocols and autonomous agents; and in the RegTech-SupTech tools that monitor blockchains and enforce sanctions and anti-money-laundering (AML) rules. At the same time, the same technologies are lowering the cost of market manipulation, fraud, sanctions evasion, and sophisticated money laundering. Building on recent work by the BIS, IMF, FATF and IOSCO on AI in finance and crypto supervision, this paper develops an integrated framework for understanding how AI reshapes market-integrity and AML/CFT risks in crypto markets, with a particular focus on emerging economies. It argues that the net impact of AI will be determined less by technology itself and more by policy choices: data access for supervisors, investment in human capital, governance of AI models, and cross-border coordination. The paper concludes with a practical policy agenda for emerging-market authorities seeking to harness AI for safer innovation while containing its amplifying effects on financial crime and systemic risk.

detail.abstract: We describe cross dominance - a bilateral strengthening of weak dominance: switching B → A is never worse for either player. Cross dominance is strictly stronger than weak dominance yet orthogonal to strict dominance; within the Pareto-monotone slice we have SD ⇒ CD ⇒ WD. This yields a shared-interest ladder (weak → cross → strict-cross) that runs in parallel to the classical self-interest ladder (weak → strict), offering a simple, outcome-agnostic rationale for pruning strategies like B in the motivating 2 × 2 game presented.

detail.abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive historical account of Bohemia from 1085 to 1526, tracing its transformation from a medieval duchy into a culturally distinct and politically influential kingdom within Central Europe. It examines the region’s political evolution under the Přemyslid, Luxembourg, and Jagiellonian dynasties, the development of Czech cultural identity through language, literature, and religious expression, and Bohemia’s impact on regional diplomacy, imperial politics, and cross-border relations. The study highlights how Bohemia balanced domestic autonomy with involvement in wider European affairs, demonstrating resilience through dynastic change, foreign pressures, and internal transformation. Presented in a clear narrative format without in-text citations, the paper offers an accessible yet rigorous overview intended to support further study and comparative research in medieval and early modern Central European history.

detail.title: Enhancing GDP and Inflation Measurement via SRDB Methodology
detail.abstract: This self-contained article presents comprehensive empirical validation of applying Pytel's SRDB (Systemic Risk of Doing Business) methodology to improve GDP and inflation measurement. Using 3,520+ quarterly observations across 15 countries (1960-2025), we demonstrate: (1) SRDB-Augmented GDP Nowcasting (SRG) achieves 27.9% RMSE improvement over AR(1) baseline for 1-quarter forecasts, with 89.3% improvement during financial crises. (2) SRDB-Augmented Inflation (SRI) reduces measurement error 25.4%, combines real-time financial market data with official CPI to eliminate publication lag. (3) Financial risk premiums predict GDP revisions 1-3 quarters in advance (R² = 0.42, all predictors p<0.01). (4) Time-varying weights based on economic cycle phases improve SRG performance additional 5.8%. (5) Development-stage adjustments improve emerging market measurement accuracy 15-20%. (6)-convergence and-convergence tests confirm global weight structure stabilization (55.6% dispersion reduction 1970-2010s). All results statistically significant at p<0.01 or better; robust to structural breaks, subsamples, and alternative specifications. Key Empirical Contributions: (1) First comprehensive validation of financial indicators predicting GDP revisions across 15-country panel (Coefficient:-0.34pp per 100bp spread, t=-4.3, p<0.0001). (2) Documented measurement error decomposition in CPI (substitution bias 0.22pp, hedonic uncertainty 0.15pp, new goods 0.18pp, outlet substitution 0.25pp, sampling error 0.05pp). (3) Demonstrated cycle-dependent weight adjustment mechanism improving nowcasting 5.8% beyond fixed weights. (4) International comparability validated via convergence tests (all components converge to common structure, half-lives 22-38 years). (5) Crisis forecasting superiority established: average 89.3% RMSE reduction during 2008 GFC, 2020 COVID, 2021-23 inflation surge. Operationalization: SRI publishable within T+1 business day (vs T+15 for CPI); SRG nowcast available T+5 (vs T+31 GDP advance estimate). Central banks can implement with existing market data feeds; no new data collection required. Statistical agencies recommended to publish SRI/SRG as official supplementary indicators alongside CPI/GDP.

detail.abstract: Despite decades of progress in photorealistic graphics, the "uncanny valley" remains a primary obstacle to the creation of believable digital humans. We posit that this problem is rooted not in a lack of visual fidelity, but in a lack of behavioral authenticity the cognitive dissonance that arises from a mismatch between an avatar's appearance and its lifeless behavior. This paper introduces a novel synthesis pipeline for photorealistic avatars that addresses this challenge. Our approach drives real-time facial animation not only from an audio stream for lip-syncing but from a stream of emotional metadata generated by a deep, multi-modal personality model. We present the complete pipeline, which includes the creation of a personalized, AI-driven rig that captures a user's unique micro-expressions and a mechanism for the perfect synchronization of vocal prosody, facial expressions, and articulation. We argue that this deep behavioral coherence, rather than graphical fidelity alone, is the key to crossing the uncanny valley and creating truly "living" digital interlocutors. Our approach drives real-time facial animation not only from an audio stream for lip-syncing but from a stream of emotional metadata generated by a deep, multi-modal personality model. detail.abstract: This study evaluates the effectiveness of MiFID II’s mandatory elicitation of retail investors’ sustainability preferences in aligning investment advice with EU climate goals. Using comprehensive real-world data from 18,250 advisory meetings at a German savings bank, we analyze how clients’ ex-pressed ESG preferences influence advisory recommendations and actual investment behavior. Despite regulatory intent, the share of clients stating sustainability preferences declined significantly after mandatory implementation, and expressed preferences rarely translated into changed in-vestment decisions. Our findings reveal a gap between regulatory frame-works and client engagement, highlighting challenges in operationalizing sustainability preferences. We discuss these results alongside ESMA stake-holder feedback and propose practical improvements to enhance alignment and impact.

detail.abstract: This policy brief explores the potential consequences for Italian wholesale electricity prices if the 2024 NECP objectives for installed capacity of Variable Renewable Energy Sources (VRES) by 2030 are not met. Using the PLEXOS model, the analysis-based on hourly granularity-simulates EU electricity market dynamics under alternative scenarios of national goal attainment (-10%,-20%,-30%), incorporating sensitivities to gas and CO 2 price parameters. Results indicate that shortfalls in VRES deployment significantly increase Italy's reliance on gas, widening its price gap with other EU countries. Such underperformance also exacerbates internal market-splitting effects and reduces socioeconomic welfare gains. Moreover, meeting NECP objectives proves essential to minimize CO₂ emissions and gas offtake. Overall, the findings underscore the urgent need for policy and infrastructure investments to accelerate VRES deployment in Italy. Delays or setbacks in reaching these objectives would entail considerable economic and environmental costs, further distancing Italy from EU energy transition benchmarks.

title: Preserving Intangible Heritage: Using Personality Simulation to Create Dynamic, Interactive Archives of Cultural and Linguistic Knowledge

detail.abstract: Humanity's intangible cultural heritage, including languages, oral traditions, and crafts, is under constant threat of extinction as it exists only in the living memory of its practitioners. Traditional archival methods, such as audio and video recordings, preserve valuable but static, "dead" records incapable of the interactive transmission of "living" knowledge. This paper introduces a new paradigm to address this problem: the creation of "living archives" through personality simulation technology. We propose a methodology that allows for the modeling of not just a personality, but the unique cultural and linguistic knowledge of a specific tradition bearer be it the last speaker of a language or a master artisan. The result is a dynamic, interactive avatar with which future generations can engage in dialogue. This approach transforms archival science, shifting its focus from passive preservation to active transmission and revitalization. The paper details use cases such as language revitalization through conversational immersion and the concept of a "simulated apprenticeship" for the transmission of tacit craft knowledge. We also present an ethical framework, grounded in the principle of "community ownership," for the responsible implementation of such projects. The "living archive" is not merely a technological innovation, but a fundamental step toward enabling the most fragile treasures of human culture to continue to live and speak to future generations.

In order to compare the performance of each prediction method, the root mean square error (RMSE) and the mean absolute error (MAE) between the observed UV-B values and the predicted one were computed. Consequently, Informer shows the best highest prediction accuracy among all methods.

title: The Transformation of Broadband Demand: From Discretionary Service to Essential Infrastructure (2010-2024)
affiliations: ADA University, Charles University and Information Communication Technologies Agency of Azerbaijan

detail.title: The Transformation of Broadband Demand: From Discretionary Service to Essential Infrastructure (2010-2024)
detail.abstract: Has broadband become a necessity good immune to price changes? Using a 15-year panel of 33 European countries (2010-2024) and two-way fixed effects with Driscoll-Kraay standard errors, we document a fundamental transformation in broadband demand. Pre-COVID, Eastern Partnership countries exhibited highly elastic demand (ε =-0.61, p<0.001)-a 10% price reduction increased subscriptions by 6%—while EU countries showed moderate elasticity (ε = −0.12, p<0.05). By 2020–2024, both regions converged to near-zero elasticity, with price changes having no detectable effect on adoption. Crucially, placebo tests reveal this transformation began in 2015, not 2020, indicating a decade-long digital integration process rather than a COVID-19 shock. We further demonstrate that price measurement critically affects inference: income-relative prices (as % of GNI) yield significant results in 100% of specifications, compared to only 25% for PPP-adjusted prices. These findings have immediate policy relevance: as broadband transitions from discretionary service to essential utility, policy emphasis must shift from affordability subsidies to universal infrastructure deployment.

title: Corporate Greenness and Bond Yield Spreads
affiliations: Essex Business School, University of Essex, University of Essex and University of Sussex Business School

detail.title: Corporate Greenness and Bond Yield Spreads
detail.abstract: We examine the relationship between corporate greenness and the cross-section of corporate bond spreads. Using a comprehensive dataset of U.S. corporate bonds, we employ firms’ environmental scores as a proxy for greenness and find a negative cross-sectional association with bond spreads. This suggests that bonds issued by green firms are priced at a premium relative to those of brown firms. On average, greener firms exhibit greater profitability, lower leverage, and higher market-to-book ratios, among other characteristics. Exploring potential channels that can help explain our results, we find that green firms have lower cash flow uncertainty and lower default risk compared to brown firms. These findings offer valuable insights for academics, finance professionals, and policy makers.

title: Climate Change Resulting In Intense Floods in Sindh and the Impact on Population

detail.abstract: Climate change is a major global challenge, with significant impacts on natural systems and human communities around the world. Climate change and rising flood threats together provide new problems and concerns. (PRIEMUS & RIETVELD, 2009)1 One notable example is the increase in extreme weather events, including floods, which can have devastating consequences for communities and infrastructure. In Sindh, the second largest province of Pakistan, floods have had a particularly significant impact, with numerous reported instances of loss of life, damage to homes and businesses, and disruption to critical services in 2021 alone. Prior to this, the deadly flooding was witnessed in Sindh back in 2010 (Kazi, 2013)2. Given the significant impact of floods on the people and communities of Sindh recently, it is important to understand the factors contributing to these events and to identify potential strategies for mitigating their impact. To address this research question, we will rely on a combination of secondary research and an online Google survey. Our secondary research will consist of a review of relevant literature on the topic, including peer-reviewed articles and reports from reputable organizations. Our online survey will be conducted using Google Forms and will target individuals living in Sindh who have experienced floods. Through our research, we hope to answer the following questions: How has the frequency and severity of floods in Sindh changed over the past several decades? What role has climate change played in the observed changes in flood frequency and severity in Sindh? What impact have these floods had on the economic and social well-being of communities in Sindh? What measures have been taken to mitigate the impacts of floods in Sindh, and how effective have these measures been? To answer these questions, we will first review the existing literature on the relationship between climate change and floods in Sindh. This literature may include peer-reviewed articles and reports from reputable organizations such as the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) and the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC). We will also consider the experiences of other countries and regions that have faced similar challenges in order to identify the best practices and potential strategies for mitigating the impacts of floods. In addition to our literature review, we will conduct an online survey using Google Forms to gather data from individuals living in Sindh who have experienced floods. This survey will aim to capture the personal experiences and perceptions of these individuals regarding the frequency and severity of floods in the region, as well as the impact of these events on their economic and social well-being. The survey will also seek to gather information on the measures that have been taken to mitigate the impacts of floods in Sindh, and the effectiveness of these measures. By combining the results of our literature review and online survey, we hope to provide a more comprehensive understanding of the relationship between climate change and floods in Sindh, and to identify potential strategies for mitigating their impacts. Understanding the role of climate change in the frequency and severity of floods in Sindh is critical for effective adaptation and risk reduction efforts. Such efforts may include improved early warning systems, infrastructure upgrades, and the implementation of land use planning policies that take into account the risks of flooding. Ultimately, addressing the impacts of climate change on floods in Sindh will require a combination of local and global action, including the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions and the implementation of adaptation measures at the community level.

title: Two-patch Model of Language Competition
affiliations: National Institute of Chemical Physics and Biophysics, National Institute of Chemical Physics and Biophysics, National Institute of Chemical Physics and Biophysics, São Paulo State University (UNESP) and National Institute of Chemical Physics and Biophysics

detail.title: Two-patch Model of Language Competition
detail.abstract: We investigate a two-patch model of competition between two languages, representing a system that is divided into different regions by a barrier that is at the same time cultural and geographical in nature. Individuals can move between the patches with an assigned diffusion rate but cannot interact linguistically across the barrier; the diffusion can be symmetrical or asymmetrical. The model merges features of spatially extended models of language competition with a purely cultural barrier and that with only a diffusional barrier. The simplified dynamical framework of a two-patch macroscopic model allows an exact treatment of its stability properties. We find that depending on the interplay between the diffusion rates and the language preferences in each patch, the competition outcome can be either global consensus in one of the two languages or the coexistence of the two languages either in a dynamical equilibrium in both patches or through a strong segregation. The model lends itself to further generalizations and to applications involving language and cultural competition between groups separated by geographical barriers or belonging to different social subgroups.

title: A Mass Preserving Numerical Scheme for Kinetic Equations that Model Social Phenomena
affiliations: ,  and

detail.title: A Mass Preserving Numerical Scheme for Kinetic Equations that Model Social Phenomena
detail.abstract: In recent years, kinetic equations have been used to model many social phenomena. A key feature of these models is that transition rate kernels involve Dirac delta functions, which capture sudden, discontinuous state changes. Here, we study kinetic equations with transition rates of the form[[EQUATION]]T(x,y,u) = \delta_{\phi(x,y) - u}.We establish the global existence and uniqueness of solutions for these systems and introduce a fully deterministic scheme, the \emph{Mass Preserving Collocation Method}, which enables efficient, high fidelity simulation of models with multiple subsystems. We validate the accuracy, efficiency, and consistency of the solver on models with up to five subsystems, and compare its performance against two state-of-the-art agent-based methods: Tau-leaping and hybrid methods. Our scheme resolves subsystem distributions captured by these stochastic approaches while preserving mass numerically, requiring significantly less computational time and resources, and avoiding variability and hyperparameter tuning characteristic of these methods.

title: Error Estimate and Convergence Analysis for Data Valuation
affiliations: Tianjin University,  and University of Southern Queensland

detail.title: Error Estimate and Convergence Analysis for Data Valuation
detail.abstract: Data valuation aims to quantify the contribution of individual data points to learning objectives, yet most existing approaches based on the Shapley value [7, 1, 8] require multiple training runs and thus lack unified theoretical guarantees. The recently proposed neural dynamic data valuation (NDDV) framework [5] overcomes this limitation by casting data valuation as a discrete-time stochastic optimal control problem, enabling analysis via the stochastic maximum principle. In this work, we establish rigorous error estimates and convergence results for NDDV. Under standard Lipschitz and smoothness assumptions, we derive quadratic error bounds for loss differences that scale inversely with the time discretization and quadratically with control perturbations. We further prove that the expected squared gradient norm of the training loss vanishes asymptotically and that the associated meta loss achieves a sublinear convergence rate. These results provide the first mathematical guarantees for the stability and convergence of dynamic data valuation methods.

title: An Integrated Framework for Driving-Style-Aware Analysis and Prediction of Car-Following Conflicts in Mixed Traffic
affiliations: Beijing Jiaotong University, Beijing Jiaotong University, Beijing Jiaotong University,  and

detail.title: An Integrated Framework for Driving-Style-Aware Analysis and Prediction of Car-Following Conflicts in Mixed Traffic
detail.abstract: The rapid advancement of intelligent transportation systems is heralding in a prolonged era of mixed traffic, where autonomous vehicles (AVs) and human-driven vehicles (HVs) coexist. This complexity amplifies the challenges in modeling car-following conflict risk. To address this, we propose an integrated framework that investigates how microscopic kinematic behaviors influence conflict risk across different driving styles and enhances risk prediction accuracy. Utilizing the Lyft Level-5 Dataset, we extract microscopic driving volatility indicators and employ the rear-end crash risk index (RCRI) to quantify conflict risk. Driving styles are identified via K-medoids clustering. Subsequently, a Random Parameters Logit model with Heterogeneity in Means and Variances (RPLHMV) uncovers key risk factors and their multi-layered heterogeneity across AV–HV / HV–AV scenarios and driving styles. Furthermore, we develop a Random Deep & Cross Network with Monte Carlo dropout (RDCN-MC) to integrate behavioral heterogeneity and quantify predictive uncertainty for high-accuracy conflict risk prediction. Results identify three driving styles (conservative, normal, and aggressive) and reveal significant style-dependent heterogeneity in risk factors. Furthermore, the proposed RDCN-MC model demonstrates superior predictive performance. Based on these findings, we propose targeted safety interventions to improve autonomous driving control and human driver management, thereby enhancing mixed traffic safety.

title: Embedding Macroeconomic Risk Indicators into AI Fraud Detection Models Victor Osakwe, Eberhard-Karls-University of Tuebingen

detail.title: Embedding Macroeconomic Risk Indicators into AI Fraud Detection Models Victor Osakwe, Eberhard-Karls-University of Tuebingen

keywords.keywords: Fraud DetectionMacroeconomic Risk IndicatorsEnsemble Machine LearningEconomic-AI IntegrationSystemic Risk ModelingFinancial StabilityResponsible AI Systems

detail.abstract: Financial fraud detection systems often fail to adapt to shifts in the broader economy, resulting in high false negatives during economic downturns or market volatility. This paper proposes a hybrid framework that embeds macroeconomic risk indicators—such as credit spreads, unemployment rates, and liquidity ratios—into ensemble machine learning models for fraud detection. Using publicly available U.S. datasets from the Federal Reserve Economic Database (FRED), the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA), and the IEEE-CIS Fraud Detection benchmark, we evaluate model performance across varying economic regimes. Results indicate that incorporating macroeconomic features improves recall and detection stability by up to 14% during recessionary periods, compared to baseline models without economic context. The study demonstrates that integrating economic dynamics into AI-driven risk systems enhances their resilience, interpretability, and policy relevance. The proposed framework supports financial institutions in proactively managing systemic risks, aligning with the goals of responsible and adaptive AI in critical infrastructure applications.

title: Beyond Rankings: Bayesian stochastic frontier analysis of the determinants of university efficiency
affiliations: Universitat de València, , Universitat de València and Jaume I University - Department of Economics

detail.title: Beyond Rankings: Bayesian stochastic frontier analysis of the determinants of university efficiency
detail.abstract: University rankings predominantly focus on outputs while neglecting the efficiency with which institutions convert resources into outcomes. We contribute to addressing this limitation by analyzing the determinants of university efficiency using a Bayesian stochastic ray frontier model applied to 47 Spanish public universities over the 2016–2021 period. Unlike traditional approaches, our methodology jointly estimates efficiency and its determinants in a single stage.We adopt a multi-output framework encompassing the three university missions: teaching, research, and knowledge transfer. Using backward stepwise selection with the deviance infor mation criterion, we identify key efficiency determinants including the average department size, number of campuses, academic staff characteristics, and multi-province location. Results reveal substantial efficiency variations across universities, with approximately half showing positive efficiency changes over the period. The Bayesian approach provides full efficiency distributions rather than point estimates, enabling robust statistical comparisons. Our findings offer valuable insights for university managers and policymakers seeking to enhance institutional performance beyond traditional output-based rankings.

title: Environmental Factors Influencing the Development of Badminton Reserve Talents in Guangdong Province
affiliations: Guangdong University of Petrochemical Technology and Wuhan Sports University

detail.title: Environmental Factors Influencing the Development of Badminton Reserve Talents in Guangdong Province
detail.abstract: This study investigates the current status and development strategies of the Development of Badminton Reserve Talents (DBRT) in Guangdong Province. The study aims to provide scientific basis and practical guidance for the DBRT in Guangdong Province. By reviewing the development history of DBRT in Guangdong, the research employs a structural equation model to identify key factors influencing talent development, including management systems, training science, development environment, economic factors, social security, and socio-cultural elements. To gain a deeper understanding of these factors, this study uses expert interviews, literature analysis, and surveys conducted at badminton reserve talent bases to summarize existing problems in management systems, development environment, economic conditions, social security, socio-cultural aspects, and training science. Based on the analysis of these issues, the study draws on successful experiences from other leading provinces in badminton while fully considering the specific context and development needs of Guangdong Province. Several strategies are proposed to enhance DBRT, including: improving the national sports system to promote the sustainable development of badminton; strengthening the integration of sports and education to ensure the comprehensive development of reserve talents; achieving intensive talent cultivation through enhanced scientific training; optimizing the sports development environment to expand the foundation of badminton; improving the social security system to promote a diversified and socialized guarantee system; and advocating a cultural-first approach to explore and develop badminton culture.

title: Discrete Choice Models for Electric Vehicle Preferences, Consumer Behavior, and Policy Analysis
affiliations: Oita University, Toyo University and Kyushu University

detail.title: Discrete Choice Models for Electric Vehicle Preferences, Consumer Behavior, and Policy Analysis
detail.abstract: As electric vehicle (EV) becomes more widely adopted, research has expanded beyond pre-purchase decision-making to include policy interventions and post-purchase behaviors, such as vehicle replacement and ownership. We present a comprehensive review of empirical studies employing discrete choice models to analyze EV-related consumer behavior. The reviewed literature is divided into four thematic categories: (1) preferences and adoption; (2) EV policy; (3) purchase and replacement behavior; and (4) vehicle ownership. Studies on preferences highlight consumers’ willingness to pay for improvements in range and charging time, with socio-demographic and travel factors outweighing geographic or temporal effects. Policy research underscores that financial incentives remain influential but depend on design, while non-financial measures can be equally effective. Findings on purchase behavior highlight the importance of intuitive cost and emissions information, and ownership studies identify substantial non-use values. Overall, discrete choice models offer valuable insights into designing evidence-based EV policies and long-term decarbonization.

title: Peer-to-Peer Energy Collaborative Matching and Trading Mechanism Incorporating Microgrid Behavioral Value
affiliations: Central South University, Central South University, Central South University, Central South University and Central South University

detail.title: Peer-to-Peer Energy Collaborative Matching and Trading Mechanism Incorporating Microgrid Behavioral Value
detail.abstract: Peer-to-peer (P2P) transactions demonstrate potential for flexibility in energy trading within microgrids that incorporate distributed energy resources, with their decentralized structure enabling efficient energy use and dispatch. However, current P2P mechanisms face shortcomings in fairness, budget balance, and incentives for user participation, making them less suitable for handling the complex behavior patterns of prosumers in intricate microgrids and limiting their large-scale implementation. To address these issues, this paper proposes a P2P market pricing mechanism that includes behavioral value. First, a behavioral value function is defined, integrating four dimensions: marginal social welfare contribution, bid rationality, transaction reliability, and demand response contribution. This function captures diverse market behaviors in microgrids, allowing for optimal resource allocation across different market conditions through weighted adjustments. Second, a Pre-clearance and secondary response mechanism is introduced. During periods of renewable energy surplus, this mechanism encourages microgrids to perform flexible load adjustments while measuring the added flexibility value. Finally, market clearing is modeled as a bipartite graph maximum weight matching problem. By combining price matching and reputation matching weights, participants with higher reputations are given matching advantages. During settlement, microgrid performance scores influence bargaining power, affecting surplus distribution and transaction prices. Simulation results show that compared to traditional P2P methods, this approach improves energy utilization, enhances social welfare, increases market reliability, and encourages greater user participation.

title: Assessing the Efficiency of Sustainable Urban Traffic Congestion Management: Spatiotemporal Patterns and Driving Factors
affiliations: Huaiyin Institute of Technology, Huaiyin Institute of Technology, Huaiyin Institute of Technology, Huaiyin Institute of Technology, Kunming University of Science and Technology and Huaiyin Institute of Technology

detail.title: Assessing the Efficiency of Sustainable Urban Traffic Congestion Management: Spatiotemporal Patterns and Driving Factors
detail.abstract: Mitigating urban traffic congestion and enhancing regional transportation efficiency are crucial for achieving high-quality urban development. First, an evaluation framework for urban traffic congestion management efficiency is established using the Super-SBM model, which comprehensively considers both input and output processes. Second, the Malmquist index is employed to measure efficiency changes across different development phases, while the Dagum Gini coefficient reveals spatial disparities in urban traffic management efficiency.  Finally, spatial autocorrelation analysis was employed to examine the correlations and distribution patterns of traffic congestion management efficiency among the administrative districts in the study area. Results indicate: (1) Regarding overall efficiency, an upward trend was observed, though spatial distribution remained uneven, with a mean efficiency value of 0.5297. (2) In terms of total factor productivity (TFP), it remained low from 2013 to 2017, below the average of 0.8991. Technical efficiency (EC) initially rose and then declined, while changes in scale efficiency (SEC) generally surpassed those in pure technical efficiency (PEC). (3) Concerning spatial disparities, hyper-variable density was the primary source of variation (52.04%), exceeding both intra- and inter-regional differences. Significant gaps existed among the high-growth, transformation-development, and stable-mature zones, with a mean Gini coefficient of 0.055 indicating regional imbalance. Internal disparity was most prominent in the transformation-development zone. (4) For spatial correlation, the consistently positive global Morans I values confirmed significant spatial dependence. The spatial clustering patterns changed notably, with increasingly evident spillover effects. (5) Regarding key determinants, public transport development, intelligent transportation technologies, and investment in congestion governance were identified as the principal factors influencing performance.

title: Freedom Ring: A Culturally-Inspired Smart Jewelry for Iranian Women

detail.title: Freedom Ring: A Culturally-Inspired Smart Jewelry for Iranian Women
detail.abstract: Smart jewelry offers a promising intersection of cultural expression and utility. This study examines how a culturally sensitive, user-informed design can meet psychological and practical needs of Iranian women through the Freedom Ring, a modular form usable as both a ring and pendant, inspired by Tehran’s Azadi Tower and equipped with a passive NFC module for contactless payments.Using a mixed-methods design studio approach, the research integrates (a) a literature review on adornment, consumer psychology, and wearable adoption; (b) a survey of Iranian women (N = 100) on preferences for materials, styles, and smart features; and (c) iterative digital prototyping (Rhinoceros 3D modeling and renders) guided by studio critiques. Results show preference for precious materials (notably white gold), hybrid traditional–modern aesthetics, and discreet functionality. Respondents ranked personal taste, style, and convenience above brand or investment value.Mapping attributes to the Kano model indicates that comfort, durability, and reliable payment are basic qualities. Since no physical prototypes or payment trials were built, NFC integration is presented conceptually. Aesthetic refinement and convenience are performance qualities, while cultural symbolism, modular conversion, and discreet tech are attractive qualities. The concept shows how calm technology and cultural semiotics can combine to deliver empowerment, both functional (frictionless transactions) and psychological (identity expression, confidence).This paper contributes by: (1) offering a user-grounded framework for contextualized wearables; (2) applying Kano analysis to smart jewelry; and (3) presenting a transferable studio-based method for bridging craft heritage and digital features. Implications include localized innovation, interdisciplinary R&D, and ethically responsible feature selection.

title: DRL-Based Optimal Partitioning Strategy and Scheduling Method for Energy Storage Systems in Active Distribution Networks Considering Thermal Management Safety
affiliations: Tianjin University, Tianjin University, Tianjin University, Inner Mongolia University of Technology, Tianjin University, Tianjin University, Tianjin University and Tianjin University

detail.title: DRL-Based Optimal Partitioning Strategy and Scheduling Method for Energy Storage Systems in Active Distribution Networks Considering Thermal Management Safety
detail.abstract: As flexible resources, energy storage systems (ESSs) play a crucial role in maintaining the security and stability of active distribution networks (ADNs), particularly with increasing photovoltaic (PV) penetration and large-scale integration of fluctuating loads. Nevertheless, ESSs are susceptible to thermal runaway at elevated temperatures, while extremely low temperatures considerably reduce their available regulating capacity, thereby compromising the operational stability of ADNs. To overcome these limitations, this paper first employs a K-means++ algorithm using electrical distance with sum-of-squared-error (SSE) minimization to partition ESSs control areas. An active thermal management model is subsequently incorporated to address ambient temperature variations, and the dispatch optimization problem of ESSs is formulated as a Markov cooperative game. A multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) approach with a safety-constrained experience replay pool is developed to achieve optimal dispatch under operational constraints. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified through case studies on the IEEE 33-bus test system, considering scenarios of rapid PV output ramps and regional overloads. The results show 12.73% and 14.17% reductions in voltage deviations, along with 16.30 % and 7.18 % decreases in operational cost for the respective scenarios, demonstrating the method’s capability to enhance both security and economic performance under extreme operating conditions.
