detail.title: Information Asymmetrnals in Physician Selection: An Eye-Tracking and Discrete Choice Experiment Study
detail.abstract: Background: Information asymmetry between physicians and patients shapes healthcare decision-making. Online platforms provide quality signals through credentials, reviews, and satisfaction metrics, yet how physicians versus patients process these signals remains poorly understood. Objective: This study examines how patients and physicians respond to medical service quality signals when selecting doctors, combining stated preferences with objective visual attention data. Methods: We conducted two discrete choice experiments with eye-tracking in Nanjing, China (March 2024). Experiment 1 involved 54 participants (31 patients, 23 healthcare professionals) evaluating physicians based on four visual signals: reputation badges, treatment effectiveness, service attitude, and peer recommendations. Experiment 2 examined 31 patients' responses to visual and textual information combinations. Probit models analyzed relationships between attention and choices. Results: Patients' stated preferences diverged from visual attention. While patients rated treatment effectiveness most important (mean 4.52/5.0), eye-tracking revealed longest fixation on peer recommendations (2.89 vs 2.67 seconds; P=.04). Healthcare professionals focused more on treatment effectiveness (3.12 vs 2.67 seconds; P=.049). Peer recommendations showed the strongest attention-dependent effect (β=0.341, P=.001). Visual signals increased textual information attention by 18.5% (P=.002) without reducing decision time (P=.38). Conclusions: Substantial discrepancies exist between patients' stated preferences and actual information-seeking behavior. Physicians and patients process quality signals differently, with patients showing attention-preference misalignment for technical metrics. Visual indicators increase information processing depth rather than serving as shortcuts. Online health platforms should account for unconscious attention patterns alongside stated preferences.

detail.abstract: We extend the reference DSGE model used for policy analysis at the NBB with a financial sector, by incorporating multi-period fixed-rate corporate and mortgage loans, an imperfect pass-through from policy rates to the deposit rate, and bank capital re-quirements. Adding multi-period fixed-rate loans amplifies the propagation of default risks and strengthens the effectiveness of macroprudential policy. This amplification operates through a bank capital channel and a market timing effect that delays borrowing and investment when rates are expected to fall. The bank capital channel also propagates shocks across sectors, and amplifies the effects of monetary policy when the duration of banks’ assets is larger than that of their liabilities. With universal banks, that grant both corporate and mortgage loans, sectoral prudential policy instruments can have unintended consequences on credit supply in the untreated sector. These crowding out effects increase with the loan duration in the treated sector and decrease with the risk weight differential between the treated and untreated sectors. Finally, we apply our model to the mortgage risk weight add-on introduced by the NBB in 2013.

detail.abstract: This paper investigates the interaction between the rise of inelastic intermediaries, e.g. mutual funds and exchange traded funds (ETFs), and exchange rate dynamics. By leveraging regulatory microdata on the universe of mutual funds domiciled in Switzerland, we first document the remarkable rise of the market share of this industry. Mutual funds went from holding 5% of domestic currency fixed income instruments in 2005 to 51% in 2024. We show that these intermediaries have strict mandates and trade only when faced with in(out)-flows. This makes the market more price-inelastic on aggregate in response to asset demand shocks. We develop an analytical model that we bring to the microdata. We find that (i) an inflow into domestic mutual funds with a large portfolio weight on the domestic currency appreciates it and (ii) the reduced aggregate elasticity makes the exchange rate more sensitive to capital flows. Finally, using a weekly panel of five advanced economies, we document the external validity of this mechanism. We show that the currencies whose markets see a higher prevalence of inelastic intermediaries react significantly more strongly to capital inflows.

title: Power to the people and planet: democratising nature finance

detail.title: Power to the people and planet: democratising nature finance
detail.abstract: Market-based nature finance is rapidly expanding, yet many current models risk deepening social and ecological injustices. Democratising nature finance is not only about improving participation, but also shifting who defines values, makes decisions, and benefits. We undertook a study to understand how diverse community-led, market-based nature finance mechanisms (such as bonds, payments for ecosystem services, and nature credits) can contribute to more democratic nature finance. We propose a 4-part framework for assessing democratisation of these instruments and applied it to 11 community-led case studies. Our qualitative methodology combined semi-structured interviews (14 participants) with thematic analysis of 67 project documents, examining the governance, design, delivery and outcomes underpinning more democratic approaches. We found that community-based initiatives are governed by distinct institutional logics, centred on self-determination, local knowledge, and collective decision-making. Three archetypal institutional logics of democratisation—externally-led, partnership, and community-led—derived from the analysis. We show how these logics differentially configure authority, value, and financial control, thereby theorising democratisation as a structural feature of institutional arrangements, compared with a peripheral procedural element. Key enablers for more democratic approaches included securing land tenure, legal recognition of rights, community financial control, and safeguards against elite capture. Yet significant barriers persisted: limited access to capital, funder risk aversion, technocratic conditionalities, and systemic power imbalances. This study contributes to the emerging field of transformative nature finance by offering empirical insights into what more democratic market-based nature finance mechanisms look like in practice and how they begin to reconfigure power and decision rights within the wider financial system.

title: Stoicism and Christianity Compared: A Systematic Analysis of Their Parallels and Differences

detail.title: Stoicism and Christianity Compared: A Systematic Analysis of Their Parallels and Differences
detail.abstract: This paper examines the relationship between Stoicism and Christianity through a historically grounded and conceptually precise analysis. While both traditions emphasize moral character, inner steadiness and resilience in adversity, they rest on fundamentally different foundations. Stoicism is based on rational self mastery and an impersonal cosmic order, whereas Christianity centers on a personal God, divine grace and a relational understanding of human existence. Drawing on classical Stoic sources, biblical texts and contemporary scholarship, the article identifies key parallels, clarifies conceptual boundaries, and explains why certain differences remain irreducible.

detail.abstract: The collaboration between BUMDes Panggung Lestari and PT Tirta Investama (Danone-AQUA) is a response to the phenomenon of global and national environmental crises due to inadequate waste management, where Indonesia still disposes of most of the waste openly. While BUMDes Panggung Lestari has successfully implemented a circular economy, there is a research gap in comprehensively analyzing the implementation of the Public Private Partnership (PPP) partnership model and its relevance to the Build-Develop-Finance-Operate-Maintain (BDFOM) framework at the village level. Therefore, the purpose of this study is to examine how BUMDes Panggung Lestari and PT Tirta Investama apply the concept of PPP in waste management based on the circular economy and examine its relevance to the BDFOM model. The discussion shows that this partnership is an effective PPP at the micro level, where PT Tirta Investama carries out the role of Build, Develop, and Finance (such as the provision of pyrolysis machines and technical training) through CSR funds, while BUMDes independently manages the Operate and Maintain stagesby involving the community. This collaboration has been proven to produce sustainable impacts, such as increasing the turnover of BUMDes from IDR 450 million to IDR 1.8 billion, job creation, and reducing plastic waste stockpiles. This BDFOM-based PPP model is worthy of being used as a reference in encouraging sustainable village development in Indonesia.

detail.abstract: Policies supporting small businesses are popular among policymakers but often criticised by economists for their potential to distort the economy. This paper provides a comprehensive evaluation of a unique policy that subsidises the first employee. Empirically, we find that the policy led to a surge in the number of firms employing exactly one employee, without a noticeable effect on the number of firms with two or more employees. A simple frictionless general equilibrium model of occupational choices predicts the empirical facts remarkably well. detail.title: Gender differences in sustainable investment preferences: The role of disclosure and product category labeling
detail.abstract: We examine whether women and men behave differently in sustainable investment decisions and how these differences interact with disclosure and product category labeling of funds. Using the product categories ‘Sustainable’ and ‘Transition’, aligned with the EU’s proposed amendments to the Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation (SFDR), we run a discrete choice experiment with a representative sample of the German population. We find that funds labeled under a product category are generally preferred, with women more likely than men to select them, while men prioritize returns. Across all participants, funds with a stronger disclosure scope (‘Light-’ or ‘Dark-Green’) or labeled under a product category (‘Transition’ or ‘Sustainable’) are consistently preferred to funds without such labels. However, product categories dominate: participants systematically prefer Sustainable over Transition funds, while differences between disclosure scopes within a category are small. Providing additional information on environmental or social components of sustainability has no effect on investment choices.

detail.abstract: Rwanda has emerged as one of Africa’s most institutionally resilient and sustainability-oriented economies. Despite its relatively small size, landlocked geography, and limited natural-resource base, the country has demonstrated exceptional capacity for institutional rebuilding, governance reform, and environmental stewardship since the 1994 genocide. This paper examines Rwanda’s Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) trajectory by integrating analysis of demographic dynamics, economic structure, biodiversity assets, climate vulnerability, regulatory strength, and capital-market development. Particular attention is given to the role of the Rwanda Stock Exchange (RSE) in enabling SME growth, enhancing transparency, and supporting innovation. Drawing on global and African precedents in SME-focused capital-market models, the paper identifies actionable pathways through which Rwanda can leverage its governance advantages to expand green finance, incubate high-growth firms, and drive sustainable economic transformation. The analysis concludes that Rwanda is well positioned to become an East African exemplar of green, inclusive, and innovation-led development.

title: Keeping the Human in Humanitarian: The Effects of Artificial Intelligence on Donations to Humanitarian Organizations
affiliations: , University of Notre Dame and Independent

detail.title: Keeping the Human in Humanitarian: The Effects of Artificial Intelligence on Donations to Humanitarian Organizations
detail.abstract: Nonprofit organizations (NPOs), particularly humanitarian organizations (HOs), differ fundamentally from for-profit organizations (FPOs) in their revenue models; while FPOs are sustained by paying customers, HOs rely heavily on donor contributions. Private donors, who do not receive direct benefits in return for their contributions, are driven by organizational, personal, and environmental motivations unique to the humanitarian context. HOs, like FPOs, are increasingly adopting artificial intelligence (AI) technologies, yet little is known about how private donors' motivations and behavior are affected by HOs' use of AI. To address this gap, we conducted three online experiments exploring private donor preferences toward HOs with varying attributes, including the degree of AI involvement in decision-making. Across studies, donors consistently preferred human decision-makers over AI, especially when AI operated autonomously. Contextual factors, such as disaster stage and task type, further influenced these preferences. For example, across varying task types, AI use in the response-stage lowers donor activation by roughly 39% and donation amount by approximately 28%. Notably, human-AI collaboration did not offset such negative effects of AI use on donor support. These findings present important implications for the integration of AI within HOs, particularly amid current funding shortages. Our work highlights the critical need to align AI adoption with donor motivations to preserve trust, sustain financial contributions, and safeguard organizational impact.

detail.abstract: Skateboarding in Nairobi, Kenya, offers young people ways of asserting subjectivity, reimagining the city through movement, care, and shared presence. Based on semi-structured interviews, field observations, and sensory ethnography, this study traces how skateboarders transform overlooked sites-plazas, rooftops, and improvised parks-into spaces of community building, ecological care, and affective belonging. Grounded in decolonial thought, Indigenous teachings, and feminist ethics of care, the analysis frames skateboarding as a collective practice through which personhood is shaped, care for community and environment is sustained, and otherwise ways of being in the city are made possible. The findings show how Nairobi's skateboarders negotiate colonial and patriarchal histories and structures, generate affective ecologies of belonging through sound and movement, and practice feminist placemaking through accountability and solidarity. Clean-ups, DIY ramp-building, and the reclaiming of wastelands illustrate how skaters convert abandonment into commons and environmental responsibility. Such practices are not without tension, as skateboarders navigate precarity, layered marginalization, policing, stigmatization, the absence of formal facilities, complicity and conflicts within their own collectives. Ultimately this paper demonstrates that Nairobi's skateboarding practices are not only leisure, but also affective and relational world-making that point toward alternative decolonial urban futures.

detail.title: Analysis of the Implementation of CV Lion Ayang MSME Financial Statement Based on SAK EMKM
detail.abstract: The Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSME) sector plays a significant role in Indonesia’s economic growth. However, many MSME actors still face challenges in preparing financial statements in accordance with applicable accounting standards. This study aims to analyze the implementation of financial statement preparation at CV Lion Ayang, a catering service business located in South Jakarta, based on the Financial Accounting Standards for Micro, Small, and Medium Entities (SAK EMKM) 2024. This research applies a qualitative method through interviews, observations, and documentation. The results show that the financial recording system used by CV Lion Ayang is still simple and focuses mainly on cash flow records, without adopting the accrual basis of accounting. In addition, the business has not yet prepared a statement of financial position or notes to the financial statements as required by SAK EMKM. The main challenges identified include limited accounting knowledge, the absence of training or socialization regarding the standard, and insufficient human resources dedicated to financial management. This study recommends increasing accounting literacy and providing technical assistance for the implementation of SAK EMKM, so that financial statements can be prepared more accurately, support business decision-making, and enhance accountability.

detail.abstract: SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) has become the gold standard for explaining machine learning predictions, but its application to interrupted time series with multiple interventions suffers from a critical flaw: temporal contamination. When baseline distributions include data from future interventions, SHAP produces systematically biased attributions that can misclassify harmful interventions as beneficial. We introduce Windowed SHAP, a simple yet effective adaptation that limits analysis windows to exclude subsequent structural breaks. Tested on Israeli healthcare mortality data (2010-2022) with two major policy interventions, Windowed SHAP achieved 73.6% accuracy in identifying a harmful intervention (versus 15.5% with standard SHAP, a 58.1 percentage point improvement) while maintaining directional accuracy for a beneficial intervention despite challenging COVID-era confounding. Our method requires no modifications to SHAP's core algorithm, is computationally efficient, and provides a practical solution for policy evaluation and causal analysis in temporal settings. We discuss when Windowed SHAP is appropriate, identify its limitations with mixed baselines, and outline extensions including Segmented SHAP for complex scenarios.

detail.abstract: Evaluating and selecting among numerous alternative solutions shapes the trajectory and rate of innovation. Central to this process is a fundamental tension between novelty and feasibility that evaluators, operating under bounded rationality, cannot consider simultaneously and therefore rely on heuristics to guide their evaluations. A common heuristic is criteria-sequencing, in which evaluators prioritize alternative criteria at different evaluation stages. Yet, the idiosyncratic ways evaluators sequence these criteria often introduce inconsistencies, creating significant path dependencies in the process. In this paper, we propose that artificial intelligence (AI) offers a potential lever to structure evaluators’ criteria-sequencing heuristics. Leveraging a field experiment with 353 evaluators, we investigate how the sequencing of AI recommendations focusing on novelty and feasibility shapes the mean and variance of innovation among selected solutions. Our results reveal a mean–variance innovation tradeoff: a feasibility-then-novelty sequence leads to selections with higher mean innovation, whereas a novelty-then-feasibility sequence yields selections with greater innovation variance. Furthermore, a post hoc analysis uncovers that the format accompanying AI recommendations also matters. A dynamic format (i.e., interactive chatbot) increases the innovation variance among selected solutions but reduces their mean innovation relative to a static format (i.e., fixed explanatory content). Because these effects operate independently, our findings show that in AI-augmented evaluations, both the sequence of criteria and the format accompanying AI recommendations shape the mean–variance innovation tradeoff. These differences have important implications for the composition of innovation portfolios. Our paper contributes to innovation evaluation research and to emerging literature on human–AI collaboration in innovation-related contexts.

detail.title: Entrepreneurial Barriers and the Intention–Action Gap: A Case Study of Indonesian Generation Z Business Graduates
detail.abstract: Despite the strong entrepreneurial aspirations among Indonesia’s Generation Z business graduates, few manage to turn their intentions into actual business ventures. Through a deductive, explanatory case-study approach, the study conducted in-depth, semi-structured interviews with two recent graduates to explore how four barriers identified in the literature—psychological, financial, lack of mentorship, and regulatory complexity—interact to hinder action. The findings reveal that (1) a profound fear of failure, stemming from previous venture setbacks, undermines the confidence needed to launch; (2) persistent capital shortages are exacerbated by the respondents’ religious aversion to interest-bearing loans, necessitating slow self-financing; (3) limited access to affordable, ongoing mentorship leaves critical capability gaps unaddressed, reinforcing self-doubt; and (4) complex licensing fees, neighborhood approvals, and documentation requirements inflate start-up costs and timelines, intensifying both financial and psychological stress. These interconnected obstacles create a self-imposed readiness pause, during which graduates focus on skill-building and incremental saving rather than formalizing their ventures.

title: Implementing the Risk–Proportionality Principle: A Minimal Real–World Pricing Engine Based on Lognormal Simulation

detail.title: Implementing the Risk–Proportionality Principle: A Minimal Real–World Pricing Engine Based on Lognormal Simulation
detail.abstract: This technical note presents a minimal and implementation-ready version of the Risk–Proportionality Principle (RPP). The goal is to provide a straightforward pricing engine that avoids risk-neutral assumptions and relies only on the historical (physical-measure) distribution of index returns. For simplicity and stability, the terminal index level is modeled as lognormal under the physical measure, and the option premium is adjusted using the Sharpe-consistency correction term derived from SCP/RPP. No density capping, no measure transformation, and no PDE machinery are used. This version is optimized for engineering deployment, backtesting, and prototyping.

title: A Strategic Framework for Sustainable Centralisation of Wastewater Treatment Plants: Integrating economic and environmental analysis

detail.title: A Strategic Framework for Sustainable Centralisation of Wastewater Treatment Plants: Integrating economic and environmental analysis
detail.abstract: Across Europe, water utilities face increasing challenges, from aging infrastructure to limited operational capacity. Centralisation strategies, redirecting flows from smaller to larger facilities, might offer opportunities to improve performance and capacity. This study presents decision-support tools to evaluate the economic and environmental impacts of centralisation plans, using a real-world case involving five Wastewater Treatment Plants (WWTPs) (Døjsøvej, Skovby, Ry, Hørning, and Gl. Rye) in Skanderborg, Denmark. The framework combines techno-economic analysis (TEA) and life cycle assessment (LCA) to evaluate both the construction and operational phases. TEA estimates the net present value (NPV) over 40 years, considering five cost categories: capital expenditure (CAPEX), operational expenditure (OPEX), maintenance, staffing, and renovation. LCA helps identify critical environmental trade-offs, focusing on impacts to human health (HH), ecosystem degradation (EQ), and resource depletion (RD). Monte Carlo simulations propagate parameter uncertainty in both TEA and LCA to evaluate decision robustness. Results show centralisation is 18% more profitable than decentralisation, NPVs of –€83M versus –€101M for the decentralised option. This difference is mainly driven by lower maintenance, OPEX, and staffing costs. Environmentally, centralisation showed substantially higher impacts: the construction phase damages were ~75% higher due to energy-intensive pipeline works. During operations, centralised systems also showed higher impacts, with freshwater eutrophication accounting for 65% of ecosystem quality impacts in the centralisation scenario due to higher emissions to water. Uncertainty analysis confirmed the robustness of the TEA and LCA results. The proposed framework supports informed decision-making in utility planning and can be applied to other utilities facing similar challenges.

title: When Trust Obscures Truth: Can Machine Learning Detect Fraud Where Traditional Audits Fail?
affiliations: and

detail.title: When Trust Obscures Truth: Can Machine Learning Detect Fraud Where Traditional Audits Fail?
detail.abstract: Microfinance institutions are critical drivers of economic development, yet their stability is frequently undermined by internal fraud. This study addresses this challenge within Bali's indigenous microfinance institutions, the Lembaga Perkreditan Desa (LPD), which is persistently threatened by internal fraud, a problem rooted in the information asymmetries and goal incongruence described by Agency Theory. Traditional audits often fail to mitigate these agency costs because they are reactive and lack the capacity to analyze complex transactional data. This study addresses this critical governance gap by integrating Agency Theory with Prediction Theory to develop and validate a proactive, data-driven fraud risk assessment framework. Employing an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design, we analyzed 5 years of panel data (2019–2023) from 30 LPDs using the unsupervised Isolation Forest (iForest) algorithm to detect financial anomalies. The quantitative findings were subsequently contextualized through in-depth interviews with eight experienced LPD auditors and supervisors. The iForest model successfully identified high-risk observations characterized by patterns such as anomalously low loan-loss provisions and inconsistent asset-deposit growth. The qualitative phase confirmed these patterns are significant red flags often overlooked due to a culturally rooted trust bias and the absence of forensic data analytics. This research concludes that unsupervised machine learning offers not just a technical tool, but a novel governance mechanism to mitigate agency problems in a microfinance context. The primary implication of these findings is a potential paradigm shift in regulatory oversight, moving from reactive, compliance-based audits to a proactive, risk-based supervisory model, ultimately enhancing financial transparency and securing the long-term viability of these vital community institutions.

title: An Integrated Framework of Agile Leadership, Trust, and AI Implementation: Impacts on Organizational Capabilities and Performance

detail.title: An Integrated Framework of Agile Leadership, Trust, and AI Implementation: Impacts on Organizational Capabilities and Performance
detail.abstract: The contemporary business environment demands effective artificial intelligence (AI) implementation strategies to achieve competitive advantages, yet organizations face significant challenges in translating AI investments into tangible outcomes. This study develops and empirically tests an integrated framework examining the relationships among management commitment, agile leadership factors, trust in AI, AI implementation, and organizational performance outcomes. Using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with data from organizations implementing AI technologies, the research reveals counterintuitive findings that challenge conventional assumptions. While management commitment strongly predicts trust in AI, trust does not significantly influence AI implementation success. Among agile leadership dimensions, only concrete organizational capabilities, specifically agile work environment and team skills, significantly drive implementation, while general agile leadership shows non-significant effects. AI implementation demonstrates powerful cascading effects on company competitiveness, knowledge management capacity, and dynamic capabilities, which subsequently enhance sustainable employee work performance. These findings suggest that AI implementation success depends more on tangible organizational capabilities than on psychological factors or leadership styles. The study provides evidence-based guidance for organizations, recommending prioritization of concrete capability-building initiatives over trust-building or general leadership approaches. This research contributes to theory by challenging trust-centric AI adoption models and extends agile leadership theory by distinguishing between general traits and specific capabilities, while offering practical insights for organizations navigating AI adoption in an increasingly AI-driven business landscape.

title: Research on Coordinated Dispatch Model of Generation-Grid-Load-Storage for New Power Systems Under Continuous Meteorological Disasters

detail.title: Research on Coordinated Dispatch Model of Generation-Grid-Load-Storage for New Power Systems Under Continuous Meteorological Disasters
detail.abstract: This paper addresses compound disaster scenarios involving sandstorms and static stability weather, constructing a quantitative resilience analysis framework for power systems. By establishing a joint probability model for cold waves and static stability weather, the study quantifies their coupled occurrence risk. Furthermore, it develops a time-varying transmission line outage probability model, a photovoltaic output degradation model, and a coordinated generation-grid-load-storage dispatch model. Simulation case studies based on the North China Power Grid demonstrate that although compound disasters have an extremely low probability of occurrence, they pose the highest risk, leading to severe photovoltaic output degradation and significant power supply pressure. While system operation can be maintained through the coordinated dispatch of multiple resources, economic costs increase substantially. Sensitivity analysis further reveals that the total system cost is highly sensitive to temperature changes and disaster duration, and compound disasters exhibit a nonlinear superimposition effect. This research provides a methodology for assessing power system resilience under compound disasters, offering reference value for enhancing the ability of new power systems to cope with climate risks.

title: Good Governance in Practice: A Qualitative Analysis of Village Government Performance in Indonesian Independent Villages
affiliations: , Bandung Institute of Technology and

detail.title: Good Governance in Practice: A Qualitative Analysis of Village Government Performance in Indonesian Independent Villages
detail.abstract: This study examines the effectiveness of village governance in Indonesian Independent villages, highlighting the critical paradox where villages achieving the highest Village Development Index (IDM) ratings simultaneously exhibit substantial governance deficiencies that contradict good governance principles. Despite their elevated status, these villages continue to face persistent challenges, including corruption, financial mismanagement, and limited community outcomes, which directly violate the principles of transparency, accountability, and effectiveness. Using qualitative multiple case study design with semi-structured interviews across two Independent villages in Bandung Regency and employing Gioia methodology, this research identifies five critical governance dimensions: (1) Governance Capacity & Resources, revealing significant competency gaps hinders performance efficiency; (2) Planning & Coordination Mechanisms, as top-down policies frequently conflict with bottom-up community aspirations, reducing participatory effectiveness; (3) Transparency, Accountability & Oversight, demonstrating procedural compliance with reporting serving as a formality rather than a genuine tool of performance accountability; (4) Community Engagement & Inclusion, dominated by conventional mechanisms limiting inclusive participation; and (5) Institutional Functionality & Governance Structure, displaying leadership-dependent effectiveness that challenges rule of law consistency. These findings reveal a governance paradox in which formal compliance with structures conceals practices that contradict the principles of good governance. The study emphasizes the need for outcome-based performance evaluation systems that prioritize substantive governance over procedural compliance.

title: Commercial Representation under Lebanese Law: An Analytical Legal Study
affiliations: Islamic University of Lebanon

detail.title: Commercial Representation under Lebanese Law: An Analytical Legal Study

keywords.keywords: Trade Representation Commercial Agency Legal Classification Legislative Reform Commercial Contracts Contractual Independence

detail.abstract: This research examines the legal framework of trade representation under the Lebanese law by analyzing its concept, legal nature, and the legislative foundations upon which its practices are based within the Lebanese commercial environment. Despite the crucial role that trade representation plays in stimulating market activity, attracting investments, and expanding distribution networks, the Lebanese legal system still lacks a clear and comprehensive legislative framework that defines this system and determines its elements, the rights of its parties, and their obligations. This legislative void has given rise to complex practical challenges, especially in distinguishing between trade representation and commercial agencies, which has compelled the judiciary to assume the central role in determining the correct legal classification of the contractual relationship between the parties. The research aims to study the composite nature of trade representation as a professional activity based on the commercial independence of the representative while remaining connected to the interests of the principal. It also analyzes the elements of the representative relationship and assesses the extent to which it is subject to the rules of civil agency, commercial principles, or contractual customs. The research further highlights the main judicial challenges that have emerged due to the absence of a unified legislative framework—such as the difficulty of legal classification, proving the nature of the relationship, the consequences of its termination, and the representative’s right to compensation. Additionally, the research presents the most notable Lebanese judicial precedents that attempted to delineate the boundaries of trade representation and establish objective criteria for it, offering a critical perspective on the current legal situation and proposing mechanisms for adopting modern legislation that meets the needs of the Lebanese market and achieves balance between party freedom and commercial stability. The research concludes that strengthening the legal framework of trade representation in Lebanon requires issuing a unified law that ends legislative and judicial fragmentation, guarantees effective protection for the trade representative, and provides a clear and reliable legal environment that enhances confidence in commercial transactions and supports economic growth.

title: Short-term renewable energy forecast errors: spatial dependency and smoothing potential
affiliations: German Aerospace Center (DLR), German Aerospace Center (DLR) - German Remote Sensing Data Center and

detail.title: Short-term renewable energy forecast errors: spatial dependency and smoothing potential
detail.abstract: Renewable energy forecast errors lead to costly countermeasures such as countertrading, redispatch, and increased operating reserve requirements. Large-scale, correlated regional forecast errors pose significant challenges to renewable energy portfolios, however, the spatial structure of renewable energy forecast errors remains relatively little understood. This study aims to address this gap by investigating the spatial dependencies of short-term (intraday to two-days ahead)  renewable energy forecast errors. We derive site-specific correlation lengths and evaluate the forecast error smoothing potential in Europe. By increasing the site separation beyond 150 km, renewable energy forecast errors become uncorrelated, leading at day-ahead lead time to a reduction in mean absolute errors and extreme forecast error events of more than 33% for wind energy and around 25% for solar energy. Furthermore, leveraging the principal directions of forecast errors can further reduce the site separation required to achieve even greater forecast error reductions. Finally, we evaluate the current and planned renewable energy sites in Europe in light of these findings and identify forecast error hotspots. This study provides an unprecedented characterization of renewable energy forecast errors in Europe and provides actionable insights for decision-makers involved in designing and operating renewable energy portfolios, supporting the development of forecast error-resilient systems.

title: The Discovery and Pursuit of a Leadership Quest

detail.title: The Discovery and Pursuit of a Leadership Quest
detail.abstract: Leaders are the architects of a better and more desirable future. It can be contented that these futures are embodied in and manifest through the discovery and pursuit of worthy, value-adding leadership quests. Understanding the discovery and pursuit of a leadership quest is thus mission-critical to the continuing assured, viable, and desired future of organizations, communities, and humanity. However, a growing, accelerating leadership crisis is seemingly in the making globally, as evident in multiple indicators—such as rising leadership incompetence,  unwiseness, unethical conduct, and follower disengagement—affecting not only leaders, but also their followers and contexts. Bad leadership is on the rise. This begs the question: are we entering the dark ages of leadership? The discovery and pursuit of a worthy, value-adding quest as the core manifestation of leadership excellence is posited as a counter-measure to this crisis. However, leadership quest as a concept has not been systematically researched , with the closest concept being calling. Adopting a narrative inquiry research design, our research set out, first, to develop a leadership quest model based on personal interviews with a sample of seasoned, senior leaders; secondly, by a validation of the model through ‘simulated’ interviews with three famous leaders. Next, as a first step towards the development of a leadership quest theory, a set of hypotheses were deduced from the model.

title: Improving performance and attractiveness of rural train-bus networks with timetable synchronisation
affiliations: , , Delft University of Technology, Delft University of Technology and Delft University of Technology

detail.title: Improving performance and attractiveness of rural train-bus networks with timetable synchronisation
detail.abstract: This study presents a comparative analysis of the three train-bus timetable synchronisation approaches in order to improve the performance and attractiveness of integrated public transport networks in rural areas. While the existing literature mainly focuses on synchronisation approaches separately, limited attention has been given to comparing the different synchronisation approaches, with the incorporation of passenger demand. By understanding the differences between these approaches, this research seeks to provide transport operators with insights into the effectiveness of the approaches. To address this gap, this research develops a Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model to compare the three synchronisation approaches: train-first, bus-first, and simultaneous synchronisation. Applied to a rural public transport network in Friesland, the model minimises total passenger travel time weighted by passenger demand. The case study, consisting of one train line and thirteen connecting bus services, provides a manageable evaluation of the model. The results show that simultaneous synchronisation consistently outperforms the sequential approaches, achieving the lowest total passenger waiting time for most operating hours and service lines. Comparing the simultaneous synchronisation approach to the current timetable shows significant improvements in total passenger waiting time across all operating hours and for most of the lines. A mode choice analysis using a Multinomial Logit (MNL) model shows an increase in ridership of 4.4% based on the improved timetable, which facilitates a modal shift of 0.58% from private car to public transport. These findings show that timetable synchronisation alone, without improving infrastructure or the addition of more services, can increase the attractiveness of the public transport network. These findings are especially important in rural areas where car dependency is typically higher. The results suggest that transport authorities should reconsider the current sequential timetable synchronisation practices. Optimisation of multimodal networks simultaneously can improve the performance and attractiveness of integrated public transport networks in rural areas.

title: Applications of Virtual Reality Integrated with BIM in Modeling, Management, and Training in Civil Construction: A Systematic Review of the Literature
affiliations: , ,  and

detail.title: Applications of Virtual Reality Integrated with BIM in Modeling, Management, and Training in Civil Construction: A Systematic Review of the Literature
detail.abstract: The digitalization of the Architecture, Engineering, Construction and Operation (AECO) sector has intensified the adoption of technologies to improve productivity, efficiency, and safety. In this context, the integration of Building Information Modeling (BIM) and Virtual Reality (VR) has emerged as a promising approach for project management, modeling, and immersive training. This study conducted a Systematic Literature Review following PRISMA and PICO guidelines, resulting in 51 selected articles. The findings highlight the use of Revit, Navisworks, IFC, and game engines, with applications focused on collaborative modeling, information management, and safety training.

title: An Adaptive Iterative Multi-Objective Optimization Framework for Public EV Charging Infrastructure Planning
affiliations: Beijing Institute of Technology and Beijing Institute of Technology

detail.title: An Adaptive Iterative Multi-Objective Optimization Framework for Public EV Charging Infrastructure Planning
detail.abstract: The rapid growth of electric vehicles (EVs) poses significant challenges for electric vehicle charging infrastructure (EVCI) planning. This study proposes an adaptive multi-objective optimization framework for public EVCI siting and sizing. It integrates a spatiotemporal charging load prediction model with an iterative facility optimization process. It first simulates charging demand under a given infrastructure layout and subsequently performs joint optimization of the number and types of chargers (fast and slow) according to cost, annual revenue, and charging abandonment rate. This simulation–optimization cycle is repeated until convergence, yielding a globally optimal configuration. The proposed method employs real-world EV operation data from Beijing along with a hybrid trip-chain-based charging load prediction model to generate comprehensive charging demand profiles under diverse scenarios. Through controlled variable analysis, the study investigates how optimal infrastructure configurations evolve in response to variations in investment levels, EV feet size, the ratio of private to non-private EVs, and the penetration rate of private chargers. The results demonstrate their impacts on revenue, vehicle-to-charger ratios, and the balance between fast and slow chargers. Overall, the proposed method offers a flexible, data-driven, and mechanism-oriented approach for scalable public EVCI planning.

title: Personalized metro crew rostering: A hybrid machine learning approach to account for driver preference heterogeneity
affiliations: , Beijing Jiaotong University and Tsinghua University - Department of Industrial Engineering

detail.title: Personalized metro crew rostering: A hybrid machine learning approach to account for driver preference heterogeneity
detail.abstract: Metro crew rostering is the process of constructing work timetables for metro drivers to ensure efficient and compliant operation of metro services. Current crew rostering models ignore driver preference heterogeneity and use a one-size-fits-all approach that treats all staff as homogenous, aiming to minimize the penalty incurred from violating crew preference or operation rule constraints. However, crew preferences are demonstrated to be heterogeneous, meaning that modeling all staff with a uniform preference metric cannot truly reflect individual preference and will not lead to genuine penalty minimization. To cope with this situation, we propose a personalized crew rostering model accounting for driver preference heterogeneity in this research, which is new to the literature. We collect driver preferences through a weight-allocation survey covering seven roster types, and model heterogeneous preference metrics by a hybrid machine learning approach, which compares nine statistical and machine learning models and selects the best-performing one for each roster type. To optimize rostering for each individual, we formulate a mixed-integer linear programming that integrates heterogeneous crew preference. The personalized crew rostering problem is solved using a commercial solver and we further discuss the relationship between overall preference satisfaction and individual preference satisfaction. Numerical experiments are conducted against the background of two metro lines in Beijing. The numerical experiment results confirm that the heterogeneous preference-based personalized crew rostering model can improve overall satisfaction by 140% while fulfilling each individual’s top three preferred roster types, all within a relatively short computational time, thus providing a valuable practice for metro companies.

title: Designing a School Development Index from a Strategic Management Perspective: A Multi-Criteria Decision Support System
affiliations: Republic of Turkey Ministry of National Education and Marmara University

detail.title: Designing a School Development Index from a Strategic Management Perspective: A Multi-Criteria Decision Support System
detail.abstract: Improving school performance within public education systems constitutes a complex socio-economic planning challenge, shaped by multi-dimensional institutional processes and the growing requirement for evidence-based resource allocation. Despite considerable progress in strategic management and performance measurement, existing frameworks lack a validated composite indicator that systematically integrates managerial capacity, governance effectiveness, and data-driven evaluation into a unified decision-support structure. This study addresses this gap by developing a School Development Index (SDI) built upon Critical Success Factors (CSFs) to guide strategic priority setting for policymakers and school leaders.Using an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design within the context of an emerging economy, the study applies a hybrid Multi-Criteria Decision-Making (MCDM) framework: the Delphi technique to refine CSFs, Lawshe’s Content Validity Ratio to ensure indicator validity, DEMATEL to model causal interactions among improvement dimensions, and SWARA to determine their strategic weights. Results show that Leadership and Governance functions as the principal causal lever influencing the improvement system, whereas Learning–Teaching Processes emerge as the most policy-sensitive dependent dimension. A scenario-based simulation further demonstrates the SDI’s utility as a diagnostic Decision Support System (DSS), enabling differentiated, context-specific policy interventions rather than static performance rankings.This study contributes to socio-economic planning by offering a theoretically grounded and methodologically robust composite indicator that enhances strategic management, supports efficient resource deployment, and strengthens the capacity of public education systems to design targeted, high-leverage improvement policies.

title: Reinforcement Learning-Guided Dynamic Multi-Graph Fusion for Evacuation Traffic Prediction
affiliations: University of Central Florida and University of Central Florida

detail.title: Reinforcement Learning-Guided Dynamic Multi-Graph Fusion for Evacuation Traffic Prediction
detail.abstract: Real-time traffic prediction is critical for managing transportation systems during hurricane evacuations. Although data-driven graph-learning models have demonstrated strong capabilities in capturing the complex spatiotemporal dynamics of evacuation traffic at a network level, they mostly consider a single dimension (e.g., travel-time or distance) to construct the underlying graph. Furthermore, these models often lack interpretability, offering little insight into which input variables contribute most to their predictive performance. To overcome these limitations, we develop a novel Reinforcement Learning-guided Dynamic Multi-Graph Fusion (RL-DMF) framework for evacuation traffic prediction. We construct multiple dynamic graphs at each time step to represent heterogeneous spatiotemporal relationships between traffic detectors. A dynamic multi-graph fusion (DMF) module is employed to adaptively learn and combine information from these graphs. To enhance model interpretability, we introduce RL-based intelligent feature selection and ranking (RL-IFSR) method that learns to mask irrelevant features during model training. The model is evaluated using a real-world dataset of 12 hurricanes affecting Florida from 2016 to 2024. For an unseen hurricane (Milton, 2024), the model achieves a 95% accuracy (RMSE = 293.9) for predicting the next 1-hour traffic flow. Moreover, the model can forecast traffic flow for up to next 6 hours with 90% accuracy (RMSE = 426.4). The RL-DMF framework outperforms several state-of-the-art traffic prediction models. Furthermore, ablation experiments confirm the effectiveness of dynamic multi-graph fusion and RL-IFSR approaches for improving model performance. This research provides a generalized and interpretable model for real-time evacuation traffic forecasting, with significant implications for evacuation traffic management.

reference: AI in Supply Chains. Maxime Cohen and Tinglong Dai, Edts. Springer Series in Supply Chain Management.
title: The Invisible Backbone: How Supply Chains Bring AI to Life
affiliations: University of Pennsylvania - The Wharton School and

detail.title: The Invisible Backbone: How Supply Chains Bring AI to Life

publicationDetails.detailsText: AI in Supply Chains. Maxime Cohen and Tinglong Dai, Edts. Springer Series in Supply Chain Management.

detail.abstract:
The sustained growth of Generative AI (GenAI), exemplified by technologies like ChatGPT, fundamentally depends on the performance of its supply chain-an often overlooked
"invisible backbone." This backbone encompasses everything from the sourcing of critical raw materials and manufacturing of AI chips to the infrastructure powering data centers worldwide. As GenAI rapidly becomes indispensable in critical sectors like healthcare, finance, and transportation, global supply chains face unprecedented strain. Supply chain professionals must therefore urgently address vulnerabilities, build resilience, and implement sustainable lifecycle management, including end-of-life recycling strategies, to ensure the continued expansion and reliability of AI technologies. In this chapter, we systematically examine critical environmental, political, legal, and ethical challenges that can disrupt the AI supply chain. Our goal is to highlight the unprecedented complexities and risks posed by GenAI' s rapid growth, underscoring the urgent need for proactive supply chain management and comprehensive risk mitigation strategies.

title: Methodology in technology management:,The method QuickScan+ as a modification of EDUAR&D for evaluating technologies in product development
affiliations: , ,  and

detail.title: Methodology in technology management:,The method QuickScan+ as a modification of EDUAR&D for evaluating technologies in product development
detail.abstract: For a systematic yet low-complexity technology analysis in product development, QuickScan+ method is developed and tested. It represents a methodological adaptation of the established EDUAR&D framework, aiming to support early-stage technology evaluation with reduced analytical effort. QuickScan+ is particularly suited for users without in-depth prior knowledge of the assessed technologies and provides structured guidance for independent initial evaluations. A unified technology lifecycle scheme is introduced to facilitate lifecycle classification. The method is demonstrated through the evaluation of additive manufacturing technologies. While QuickScan+ improves comparability and decision support, its significance remains limited and it should complement, rather than replace, expert-based assessments.

title: Multilevel Deep Feature Fusion for Surface Roughness Detection of Milled Workpieces
affiliations: Xiamen University, Xiamen University and Xiamen University

detail.title: Multilevel Deep Feature Fusion for Surface Roughness Detection of Milled Workpieces
detail.abstract: Existing machine vision-based methods for measuring workpiece surface roughness require manual design of roughness-related feature indicators and have stringent imaging environment requirements, making them less suitable for direct application in manufacturing processes. On the other hand, deep learning-based methods rely on many training samples and need to retrain models when the measurement target changes. To address these issues, a dual branch multilevel deep feature fusion model based on a convolutional neural network (CNN) and a Vision Transformer (DeiT-S) for measuring workpiece surface roughness is proposed. Feature fusion operations are introduced at the intermediate and final layers of the two branches, effectively enhancing the joint learning of global and local deep features from workpiece surface images. The experimental results demonstrate that with a limited dataset of 7,571 samples, the proposed model achieves a classification accuracy of 99.92% (±0.05%), outperforming single-branch ResNet18 and DeiT-S by 1.24% and 2.05%, respectively. Key innovations include (1) a dual branch feature fusion mechanism enabling joint modelling of local textures and global illumination dependencies and (2) enhanced fine-grained feature extraction through Convolutional Block Attention Modules (CBAM), effectively reducing the dependence on large-scale training data.Furthermore, the proposed model can be integrated into a fast measurement system for online roughness measurement tasks in most industrial production processes and can be adapted to measure different types of target workpiece roughness through appropriate transfer learning methods.

title: On Intensity of Preference Rank Reversal in the AHP
affiliations: Silesian University in Opava and Comillas Pontifical University

detail.title: On Intensity of Preference Rank Reversal in the AHP
detail.abstract: The analytic hierarchy process (AHP) is one of the most widely used multicriteria decision-making methods, with applications from agriculture to space engineering. Despite its popularity, AHP has been repeatedly criticised for rank reversal, a phenomenon in which the ranking of alternatives changes after the addition or removal of an irrelevant or duplicate alternative.This paper introduces a new type of rank reversal in AHP, arising when the intensity of preferences is uniformly increased. We show that even when all pairwise preferences preserve their direction and are intensified identically, the eigenvector method may produce a different ordering of alternatives. In contrast, the geometric mean (GM) method is robust to this intensity-of-preference (IOP) rank reversal.The applicability of this result is shown through a real decision-making problem taken from a NASA manual concerning capability prioritisation for the planned lunar Gateway orbital station.

title: A Hybrid DBN and TCN-Transformer Approach for Health State Assessment of Sliding Bearings
affiliations: , , Hefei University of Technology, Boehringer Ingelheim Animal Health USA Inc. - Global Pharmaceutical Technical Support (GPTS), , , ,  and

detail.title: A Hybrid DBN and TCN-Transformer Approach for Health State Assessment of Sliding Bearings

keywords.keywords: Sliding bearing ； Deep Belief Network ； Health indicator ； TCN-Transformer ； Degradation assessment

detail.abstract: Sliding bearings, as core components in rotating machinery, often exhibit nonlinear degradation and multi-scale failure characteristics under varying operational conditions, which pose signif-icant challenges for health state prediction. Traditional methods, such as Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and other linear feature extraction techniques, struggle to capture the complex, nonlinear degradation patterns inherent in sliding bearings. This paper proposes a novel health indicator construction method based on Deep Belief Networks (DBN) and a state prediction model combining Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCN) and Transformers to address these challenges. The proposed method integrates multi-domain features from time, frequency, and spectral kurtosis domains, enhancing the robustness and accuracy of health indicators for sliding bearings. Through an accelerated degradation test platform, vibration signals are collected under different rotational speeds and radial loads. The DBN-based health indicator shows a significant improvement in monotonicity (71.2%) and robustness (0.974) compared to traditional methods. Furthermore, the TCN-Transformer model outperforms existing models (TCN, GRU, LSTM) with a Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 0.0015 and a Coefficient of Determination (𝑅2) of 89.23%. The results demonstrate that the proposed method provides a more accurate and reliable solution for predicting the health state and degradation trends of sliding bearings, offering valuable insights for intelligent maintenance and prognostics in industrial applications.

title: Knowledge Graph Learning of Decision Paths for Strategy Recommendation on Sluice Group Scheduling
affiliations: Hohai University, Hohai University, Hohai University, , Hohai University, ,  and Hohai University

detail.title: Knowledge Graph Learning of Decision Paths for Strategy Recommendation on Sluice Group Scheduling
detail.abstract: The recommendation system is often used to predict users’ selection probability on potential items, by analyzing historical user-item interactions, item attributes, and collaborative preference patterns. However,  strategy recommendation aims to propose action plans for optimal outcomes, requiring causal inference on how strategies dynamically affect system states.  It needs to evaluate countless intervention sequences across evolving states, leading to substantial combinatorial explosion in the solution space. To address this challenge, this paper introduces \textit{decision path} to characterize the dynamic influences among the strategies and their relevant decision-making elements, then store them compactly in a knowledge graph. Afterwards, a transformer-based algorithm named KDPN(Knowledge-aware Decision Path Network) is proposed, in order to capture these paths’ semantic dependencies, and learn the optimal path selection in different states.  We evaluate this approach in a real sluice-group scheduling scenario, where it outperforms the baseline models by over 50\% in accuracy, demonstrating the practical utility for real-time decision-making in dynamic systems. On public datasets, our approach shows an overall improvement of about 7\% over traditional baselines, demonstrating that incorporating decision paths is a feasible approach for recommendation tasks.

title: Physics-Guided Multimodal Transformer with Hybrid Training Synergy for Intelligent Welding Quality Prediction
affiliations: Shanghai University of Electric Power, Shanghai University of Electric Power, Shanghai University of Electric Power, , Shanghai University of Electric Power, Shanghai University of Electric Power, Shanghai University of Electric Power and Shanghai University of Electric Power

detail.title: Physics-Guided Multimodal Transformer with Hybrid Training Synergy for Intelligent Welding Quality Prediction
detail.abstract: Online quality prediction for resistance spot welding (RSW) faces significant challenges due to extreme class imbalance and heterogeneous multimodal signals. To address these challenges, we propose Vision Transformer-Hierarchical Attention Aggregation Network （ViT-HAAN）, a physics-guided multimodal fusion framework that integrates visual and process data through an asymmetric hierarchical attention mechanism. In this architecture, post-welding images act as “result anchors” to guide temporal feature extraction from dynamic process signals. A hybrid training strategy—combining Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) at the data level with Focal Loss at the algorithm level—mitigates imbalance while uncovering a synergistic interaction between classification and regression objectives. Experimental results show that ViT-HAAN substantially improves both classification and regression performance compared with the baseline (Model 1). The macro-average F1-score for defect detection increases from 0.40 to 0.88 (absolute +0.48, relative +120%). For regression, the MAE of weld nugget diameter decreases from 0.26 mm to 0.20 mm (≈ 23.1% reduction, and 0.20 mm ≈ 5.6% of the mean nugget diameter), while the MAE of tensile shear strength drops from 165.57 N to 72.70 N (≈ 56.1% reduction, and 72.70 N ≈ 2.4% of the average pull-test load). These results indicate both a large algorithmic gain over the baseline and an absolute error level that is meaningful for industrial deployment.

title: Probabilistic Solar Forecasting via End-to-End Sequence Modeling and Additive Decomposition
affiliations: , Cyprus University of Technology,  and Georgetown University

detail.title: Probabilistic Solar Forecasting via End-to-End Sequence Modeling and Additive Decomposition
detail.abstract: The accelerating transition to renewable energy makes accurate and spatially scalable forecasting an imperative for modern grid operations. Given the inherent variability of solar power, direct probabilistic forecasting is critical for risk-informed decision-making in competitive energy markets. However, the majority of existing approaches report point forecasts rather than a full posterior probability distribution function. We refer to these single-value output models as deterministic, as they preclude the direct use of uncertainty necessary for risk assessment. Moreover, the few currently available probabilistic approaches rely on costly, localized data from in-situ devices, limiting their utility and scalability.To address these fundamental research gaps we propose PFN-GHI (Probabilistic Forecasting Network for global horizontal irradiance) --- an end-to-end prediction model that is truly probabilistic and fully exogenous. PFN-GHI leverages publicly available geostationary satellite imagery as its primary input, enabling spatial scalability and eliminating the need for expensive ground equipment.The model employs a specialized Sequence-to-Sequence architecture coupled with a Mixture Density Network (MDN) to output a continuous posterior probability distribution function of future GHI. Crucially, we incorporate a novel probabilistically-tractable additive structure that decomposes the forecast into a time-dependent seasonality component and a cloud-driven residual component. This design is engineered to maintain analytical tractability within the MDN framework, enhancing model stability and accuracy. PFN-GHI consistently outperforms both the commonly used persistence and deterministic benchmarks, achieving a 13% improvement in probabilistic forecasting as measured by the Continuous Ranked Probability Score. Our results demonstrate that PFN-GHI credibly captures both seasonality and cloud dynamics, enabling reliable, risk-informed operation essential for managing a high-penetration solar grid.

title: Cybersecurity Threats, Challenges, and Strategies in Humanitarian Operations: A Scoping Review
affiliations: , Leiden University, Leiden University and Leiden University

detail.title: Cybersecurity Threats, Challenges, and Strategies in Humanitarian Operations: A Scoping Review

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was supported by the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture, and Science through the Starter Grants Program (grant number FGGA/2023-0044). It forms part of the project “Securing Humanitarian Operations: Preparedness and Response to Cyber Crises in Aid Delivery.”

detail.abstract: Humanitarian organizations increasingly rely on digital tools and data with the promise of faster and more efficient aid delivery. But digitalization comes with a critical drawback: a heightened exposure to cyber threats. The data breach experienced by the International Committee of the Red Cross in 2022 is a clear example of this risk, but not an isolated one. The incidents recorded during the conflicts in Ukraine and Gaza show that cyberattacks against humanitarian organizations have become an alarming reality of modern conflict. A cyber incident on a humanitarian organization harms the protection of the identities and positions of vulnerable groups. There is therefore an urgent need to recognize cybersecurity as a core pillar of humanitarian aid. This PRISMA-ScR review maps cyber threats, challenges, and strategies in humanitarian aid. It identifies a range of cyber threats to humanitarian organizations, including cyberattacks, surveillance, and mis/disinformation concerns. Still, it reveals notable lacks in terms of cyber preparedness and response, as well as a complete absence of knowledge on crisis communication strategies. Despite the importance of strengthening cybersecurity being recognized, the findings highlight that humanitarian organizations face unique challenges which often hinder the effective implementation of cyber strategies. Given the identified gaps in both existing research and practice, this review stresses the importance of developing solutions tailored to the distinctive features and needs of the humanitarian sector. To this end, this study provides a base for further investigation, with the key themes, gaps, and proposed research avenues guiding immediate focus for this underexplored field.

title: Optimization of Dual Resource-Constrained Hybrid Flow Shop Scheduling Based on Employee Timetabling and 3D Competency Model
affiliations: Wuhan University of Technology, Wuhan University of Technology, Wuhan University of Technology, Wuhan University of Technology, Wuhan University of Technology and Wuhan University of Technology

detail.title: Optimization of Dual Resource-Constrained Hybrid Flow Shop Scheduling Based on Employee Timetabling and 3D Competency Model
detail.abstract: This paper investigates a multi-stage Dual-Resource Constrained flow shop scheduling problem in medical device manufacturing, where human operators perform essential setup and auxiliary operations. Worker availability becomes a critical resource, as the number of operators is smaller than the number of machines at each stage. To address this problem, a three-dimensional Staff Competency Model is proposed to quantify heterogeneous worker performance in terms of time, quality, and cost. Furthermore, an improved Backtracking Search Optimization Algorithm is developed by incorporating a relaxation-based real-time insertion mechanism and multi-neighborhood search strategies for dynamic environments. A MILP model is also formulated to optimally solve small-sized instances. Extensive computational experiments benchmark the proposed method against seven state-of-the-art metaheuristics. The results demonstrate that iBSATS achieves superior performance in makespan and cost minimization while maintaining timetable stability, confirming the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed approach.

detail.title: Constitutionality of Mobile Court in Bangladesh
