detail.abstract: The 9 th parliament legislated the Mobile Court Act in 2009 which introduces a new dimension in the history of Bangladesh to try instantly at the place of occurrence upon the confession of the wrongdoer. Mass people of this soil welcomed the piece of legislation preliminarily. Because they witnessed speedy trial in case of eve teasing, food adulteration etc. while they accustomed to get justice after countless patient. However, the law had also enforced to oppress the innocent citizens in the name of maintaining peace and order (i.e. during hartal (strike) period) by cutting down their constitutionally guaranteed fundamental rights and fundamental principles of natural justice. In addition, the enactment does not fulfill the requirement to be an actual enactment in the eye of jurisprudence. This manuscript is aimed to examine the constitutionality of the mentioned statute from human rights perspective.

title: Stoic Leadership in the Digital Age: A Conceptual Model Integrating Virtue Ethics and Psychological Science

detail.title: Stoic Leadership in the Digital Age: A Conceptual Model Integrating Virtue Ethics and Psychological Science
detail.abstract: This paper introduces an original conceptual model that explains how a stable stoic orientation can support leaders in digital work environments. The model combines the core elements of classical Stoic virtue ethics with evidence from modern psychology, including cognitive reappraisal, acceptance and value-based behaviour. It proposes that stoic leadership orientation acts as a dispositional resource that shapes how leaders interpret and respond to digital stressors. Three psychological mechanisms-reappraisal, acceptance and value aligned goal commitment form the central pathways of influence. The model is operationalizable and suitable for empirical research. Its originality lies in the translation of Stoic philosophy into a clear, testable framework for organisational behaviour and leadership studies.

title: Christian Faith as a Stabilizing Factor in Existential Crises: An Interdisciplinary Analysis Across Psychology, Stoicism, and Religious Studies

detail.title: Christian Faith as a Stabilizing Factor in Existential Crises: An Interdisciplinary Analysis Across Psychology, Stoicism, and Religious Studies
detail.abstract: Periods of existential disruption expose the fragility of human autonomy. Contemporary individuals often interpret stability as the product of personal control. When this control collapses, psychological disintegration becomes likely. This article examines the stabilizing function of Christian faith in moments of extreme vulnerability. Drawing on psychological resilience research, existential philosophy, and early Stoic thought, the paper argues that Christian trust in God functions as an external, relational anchor, protecting individuals from the collapse of self-referential meaning systems. Unlike optimism or self-efficacy, faith provides a non-contingent horizon of significance. The article outlines a conceptual framework for understanding why Christian belief can sustain individuals when conventional coping resources fail.

title: The Theory Of Consumption Value To Inspire Purchasing Intention Of Green Product In Malaysia Hypermarket
affiliations: Universiti Teknologi MARA Sarawak, Universiti Teknologi MARA Sarawak, Universiti Teknologi MARA Sarawak, Universiti Teknologi MARA Sarawak, Universiti Teknologi MARA Sarawak and Universiti Teknologi MARA Sarawak

detail.title: The Theory Of Consumption Value To Inspire Purchasing Intention Of Green Product In Malaysia Hypermarket
detail.abstract: As sustainability gains momentum globally, this study investigates the factors influencing green purchase intention in the Malaysian context. The research focuses on understanding the unique blend of elements that impact consumers' decisions to choose green products in the Malaysian market. Key factors explored include ecological value, functional value, symbolic value, experiential value, and epistemic value. The implications of this research extend to businesses, marketers, and policymakers aiming to promote sustainable practices in Malaysia. By identifying the factors that resonate with Malaysian consumers, businesses can tailor their strategies to meet the specific needs and preferences of the local market. Additionally, this study contributes to the academic understanding of green consumer behavior in Malaysia, enriching the global discourse on sustainable consumption. In essence, this research seeks to provide actionable insights that foster environmentally responsible consumer choices in Malaysia, contributing to the broader goal of sustainable development in the region.

title: Dynamic Recovery Capacity Modeling for Multi-Sector Urban Infrastructure: Bridging Traffic Flow Perspectives and Resilience Analysis
affiliations: Arizona State University (ASU) - School of Sustainable Engineering and the Built Environment, , Johns Hopkins University, , , Arizona State University (ASU) - School of Sustainable Engineering and the Built Environment and University of Washington

detail.title: Dynamic Recovery Capacity Modeling for Multi-Sector Urban Infrastructure: Bridging Traffic Flow Perspectives and Resilience Analysis
detail.abstract: Urban systems are increasingly vulnerable to climate change, natural disasters, and global health crises, demanding more sophisticated strategies for resilience and adaptability. Traditional recovery models, such as the "V-shape" recovery curve, often oversimplify these processes, failing to capture the complex relationship between short-term recovery and long-term adaptation. This paper introduces a capacity-oriented quantification framework that combines recovery capacity, the peak recovery rate after a disruption, with stress-strain analysis to assess the point at which systems transition from elastic recovery to adaptation, known as the yield point. Through case studies involving diverse datasets, including Google COVID-19 Community Mobility Reports and post-disaster recovery data from Japan, we demonstrate the framework's ability to capture the intricate dynamics of urban recovery. Additionally, we examine adaptive capacity under extreme heat conditions in the Phoenix metropolitan area, using data from the National Land Cover Database (NLCD) and the National Solar Radiation Database (NSRDB). This framework offers a more comprehensive understanding of how urban systems respond to disruptions, providing critical insights for resilience planning and adaptation strategies. Future research should focus on refining these models by integrating more granular data and exploring the variability of recovery and adaptation across different urban systems and disruption types.

title: Energy flow diagnosis-guided meta-heuristic optimization with reinforcement learning-based parameter adaptation for multi-energy system configuration
affiliations: Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Huazhong University of Science and Technology and Huazhong University of Science and Technology

detail.title: Energy flow diagnosis-guided meta-heuristic optimization with reinforcement learning-based parameter adaptation for multi-energy system configuration
detail.abstract: Optimization of multi-energy system (MES) configuration under realistic operational constraints remains highly challenging due to strong nonlinearity, non-convexity, and highly fragmented feasible regions induced by multi-carrier coupling, reliability requirements, and diverse complex operational constraints.   Although simulation-based meta-heuristic approaches are widely adopted to capture energy management system (EMS)-driven operational behavior, their search processes remain largely fitness-driven and structure-blind, treating EMS simulations as black-box evaluators and failing to explicitly exploit system-level information embedded in energy flow trajectories and constraint activations.   As a result, existing methods often suffer from slow convergence, inefficient feasibility exploration, and frequent trapping in infeasible regions when addressing complex configuration problems. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes an energy flow diagnosis-guided meta-heuristic optimization framework for EMS-driven MES configuration. A diagnosis-based adjustment operator is designed to extract feasibility-related and operational characteristics from EMS simulations and transform them into directional guidance signals for the search process, without altering the intrinsic dynamics of the underlying algorithms. The proposed diagnosis-guided mechanism can be consistently embedded into genetic algorithm, particle swarm optimization, simulated annealing, and tabu search, demonstrating strong generality and algorithm independence. Furthermore, reinforcement learning is employed to adaptively regulate the activation probability and correction strength of the diagnosis operator based on search feedback, enabling a dynamic balance between exploration and feasibility-oriented guidance. Extensive case studies based on a highly complex EMS-driven optimization model demonstrate that the proposed energy flow diagnosis-guided framework substantially accelerates convergence and consistently yields higher-quality configuration solutions across all four algorithms. The diagnosis mechanism effectively mitigates premature stagnation under complex feasibility constraints and enables recovery from infeasible regions, while the reinforcement learning-based adaptation further enhances search efficiency and robustness, particularly for population-based algorithms such as genetic algorithm and particle swarm optimization. These results confirm the effectiveness and generality of integrating energy flow diagnosis and adaptive regulation for complex MES configuration problems.

title: Strategic Leadership and AI-Driven Approaches for Innovative Library Management
affiliations: Bandung Institute of Technology, Bandung Institute of Technology and Bandung Institute of Technology

detail.title: Strategic Leadership and AI-Driven Approaches for Innovative Library Management
detail.abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping how libraries organize knowledge and deliver digital services. Evidence shows that AI integration succeeds not primarily through technological capability but through strategic leadership that guides organizational readiness, capacity development, and an innovation culture. This study examines how strategic leadership enables AI-driven innovation in library management using a qualitative case study grounded in document analysis of the National Library of Indonesia (Perpusnas). The findings identify three leadership mechanisms essential for AI adoption: vision framing, capacity orchestration, and the cultivation of an innovation-oriented culture. AI-driven approaches such as automated metadata generation, intelligent discovery tools, and predictive analytics, become transformative only when aligned with strategic institutional direction. The study concludes that strategic leadership and AI interact as mutually shaping forces: leadership determines the conditions that allow AI to generate value, while AI technologies reshape organizational expectations and competency demands. These insights contribute to leadership-oriented digital transformation scholarship and provide actionable guidance for library institutions formulating sustainable AI strategies.

title: The Influence of Emotional, Social Media, and Community Engagement on the Sport-entertainment Experience in a Developing Country
affiliations: Politeknik Negeri Jakarta, Politeknik Negeri Jakarta, Politeknik Negeri Jakarta and Politeknik Negeri Jakarta

detail.title: The Influence of Emotional, Social Media, and Community Engagement on the Sport-entertainment Experience in a Developing Country
detail.abstract: The evolution of sport into sportainment increasingly relies on emotional, social media, and community engagement to build fan loyalty. Yet, emerging evidence from developing countries suggests these drivers are often pursued in isolation, with their synergistic impact remaining empirically unverified. This exploratory study employed a quantitative survey design (N=50) in the Indonesian context to test an integrated model examining how three drivers (emotional, social, and community) collectively influence the sportainment experience, with fan engagement as the proposed mediator. The analysis, using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM), reveals that emotional engagement (the strongest predictor), social media engagement, and community engagement all have a significant positive influence on fan engagement. Crucially, the analysis confirms that fan engagement functions as a significant and positive mediator, channelling the effects of all three drivers onto the final sportainment experience. These findings challenge fragmented approaches, demonstrating that fan identity (engagement) is the central mechanism through which sportainment value is co-created. The study contributes a validated, integrated framework (grounded in Social Identity Theory) that addresses a significant geographical and conceptual gap in the literature, enabling practitioners in emerging markets to move beyond isolated tactics and strategically build fan identity as the core driver of the sportainment experience.

title: Don't Touch My Pocket: The Dysfunction of National Economic Regulation, Companies Queuing for Stock Market Rescue --A Comparison of Institutions in Two Countries: Heaven and Hell
affiliations: Independent Scholar

detail.title: Don't Touch My Pocket: The Dysfunction of National Economic Regulation, Companies Queuing for Stock Market Rescue --A Comparison of Institutions in Two Countries: Heaven and Hell
detail.abstract: In 2025, China's economic regulation has shown clear signs of dysfunction: household deposits are locked in by low interest rates, with funds forcibly "relocated" to fill fiscal gaps; hundreds of companies are queuing for "rescue" via the stock market, yet trapped in dual bottlenecks of A-share review backlogs and Hong Kong listing delays due to sloppy materials, crying out "if we don't list, we'll go bankrupt." Rigid lockdown policies during the pandemic-lacking planning or subsidiesexacerbated the crisis, compounded by order transfers in foreign trade and foreign enterprise withdrawals. This paper contrasts the pandemic institutions of China and France, revealing how one country's rigid regulation resembles "hell" (tearing down the east wall to repair the west, reaching into people's pockets), while the other's flexible system approaches "heaven" (rent exemptions, wages split between company and state, no layoffs). Building on the author's previous work Danger! Danger! Danger! China's Largest-Scale Population Obedience Test and its models of deposit relocation and obedience spirals, this paper argues that national regulatory functions have degenerated from empowerment to extraction, calling for flexible reforms to halt the selfdestructive cycle.

title: Stoic Leadership Orientation Scale: Development and Validation

detail.title: Stoic Leadership Orientation Scale: Development and Validation
detail.abstract: This paper introduces the Stoic Leadership Orientation Scale. The scale operationalises the core Stoic virtues as leadership dispositions and links them with established psychological mechanisms such as cognitive reappraisal, acceptance and value aligned behaviour. A hypothetical exploratory factor analysis illustrates how the initial item pool would be evaluated. A hypothetical confirmatory factor analysis outlines the expected structure of a four factor model. The final scale consists of sixteen items that reflect wisdom, fairness, courage and disciplined emotional regulation. The framework is suitable for empirical validation and provides a foundation for future research on leadership, decision quality and digital work conditions.

title: Oversizing Caremark: An Empirical Analysis
affiliations: Ono Academic College Faculty of Law

detail.title: Oversizing Caremark: An Empirical Analysis
detail.abstract:
This Article argues, through the first empirical research on the taxonomy of oversight litigation, that the celebrated Caremark revolution requiring directors to adopt information and monitoring systems is more rhetoric than reality. While a seemingly heightened compliance requirement has reshaped boardroom practices, Delaware courts rarely convert this perception into liability. What emerges is a disconnect between Caremark’s symbolic prominence and its doctrinal modesty, a phenomenon this Article refers to as the oversizing of Caremark. 

This Article seeks to correct the prevailing assumptions regarding the gravitas of Caremark and explain how a compliance narrative developed beyond the bounds of judicial reality. It addresses this disjunction through an empirical analysis of all Delaware Caremark cases decided since the doctrine’s inception to provide instructive insights into the nature of successful oversight claims and thus the parameters of directors’ oversight duties.

To achieve this aim, this Article employs a hand-collected dataset of Delaware oversight decisions, drawing from judicial opinions, and when available, underlying pleadings and hearing transcripts. The dataset captures key elements such as claim type, litigation triggering events, case outcomes, and judicial rhetoric. By examining the interplay between these components, this Article uncovers patterns that offer a more accurate picture of how Caremark jurisprudence operates in practice.

The result of this Article’s empirical findings is that the dominate narrative around Caremark is false. While Information Systems claims are celebrated as Caremark’s most important contribution, they are pled in fewer than half of cases and rarely succeed on their own. These claims, which arise when directors utterly fail to establish proper reporting systems and compliance mechanisms, appear to have limited prominence and success thereby undermining the notion that Caremark chiefly polices ex-ante compliance architecture. Instead, the data reveals that Delaware courts are concerned with scrutinizing bad actors, not bad systems. This becomes evident in the fact that Red Flags claims overwhelmingly dominate the litigation profile appearing in 89% of cases. These claims, which pre-date Caremark, target directors who ignored clear signs of wrongdoing that should have triggered intervention. Similarly, claims that the board adopted an illegal business strategy had the highest success rate, making them the most effective oversight pathway.

By examining successful Caremark claims over the course of the doctrine’s history, the data reveals that liability is largely limited to three scenarios. This Article identifies those as (1) cases when directors implement sham monitoring systems; (2) failures by directors to oversee misconduct by their own fiduciaries; and (3) the adoption of illegal business practices as a matter of corporate strategy. The rarity and specificity of these scenarios reaffirms that Caremark remains a limited and exceptional doctrine. 

Tracing the courts’ application of Caremark reveals that its true influence lies in its power of norm creation. Delaware courts maintain exacting thresholds for oversight liability, but nonetheless offer substantial judicial commentary on the subject which, along with market responses, drive corporate governance behavior in the boardroom. By reframing the Caremark discussion, this Article lays the groundwork for a more realistic understanding of the doctrine’s influence.

title: Shaping Entrepreneurial Intention: Entrepreneurial Passion, Self-Efficacy, and Social Support
affiliations: University of Surabaya (UBAYA), University of Surabaya (UBAYA) and University of Surabaya (UBAYA)

detail.title: Shaping Entrepreneurial Intention: Entrepreneurial Passion, Self-Efficacy, and Social Support
detail.abstract: Unemployment arises from the mismatch between labour supply and job opportunities, highlighting the need for entrepreneurship. This study examines the effects of entrepreneurial passion, self-efficacy, and social support on entrepreneurial intention among 110 students at the University of Surabaya, using Structural Equation Modelling–Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) with IBM SPSS 26 and Smart PLS 4. Results demonstrate that passion, self-efficacy, and social support significantly enhance entrepreneurial intention, though social support does not moderate the self-efficacy–intention relationship. These findings underscore the importance of fostering psychological and social factors to strengthen students’ entrepreneurial orientation.

title: Green Word-of-Mouth and Green Purchase Intention among Gen Z in Bandung, Indonesia: Environmental Concern and Perceived Consumer Effectiveness as Mediators
affiliations: Sekolah Tinggi Teknologi Bandung - Universitas Teknologi Bandung, Sekolah Tinggi Teknologi Bandung - Universitas Teknologi Bandung, Sekolah Tinggi Teknologi Bandung - Universitas Teknologi Bandung and Sekolah Tinggi Teknologi Bandung - Universitas Teknologi Bandung

detail.title: Green Word-of-Mouth and Green Purchase Intention among Gen Z in Bandung, Indonesia: Environmental Concern and Perceived Consumer Effectiveness as Mediators
detail.abstract: Sustainable consumption has increasingly become a global concern, especially among Generation Z (Gen Z), who are often portrayed as environmentally aware but whose actions do not always reflect their values. This study explores how Green Word of Mouth (GWOM) influences Green Purchase Intention (GPI) among Gen Z consumers in Bandung, Indonesia, while examining the mediating roles of Environmental Concern (EC) and Perceived Consumer Effectiveness (PCE). Using a structured survey analyzed through a behavioral modeling approach, the study shows that positive peer conversations about green products encourage young consumers to become more concerned about environmental issues and to feel more confident that their individual actions can make a difference. These attitudinal shifts then strengthen their intention to engage in sustainable purchasing. The findings highlight that peer communication in the form of green WOM is most effective when it fosters genuine environmental concern and empowers consumers with a sense of personal efficacy. The study contributes to the green marketing literature by clarifying the mechanisms by which WOM translates into behavioral intention and addressing inconsistencies in prior research. From a practical perspective, the research suggests that marketers and sustainability advocates should focus not only on spreading positive WOM but also on shaping narratives that cultivate awareness and reinforce the belief that every consumer choice contributes to environmental solutions. This integrated view underscores the importance of combining social influence and psychological empowerment to transform "green talk" into "green action."

title: Hybrid Intelligence Teams: A Theoretical Framework for Human-AI Collaboration in Knowledge Work

detail.title: Hybrid Intelligence Teams: A Theoretical Framework for Human-AI Collaboration in Knowledge Work
detail.abstract: This paper develops a theory of Hybrid Intelligence Teams (HITs)-persistent groups composed of multiple humans and multiple AI agents working interdependently to accomplish knowledge-intensive tasks. We argue that traditional models of human teams, humanautomation systems, and multi-agent AI are insufficient for explaining the emergent dynamics of these hybrid systems. Building on organizational behavior, human-AI interaction, distributed cognition, and hybrid intelligence research, we extend the IMOI (Inputs-Mediators-Outputs-Inputs) model to include hybrid constructs: cross-species shared mental models, bilateral transactive memory systems, epistemic safety, and coherence anchoring. We further identify hybrid-specific failure modes-such as authority confusion, information cascades, AI consensus illusions, and cross-agent drift-that do not appear in purely human or purely artificial teams.

title: Policy and Business Models for National Electric Boat Transportation System, Case Study: Thousand Islands, Indonesia
affiliations: ,  and

detail.title: Policy and Business Models for National Electric Boat Transportation System, Case Study: Thousand Islands, Indonesia
detail.abstract: Aligned with Indonesia's ASTACITA agenda on electrification and renewable energy, and with the Koperasi Desa Merah Putih solar initiative, electric boats powered by batteries and solar energy offer a low-emission, cost-efficient alternative for short-distance coastal transport. This study examines suitable policy and business models for national deployment of electric boats, with the Thousand Islands (Kepulauan Seribu) proposed as a prototype site. The archipelago of over 100 small islands north of Jakarta, designated in the Jakarta Spatial Plan (RTRW) as a strategic environmental region, functions as both a marine conservation and tourism area with potential for sustainable marine resource development. Despite its strategic position, the region faces persistent challenges in inter-island connectivity and the delivery of essential goods, largely due to its reliance on fossil-fuel-based marine transport, which is both costly and environmentally unsustainable. Initial survey findings reveal that although transportation routes operated by the Department of Transportation already exist, they primarily connect the islands to Jakarta and do not adequately facilitate inter-island movement. As a result, residents who need to travel between islands often face long detours and difficult transit connections, relying instead on informal small-boat services that operate without fixed schedules or safety assurance. This study assesses three dimensions: (1) infrastructure and physical suitability, (2) social acceptance and regulatory readiness, and (3) economic viability. The initial findings indicate that calm waters and short travel distances support technical feasibility, although charging infrastructure requires development. On the social side, communities are interested in more affordable and sustainable options, while safety and range remain concerns. On the economic aspect, the system demonstrates strong viability under a Public–Private Partnership (PPP) model, with a total investment of approximately Rp 512.8 billion. Operational costs are projected to be 40–60% lower than conventional diesel vessels, largely due to reduced fuel and maintenance expenditures. Financial modeling yields an Internal Rate of Return (IRR) of 12.37%, and an average Return on Investment (ROI) of 17.52%, with a payback period of around 9 years. Moreover, electric boats also offer higher long-term profit margins, especially when combined with logistics and eco-tourism services. Energy efficiency gains reach up to 70%, significantly reducing lifecycle emissions and operating risks related to fuel price volatility. At the same time, revenue diversification through logistics, tourism, and carbon credits enhances long-term viability. This study recommends a phased implementation strategy beginning with high-demand routes, investment in solar charging infrastructure, and the development of a supportive regulatory and financial framework.

title: Analysis of Risk Management Practices and Organizational Performance in the Philippine Private Higher Education
affiliations: Saint Vincent's College Incorporated, Saint Vincent's College Incorporated, Saint Vincent's College Incorporated and Saint Vincent's College Incorporated

detail.title: Analysis of Risk Management Practices and Organizational Performance in the Philippine Private Higher Education
detail.abstract: This study examines the risk management practices and organizational performance of a private higher education institution in the Philippines. Risk management practices are assessed across five critical areas: strategic, financial, operational, compliance, and reputational risks. Organizational performance, on the other hand, is evaluated based on three dimensions: governance, management, and enabling features. Using a descriptive survey approach, data were collected from key stakeholders at the institution to assess existing risk management practices and institutional performance. The findings reveal a need for strengthened compliance and a more proactive approach to risk identification and mitigation. The study suggests that strategic improvements in the risk management framework can significantly enhance the institution's operational resilience, governance, and overall reputation.

title: A Constrained-Optimization Ensemble of Deep Learning Models for Sector-Specific Electric Load Forecasting
affiliations: Iran University of Science and Technology, Iran University of Science and Technology, Iran University of Science and Technology and Iran University of Science and Technology

detail.title: A Constrained-Optimization Ensemble of Deep Learning Models for Sector-Specific Electric Load Forecasting
detail.abstract: Precise electric load prediction is paramount for resource allocation optimization and power grid stability. While deep learning models show promise, their comparative performance across diverse energy consumption sectors remains underexplored. This paper introduces a systematic, sector-aware framework for short-term load forecasting, rigorously evaluating five state-of-the-art architectures—LSTM, BLSTM, Seq2Seq, CNN-LSTM, and Deep LSTM—across agriculture, industrial, commercial, and residential sectors. Optimal hyperparameters were determined via an exhaustive grid search and validated using a walk-forward approach to ensure temporal integrity. A key novelty of this work is the formulation of a sophisticated weighted ensemble model, optimized through constrained least squares minimization, to synergistically leverage the strengths of individual models while mitigating their weaknesses. Performance evaluation using RMSE, MAE, R2, and MAPE metrics demonstrates that the proposed ensemble model achieves a remarkable improvement in predictive accuracy, yielding the lowest RMSE of 3.43E+08 and the highest R2 of 0.9459 on the aggregate dataset. This research provides a scalable and robust forecasting system, offering significant utility for long-term infrastructure planning and strategic energy management.

title: Residents’ Perspective on Sustainable Branding of Bali Tourism
affiliations: Udayana University, Udayana University and Politeknik Negeri Bali

detail.title: Residents’ Perspective on Sustainable Branding of Bali Tourism
detail.abstract: Residents are a crucial stakeholder in the destination branding process. How locals perceived their destination could represent their satisfaction and quality of life, as well as their level of support toward tourism development. It is believed it could indirectly affect the tourist destination image and future intentional behavior. Meanwhile, destination image is crucial in understanding travel behavior and in designing effective tourism marketing strategies. This study aims to investigate residents’ self-perceptions of sustainable branding for Bali Tourism. Three hundred thirty-one residents were asked about their perceptions of the natural, cultural, and social environments. This study revealed that residents' perceived image of the cultural landscape and the presence of a positive social environment. Some concerns about improving residents’ quality of life and the sustainability of the tourism industry were discussed.

title: Managing Risk in Vulnerable Zones: Strategies for Responding to Risks in Nickel Mining Company
affiliations: Bakrie University, Bakrie University and Bakrie University

detail.title: Managing Risk in Vulnerable Zones: Strategies for Responding to Risks in Nickel Mining Company
detail.abstract: PT Gag Nikel (PTGN), a subsidiary of PT Aneka Tambang Tbk (ANTAM), faces considerable pressure related to environmental sustainability, global reputation, and legal complexities due to its mining activities being located in a small and ecologically sensitive island area. Therefore, this study aims to identify the key risks faced by PTGN. We formulate mitigation strategies through a SWOT analysis, risk mapping based on the ISO 31000 framework, and ESG principles. A qualitative case study methodology was employed, incorporating document analysis. Thematic analysis was conducted to identify risk patterns and develop appropriate company responses. The study identified nine key strategic risks, namely: (1) Declining in Environmental Management Performance; (2) Ecologically and Biologically Sensitive Location; (3) Environmental Pollution and Threats to Marine Biodiversity; (4) Political Interference in Company Operations; (5) Advocacy by NGOs Against Mining on Small Islands; (6) Poor Environmental Audit Results by the Ministry of Environment and Forestry (KLHK); (7) Failure in Sedimentation Control and Land Reclamation; (8) Increasing Consumer Demands for Stricter Sustainability Standards in Nickel Mining; (9) Contradictory Legal Frameworks. In response to these risks, four key strategies were formulated using the Risk Response Matrix, which include: (1) ESG Differentiation and Digital Transparency Strategy, (2) Reputation and Legal Strategy, (3) Social Relations Strengthening Strategy, and (4) Crisis and Political Ethics Management Strategy. This study concludes that the sustainability of PTGN’s operations highly depends on the integration of ESG principles, the strengthening of multi-stakeholder governance, and the company's ability to build adaptive and transparent communication in response to external dynamics.

title: Creative Content Communication Strategy Analysis of The Cabinet Secretariat of Republic of Indonesia in Public Opinion Creation Case: The One Decade of Joko Widodo’s Administration
affiliations: Bakrie University, Bakrie University, Bakrie University and Bakrie University

detail.title: Creative Content Communication Strategy Analysis of The Cabinet Secretariat of Republic of Indonesia in Public Opinion Creation Case: The One Decade of Joko Widodo’s Administration
detail.abstract: In today’s digital era, the government faces growing challenges in delivering accurate and relevant information to the public. The Cabinet Secretariat of the Republic of Indonesia (Setkab RI), as an institution under the President, plays a strategic role in managing public communication through social media. This study analyzes Setkab RI’s strategy in using creative content to shape public opinion about government policies, particularly in promoting the achievements of President Joko Widodo’s ten-year administration. Using the RACE model (Research, Action, Communication, Evaluation) and the Cyber Public Relations approach, this qualitative case study collected data through interviews, observation, and document analysis. The results show that Setkab RI applies visual storytelling and public testimonials to enhance engagement and trust. However, limited human resources, production tools, and bureaucratic constraints still affect communication effectiveness. The study recommends improving human resource competence and simplifying bureaucracy to support more effective digital communication.

title: Reframing Workforce Readiness: Bridging Soft Skills Gaps for Business and Sustainability in Indonesia
affiliations: Bandung Institute of Technology - School of Business and Management, Bandung Institute of Technology - School of Business and Management and Bandung Institute of Technology - School of Business and Management

detail.title: Reframing Workforce Readiness: Bridging Soft Skills Gaps for Business and Sustainability in Indonesia
detail.abstract: Indonesia faces persistent youth unemployment, particularly among vocational high school (SMK) graduates, whose technical skills often fail to translate into meaningful employment due to gaps in soft skills. This study explores the soft skills gap through a qualitative, stakeholder-informed case study, applying Expectation–Performance Gap Theory, Constructive Alignment, and Stakeholder Theory. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with employers, educators, policymakers, and graduates to capture holistic insights. Findings highlight systemic misalignments, under-prioritization of behavioral competencies, and fragmented curriculum implementation. The study contributes to the Business and Sustainability discourse by demonstrating that workforce readiness and employability are critical to building resilient, inclusive, and sustainable economies. Practical implications include stakeholder-driven curriculum co-design, structured soft skills assessments, and workplace mentorship, all aligned with SDG 4 (Quality Education) and SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth).

title: Personalization of Virtual Anchors on tvOne.AI in Journalism Practices for Gen Z as Digital Natives
affiliations: Bakrie University, Bakrie University and Bakrie University

detail.title: Personalization of Virtual Anchors on tvOne.AI in Journalism Practices for Gen Z as Digital Natives
detail.abstract: The rapid integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into journalism has significantly transformed the landscape of news production and consumption. This study explores the emergence of AI technologies in the media industry, particularly focusing on the use of Virtual Anchors in news broadcasts, with an emphasis on their relevance to Generation Z as the dominant digital native audience. The study investigates the growing phenomenon where AI is utilized not only as a supporting tool for content creation, automation, and data analysis but also as a primary interface between media organizations and their audiences through the embodiment of AI-generated news presenters. Virtual Anchors are not a novel concept globally, with countries such as China and India pioneering their use; however, their implementation in Indonesia marks a notable shift in how traditional news institutions adapt to the digital era. The national television channel TVOne has started incorporating Virtual Anchors into its news segments, both on television and consistently via its YouTube platform, signaling an important movement towards AI news presentation models in Indonesia. The background of this research stems from the increasing digital dependency of Gen Z, whose media consumption behavior significantly diverges from previous generations. Based on recent data, Gen Z demonstrates the highest rate of internet penetration at 34.40%, far surpassing Millennials and other older cohorts, and they exhibit a strong inclination toward visual formats such as videos, images, and infographics for news consumption. The study aims to understand how Virtual Anchors align with these changing audience preferences and what implications they hold for journalistic practices and media credibility using Uses and Gratification and Media Ecology Theory. Then the methodology of this study employs a qualitative approach that incorporates a literature review, case study analysis, and observation of digital news content. The primary case examined is the implementation of Virtual Anchors at TVOne, analyzing their deployment through visual and narrative styles, frequency, viewer engagement, and integration across platforms. Additionally, secondary data are used to analyze audience behavior, particularly among Gen Z consumers, drawing from internet usage reports, media surveys, and academic sources on digital media trends. Key findings suggest that the use of AI and Virtual Anchors has successfully created a novel visual experience for Gen Z, enhancing engagement and aligning with their preference for short-form, visually enriched news content. The immersive and customizable features of AI-generated news presenters make them more adaptable to digital platforms where personalization and interactivity are central to user experience. Gen Z audiences are more likely to perceive these formats as credible and relevant, not solely based on factual content but on presentation aesthetics and technological sophistication. Moreover, the visual simulation of human-like news anchors through AI contributes to a form of hyperreality that blurs the line between authenticity and performance, a media condition that Gen Z is particularly accustomed to. The analysis further reveals that Virtual Anchors are not merely technological substitutes for human labor but also strategic instruments for media organizations to maintain relevance in a saturated digital ecosystem. However, the findings also point to challenges regarding the ethical implications of AI in journalism, such as potential misinformation, lack of accountability, and reduced human oversight in editorial processes. While Virtual Anchors offer efficiency and cost-effectiveness, their growing presence necessitates a reevaluation of journalistic standards, including transparency in content sourcing, editorial responsibility, and the need for human editorial judgment. The study concludes that the deployment of AI, particularly Virtual Anchors, is reshaping how news is packaged and perceived in the era of digital natives. For media institutions, especially in emerging markets like Indonesia, this presents both an opportunity and a responsibility: to innovate in ways that meet the evolving expectations of Gen Z while upholding the core principles of journalism. This study concludes that the integration of Artificial Intelligence through the use of Virtual Anchors on tvOne.AI signifies a major transformation in journalism, particularly in responding to the media consumption patterns of Generation Z as digital natives. The presence of Virtual Anchors enhances engagement by offering visual personalization, interactivity, and technological sophistication that suit Gen Z’s preference for concise and visually driven content. This innovation also reflects a strategic move by media organizations to remain relevant and competitive in the digital era. However, this development also introduces ethical and professional challenges related to transparency, authenticity, and editorial responsibility.

title: Toward Sustainable Tourism Villages: A Literature Review on Stakeholder Collaboration, Value Chains, and Systems Approaches
affiliations: Institute of Technology Bandung, Institute of Technology Bandung and Institute of Technology Bandung

detail.title: Toward Sustainable Tourism Villages: A Literature Review on Stakeholder Collaboration, Value Chains, and Systems Approaches
detail.abstract: This study presents a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) examining how stakeholder collaboration, value chain integration, and systems approaches collectively enhance the sustainability of tourism villages. Using the PRISMA guidelines, journal articles published between 2014 and 2024 were screened across Scopus, ScienceDirect, Emerald Insight, and Google Scholar, yielding 75 relevant studies. Findings reveal four main patterns: (1) stakeholder collaboration remains conceptual, with limited operational frameworks, (2) value chain studies focus mainly on competitiveness, lacking sustainability integration, (3) systems thinking, particularly Soft Systems Methodology (SSM), is underutilized in tourism contexts, and (4) tourism village research often neglects informal community actors despite their central role in value creation. This study proposes several implications for future research, including advocating for the operationalization of collaborative mechanisms; an exploration of power dynamics; the inclusion of informal stakeholders; a comprehensive integration of value chains that transcends mere products; the incorporation of both formal and informal connections; the empirical application of SSM; and the utilization of participatory modeling to foster inclusive and adaptive governance.

title: The Impact of ESG Performance and Controversies on Firm Value: Evidence from the Energy Sector in Indonesia
affiliations: Bakrie University, Bakrie University, Bakrie University and Bakrie University

detail.title: The Impact of ESG Performance and Controversies on Firm Value: Evidence from the Energy Sector in Indonesia
detail.abstract: Firm value is no longer determined solely by financial performance, but is also influenced by investors' perception of the company's social and environmental responsibility. Regarding sustainability concerns, Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) issues have become a focus for investors in Socially Responsible Investing (SRI). Good ESG implementation doesn't always drive sectoral index increases, but it remains a value-added consideration for investors, especially in the energy sector. With the growing attention to SRI, the Current firm value not only reflects profitability but also contribution to sustainability, making this topic relevant for research, particularly in the context of the developing Indonesian capital market. This study examines the influence of ESG performance on firm value, with ESG controversies as a moderating variable. The population in this study consists of 44 energy sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange. The sampling technique used is purposive sampling. The analysis method used is multiple linear regression analysis using SPSS. The results of this study indicate that ESG performance has a positive effect on firm value, and ESG controversies can influence the relationship between ESG performance and firm value.

title: Fraud Hexagon Analysis in Detecting Potential Fraud in Financial Reports

detail.title: Fraud Hexagon Analysis in Detecting Potential Fraud in Financial Reports

keywords: changes in the board of directors

detail.abstract: This study aims to analyze the tendency of financial statement fraud using the fraud hexagon framework, which consists of stimulus, opportunity, rationalization, capability, arrogance, and collusion. These six elements are measured by the following proxies: financial targets, frequency of audit committee meetings, auditor changes, changes in the board of directors, number of CEO photographs, and political connections. The population of this study includes infrastructure companies listed on the Main Board and Development Board of the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) as of December 31, 2024. The research sample was selected using a purposive sampling method, resulting in a total of 87 observations over a three-year observation period from 2022 to 2024. The data used were obtained from audited financial statements and annual reports published on the IDX. Data analysis was conducted using logistic regression models. The findings of this study suggest that political connections exert a positive and significant influence on the likelihood of financial statement fraud. In contrast, financial targets, the frequency of audit committee meetings, auditor changes, changes in the board of directors, and the number of CEO photographs do not affect the likelihood of financial statement fraud.

title: Beyond Entertainment: YouTube's Impact as a Social Media Engagement Tool for Gen Z's Self-Acceptance, Case study: Menjadi Manusia – YouTube Channel
affiliations: Bakrie University, Bakrie University, Bakrie University and Bakrie University

detail.title: Beyond Entertainment: YouTube's Impact as a Social Media Engagement Tool for Gen Z's Self-Acceptance, Case study: Menjadi Manusia – YouTube Channel
detail.abstract: Generation Z, as digital natives, heavily relies on platforms like YouTube for entertainment as well as a significant source of space for identity formation. In this highly interconnected digital environment, constant social comparison and exposure to idealized images often pose unique challenges to their self-acceptance, contributing to widespread issues such as stress and anxiety. This study aims to analyze how the slice-of-life approach, as employed by the YouTube channel "Menjadi Manusia," functions as a social media engagement tool to enhance self-acceptance among Generation Z and improve their mental well-being. This study employed a qualitative approach with a case study design, specifically focusing on the YouTube channel "Menjadi Manusia." The primary data were collected from five Gen Z informants who are subscribers of the channel. The findings indicate a significant increase in self-acceptance among the subscribers of "Menjadi Manusia," Participants demonstrated an improved ability to assess their strengths and interpret expectations realistically. This research concludes that YouTube, by leveraging an authentic social media engagement approach, effectively empowers Generation Z to cultivate deeper self-acceptance, which is crucial for fostering their overall mental well-being in the digital age.

title: Implementation of Six Sigma and PDCA to Improve Delivery Process Quality at Distribution Center Fresh PT XYZ
affiliations: Harapan Bangsa Institute of Technology, Harapan Bangsa Institute of Technology and Harapan Bangsa Business School

detail.title: Implementation of Six Sigma and PDCA to Improve Delivery Process Quality at Distribution Center Fresh PT XYZ
detail.abstract: Efficient distribution management is critical for maintaining smooth operations at a distribution center (DC), yet PT FRESH PT XYZ experienced a severe delay rate of 40% over the past two months. This study applies the DMAIC (Define, Measure, Analyze, Improve, Control) framework augmented with Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) to identify and verify root causes via Risk Priority Number (RPN), and employs the Plan–Do–Check–Act (PDCA) cycle during the Improve phase to design and monitor corrective actions. FMEA in the Analyze phase revealed five high RPN failure modes (RPN > 343) affecting delivery timeliness and two high RPN modes affecting delivery accuracy. Improvement measures, including work-method optimization, operator training, and environmental adjustments, were implemented and tracked through PDCA. After these interventions, all performance indicators improved significantly: overall DPMO fell from 158,019 to 86,856, and Sigma rose from 2.50 to 3.0; the delivery timeliness DPMO decreased from 304,182 to 119,981 with Sigma improving from 2.01 to 2.68; and the delivery accuracy DPMO declined from 10,828 to 4,336 while Sigma increased from 3.80 to 4.15. Although the average post-improvement metrics have yet to fully meet the final targets (overall DPMO ≤ 66,000 and overall Sigma ≥ 3.25), weekly trends exhibit consistent progress, particularly in weeks four and five when all targets were achieved.

title: A Comparative Analysis of Operational Efficiency and ESG Implementation in Leading Public Construction Companies in Malaysia and Indonesia
affiliations: Bakrie University, Bakrie University, Bakrie University and Bakrie University

detail.title: A Comparative Analysis of Operational Efficiency and ESG Implementation in Leading Public Construction Companies in Malaysia and Indonesia
detail.abstract: The global construction industry faces dual pressures to enhance operational efficiency and adopt Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) practices. For emerging economies like Indonesia, benchmarking against regional leaders is crucial for global competitiveness. This study provides a comparative analysis of operational efficiency (cost, asset, profitability, liquidity) and ESG implementation (Environmental, Social, Governance) among leading public construction firms in Malaysia and Indonesia. A quantitative comparative approach was used, analysing secondary data from five leading companies in each country from 2015 to 2024. The results indicate that Malaysian firms are significantly superior in Profitability and Governance, while Indonesian firms exhibit marginally higher Asset Efficiency. A key finding is the "efficiency without profitability" paradox in Indonesia, linked to weaker governance and a higher-risk corruption environment. Furthermore, the study confirms a significant positive relationship between Environmental practices and Cost Efficiency across both nations. This research concludes that robust governance is the primary driver of profitability, serving as a critical differentiator for sustainable competitiveness in the construction sector.

title: Optimization of Drilling Operations: A Comparative Cost and Efficiency Analysis of Three Rig Scenarios
affiliations: Bakrie University and Bakrie University

detail.title: Optimization of Drilling Operations: A Comparative Cost and Efficiency Analysis of Three Rig Scenarios
detail.abstract: This study evaluates the cost and operational efficiency of three drilling scenarios—conventional rigs, skidding rigs, and clustering pads—in eastern Indonesia’s remote terrain. Key metrics include mobilization days, drilling days, and production cost per well. A Monte Carlo simulation, based on three months of field observations, supports a decision support system for selecting the optimal approach. Results show that the skidding rig is the most efficient, requiring only 12 mobilization days, 331 drilling days, and a production cost of USD 3.8 million per well. By contrast, conventional rigs require 309 mobilization days and 610 drilling days, while clustering pads have the highest cost at USD 5.1 million per well. The skidding rig’s key advantage is its ability to move between wells without dismantling, significantly reducing time and costs. However, successful implementation depends on resolving logistical, contractual, and regulatory challenges. While infrastructure and environmental constraints exist, the skidding rig presents a promising solution if these barriers are addressed. The study concludes that skidding rigs offer a cost-effective and operationally superior strategy for the region. Future research will refine cost estimates and enhance decision-making tools for drilling scenario selection.

title: Sustainable Entrepreneurship Development Strategy for Achieving SDGs: A Conceptual Framework for SMEs
affiliations: Institut Teknologi Bandung (ITB) and Institut Teknologi Bandung (ITB)

detail.title: Sustainable Entrepreneurship Development Strategy for Achieving SDGs: A Conceptual Framework for SMEs
detail.abstract: This research presents a conceptual framework, the Sustainable Entrepreneurship Development Strategy (SEDS), which encompasses six strategies for developing sustainable entrepreneurship in SMEs. The strategies include dynamic capabilities, innovative capabilities, stakeholder-focused approach, environmentally responsible practices, strong local ties, and excellent human resources. By implementing these strategies, SMEs can not only achieve long-term success but also contribute to addressing environmental and social challenges and fostering a more sustainable and inclusive economy. Although this study has limitations in terms of database selection and a lack of empirical evidence, it provides a foundation for future research to explore broader areas and validate the SEDS framework in real-world business settings, particularly in developing countries.
